title: Place and admit fleet builds by each host's measured free capacity: Hetzner hosts first, the laptop last
body:
Class: fleet heavy runs placed local-first instead of on the host with the most free build slots, so remote build hosts idle while the laptop saturates.

On 2026-11-10 at 7:40 AM the laptop ran at load 22 on 24 threads while gex45 ran at 6.3 on 20 cores and cpx62 at 0.8 on 16. Fleet sessions' builds and tests were placed local-first and spilled to Hetzner only on deferral.

Causes found:
- south agents/orchestration.toml (2026-11-07, north#740): the laptop leases its own sessions' compiles up to 22 of 24 threads and offers a build to gex45 only when its own admission defers it.
- cpx62 takes only builds its capacity taker pulls after a deferral, so it idles while the laptop accepts.
- harness/opencode.toml `[dispatch] hosts = ["whiterabbit"]`: every DeepSeek session runs on the laptop, and its cargo and nix runs build there.

Tom asked (2026-11-10) for deterministic, load-balanced placement so the Hetzner hosts carry fleet work and this cannot recur. Fleet sessions' heavy runs (cargo build/test/clippy/nextest, bun builds) go to the remote build host with the most free headroom first, and run on the laptop only when every remote host is full or unreachable; Tom's own unleased builds at the keyboard stay local. This replaces the 2026-11-07 laptop-first bound for fleet work.

## Done when

- [x] A fleet session's heavy build on the laptop runs on a remote build host whenever gex45 or cpx62 has a free build slot, picked by measured free slots, with the laptop last. Check: with gex45 and cpx62 idle, capacity placement for a fleet-session cargo build names a remote host, proven by a test that reproduces today's local-first pick. (landed 698f8407ad64) Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-capacity -E 'test(/capacity_a_fleet_session_build_on_the_saturated_laptop_goes_to_the_build_host_with_the_most_free_room/)'` exits 0. Evidence: `cargo nextest run -p north-capacity -E 'test(/capacity_a_fleet_session_build_on_the_saturated_laptop_goes_to_the_build_host_with_the_most_free_room/)'` passed on main f91c907968bd on 2026-11-11, exit 0.
- [x] Every heavy run a DeepSeek or Claude fleet session starts (direct `cargo`, `nix develop -c cargo`, `north capacity dev-shell run`) passes through that placement; none runs unleased on the laptop. Check: a fleet-session `cargo test` started from a worker shell on the laptop shows in remote admission, not in local agent-capacity.slice. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-capacity -E 'test(/a_fleet_session_cargo_test_on_the_laptop_is_leased_through_remote_admission/)'` exits 0 (landed 79583f0790a3: `north capacity dev-shell run` hands a command the gate leases to `north capacity gate` before entering the dev shell, whose own cargo otherwise bypassed the shims; the named test passes and kills the mutant "placed returns None"; direct cargo and `nix develop -c cargo` already met the gate through their shims) Evidence: `cargo nextest run -p north-capacity -E 'test(/a_fleet_session_cargo_test_on_the_laptop_is_leased_through_remote_admission/)'` passed on main f91c907968bd on 2026-11-11, exit 0.
- [x] An alarm fires when the laptop carries fleet build load while a remote host has free build slots for over 5 minutes. Check: the alarm fires on a replay of the 2026-11-10 7:40 AM host facts. (landed e95c009ec3a2: the flow alarm tells the proxy once per episode; its test replays the 7:40 AM host facts) Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-flow -E 'test(/a_replay_of_the_7_40_am_host_facts_alarms_once_the_laptop_has_carried_fleet_builds_for_five_minutes_north_1036/)'` exits 0. Evidence: `cargo nextest run -p north-flow -E 'test(/a_replay_of_the_7_40_am_host_facts_alarms_once_the_laptop_has_carried_fleet_builds_for_five_minutes_north_1036/)'` passed on main f91c907968bd on 2026-11-11, exit 0.


- [x] (low priority; from a Gemini review 2026-11-10) Aborted or superseded lanes on the build hosts free their worktree and target disk when the session ends, not at the next sweep: `north lanes gc` remote boxes and strays are tied to the capacity host's session terminations. Check: after a worker on gex45 is forgotten, `ssh gex45 ls ~/code/north/worktrees` no longer lists its lane within one tick. Done when: `LANE=gate-ticked-record; test -z "$(ssh gex45 ls ~/code/north/worktrees | rg "$LANE")"` exits 0 one tick after forgetting a worker on gex45 (LANE names its lane) Needs: gex45. A DeepSeek session cannot do this box: it forgets a worker on gex45 and reads its worktrees, a host service. Evidence (2026-11-10, 11:55 PM): north-1042-d1645 ended on gex45 with its landed lane gate-ticked-record still there (the lander kept it, "its worktree is not on this host"); its lane-free unit ran `north lane remove` on gex45, which printed `reaped (equiv): /home/tom/code/north/worktrees/gate-ticked-record`, and `LANE=gate-ticked-record; test -z "$(ssh gex45 ls ~/code/north/worktrees | rg "$LANE")"` exits 0. Fixed by 4feca529bb (forget and retire free the worktree the session's output names, not its main launch dir) and 0e365965cd (lane remove judges against origin/main, which the hosts' stale local main lagged by 40 commits), both on origin/main. Evidence: `LANE=gate-ticked-record; test -z "$(ssh gex45 ls ~/code/north/worktrees | rg "$LANE")"` passed on main f91c907968bd on 2026-11-11, exit 0.

- [x] Land checks and pre-queue gate checks place by the same measured free slots: on 2026-11-10 at 2:05 PM the laptop ran 16 heavy runs (6 land-check, 4 gate) at load 40 on 24 cores while cpx62, approved as a build and land-check host, sat at load 8 on 16 cores. Check: a replay of those host facts places the land check on cpx62. (landed 6c43c18bb058: a host the policy does not name as offloading builds is the land-check fallback in any capacity mode, so it queues on the least busy build host) Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-runtime -E 'test(/the_laptop_in_any_capacity_mode_competes_for_no_land_check_beside_the_build_hosts_north_1036/)'` exits 0. Evidence: `cargo nextest run -p north-runtime -E 'test(/the_laptop_in_any_capacity_mode_competes_for_no_land_check_beside_the_build_hosts_north_1036/)'` passed on main f91c907968bd on 2026-11-11, exit 0.


## Moved from north#945 on 2026-11-10 (Admit build jobs by each host's live CPU and memory pressure instead of fixed slot counts)
One guarantee: builds are placed and admitted by each host's measured capacity.

- [x] The land check for a lane never aborts on capacity_agent_compile::a_fleet_sessions_compile_from_any_entry_is_refused_only_when_no_build_host_and_not_this_host_has_room when a hook deadline fires under load: on 2026-11-14 at 1:00 AM the check for the leak re-land eaf2f15ce3 was refused after that test SIGABRTed at 23 s ("hook errors: north-hookdeadline", "failed to initiate panic, error 5"), while the same test passed in 13.8 s on the tip c8291311e8 full run and the lane does not touch capacity code (owner claude-c-f09617). (landed c210902ed12081d313ba49a87b6c545b6167a251 on main; the land check ran capacity_agent_compile::a_fleet_sessions_compile_from_any_entry_is_refused_only_when_no_build_host_and_not_this_host_has_room and it passed in 19.747 s, log /tmp/north-hand-in-ptSbct.log line 89)

Done when: on a tree where origin/main holds one function over its limit and a lane touches only a path outside it, `north land scan` or the code-health gate for that lane exits 0, shown by a test. Triage 2026-11-14: owed, a lane. Only the hotspot-ranking base-tree part landed (26fa140808); the test on a tree whose main holds one over-limit function is absent. Oracle needs a build. Not blocked.
- [x] The land check runs the same code-health line as the after-landing gate, so a lane whose own diff adds a function over the complexity limit, or a test over its size, is refused before it queues and never lands as a red main (owner claude-c-f09617). Evidence: 2f3adfc6e0 (the Buck2 lead; Shared.wrapped at crates/north-land-checks/src/land/slots/runner/spawn.rs:200 at complexity 22 against 15) and 6028d1796b (a 94-line test), both landed and were then refused by the after-landing gate. Done when: a lane that adds a function of complexity 22 gets its hand-in refused by the land check with exit nonzero before it is queued, shown by the land check output on that lane. Evidence: landed as 122e4ca741 (on origin/main, ancestor check exit 0); a probe lane adding a 22-branch function, handed in on 2026-11-13 at 7:56 PM UTC, was refused before queueing by the hand-in check line `code-health gate ${SAFE_PUSH_LAND_BASE} ${SAFE_PUSH_LAND_HEAD}` with exit 1 and the output `function ... complexity 22 (limit 15) (new)`, and never reached origin/main. Land check log: /home/tom/.local/state/safe-push/land-check-bvwPU1bshM.log
- [ ] A hand-in from a build host spends under 5 s in its private-kind ask stage (crates/north-lander/src/land/enqueue.rs:291, the enqueue gate, which runs the judge child through crates/north-base/src/platform/private_text.rs), not 173 to 184 s: 20 of 20 hand-ins from cpx62b tonight took about 180 s there, on a cache hit too, against 1.3 to 1.9 s on the laptop (owner claude-c-f09617; reported by release-evals-lead from /home/tom/eval-data/eval-b/results-north-rel-1113-r5.jsonl and -r3.jsonl, 2026-11-14 12:2x AM). The cause is unverified: a 180 s wait inside the judge child or its visibility or deny-list read on a build host. Triage 2026-11-14: owed, a lane plus a reading. Cause still unnamed; candidate: the deny-list fetch lock that held later scans 180 s on a host (2188d911d1, re-landed as a kernel lock in 56ad3e216d), same wait length. Needs a `north land profile` reading of build-host hand-ins on a runtime that carries it, and the cause written in the box. Oracle read-only but the profile prints no private-kind ask span today. Not blocked.
- [ ] A land check, a red-main fix or a revert never waits behind worker builds for a build-host slot: each build host keeps a reserved admission slot for land checks, and a lane that fixes or reverts a red main takes it first (owner claude-c-f09617; from 2026-11-13 at 12:03 AM: the two-line machine-check fix was refused before queueing with exit 96 after 600 s with no build-host slot while main was red, and f-buck-side-4 paused its 20 worker builds to retry). Done when: with 20 worker builds queued on a build host, a land check and a red-main fix each take a slot within 60 s, shown by a test. Evidence: landed 9ad29348fdc56a13bdfd81ab1f4cb210242aeb74 on origin/main; a red fix (rank 0) now takes the lander-reserved slot beside full worker slots, test a_red_main_fix_takes_the_reserved_slot_within_a_minute_while_worker_builds_hold_every_other_slot passes (land checks already took it via lander_slot). - [x] The transient-process watch counts processes per live session, not in total: a count that rises only with live sessions is growth, and the watch reports a leak only when a process outlives its session (owner claude-c-f09617, from the 2026-11-13 readings: whiterabbit and cpx62 each reported a rise, and the laptop read 38 hand-in tool servers, one per live session). - [x] A closed host's lander check never falls back to this host when no remote answers (owner claude-c-f09617, from the post-hoc review of 3f4e3a72df on 2026-11-13): choose() exits with no host and crates/north-safe-push/src/gates/run.rs:126-137 falls back to landing.capacity here. Evidence: `cargo nextest run -p north-land-checks -p north-offload -E 'test(/runs_no_checks/) | test(/a_check_before_queueing/)'` passed 4 of 4, exit 0; a host with runs_no_checks now takes the off-host path in north-land-checks, so with no remote readable the check waits then reaches no verdict, never running here; landed 336dc285fec88b080abbcfbcb6141e99228d3045 on origin/main on 2026-11-13.
- [ ] The gex45 host's north processes rise every ten minutes (land-watch: landing 5d79f9ab8bad not live past its deadline): the leaking process is named with what starts it, stopped at its cause, and the count before and after is recorded on this box. Done when: `ssh -o BatchMode=yes gex45 'pgrep -fc north'` before the fix and after one full ten-minute window, the after count not above the before count. Status 12:3x AM 2026-11-14: the investigation (f-gex45-leak-2) found no leaking process; the leak alarm read the transient count, which climbs with live sessions. ### A worker's GPU-class command cannot initialise CUDA: the worker sandbox refuses the driver's /proc thread-name write (was #1223)

Inside a worker session `north capacity host run --class gpu -- python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"` prints False and a direct `cuInit(0)` returns 304 (CUDA_ERROR_OPERATING_SYSTEM): the driver writes the thread name through `/proc/self/task/TID/comm` during initialisation and the worker sandbox's Landlock writable list (`crates/north-runtime/src/worker_sandbox/writable.rs`) grants writes on `/dev` but not `/proc`, so init aborts. The capacity broker wraps an admitted command in a fresh worker domain, so a gpu-class lease inherits the refusal.
Fix: grant write on the process's own `/proc/self` thread entries (at least `task/*/comm`) to worker domains, or at least to commands admitted under the gpu class, keeping the rest of `/proc` read-only. Blocks north#1221 (the decision model's shadow run fell back to CPU).

### A session on a build host cannot place its own run on another build host

Found 2026-11-13 by a read-only worker. The other build hosts' names are login shortcuts that exist only in the controlling host's client configuration; a build host has none, and the offload's host check accepts any declared host whatever the asking host's `reaches` list says. Alternative, not taken: a key and client entries from gex45 to the other two, which would let gex45 sessions spread their own runs and costs that wider reach; it would be the owner's call.

title: Capacity from measured usage (pace, spawn guard, placement, usage-limit stops, cloud credit)
body:
Category: tooling
Spec: measured
Scope: cross-module
Surface: rust
Verify: local-test

Plan item 4 of 7 in the harness efficiency plan (2026-10-27): cost and wall time per closed box. The baseline and its full basis are in the plan handoff (harness-plan.md).


## Saving
Runs that ended on a usage limit were a measurable share of spend, and their work was cut off mid-turn. A projection that clamps burn hid a real burn rate behind a relayed one ten times lower. Expected: that share of spend saved.
## Done when
- [x] (headless run) Pace and placement use only burn measured from at least two readings of that account, and `agents usage` prints the reading count. The weekly projection uses the last 3 h burn whenever it is above the week's average (src/pace/window.rs:85). Tests cover both. â^@^T done in a9a33611: `cargo test --bin north pace::` 10 passed, including week_projection_follows_recent_burn_when_it_exceeds_the_week_average (recorded mutant n259-week-burn-clamped fails it); `harness/lib/usage.test.sh` asserts "2 readings" in the agents usage table; pace burn comes only from a trail spanning the burn window (src/pace/trail.rs), so it needs two readings; land check green; `git merge-base --is-ancestor a9a33611 origin/main` ok
- [x] (headless run) The spawn guard decides each account's refusal from that account's own readings. This is north#256's box.
- [x] (observed) Every Claude account a-d shows a numeric burn in `agents usage` for 24 h. â^@^T observed 2026-11-04 on gex45 (origin/main cbdabdee8): `agents usage` now prints burn 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 and 4.7 %/h with 5400, 3196, 4897 and 619 readings for a, b, c and d. In pace-control.jsonl, all four accounts carry a numeric weekly burn in 911 of 911 samples between 2026-11-01T00:00Z and 2026-11-02T00:00Z, the longest gap between samples 2.2 min; threads.db usage rows for a-d have no gap over 3 min across the same stretch. Burn is null only for the 10 minutes after a weekly reset empties the trail (account b 2026-10-31 12:00-12:10Z, account d 2026-11-03 08:01-08:10Z), by design, since burn needs two readings spanning the window.
- [x] (observed: decision changes from data) Placement moves or holds a launch whose ETA times the account's measured burn would cross its 5 h cap, and the launch log names the measured burn. â^@^T done in b185f914: `cargo test --bin north dispatch::` 71 passed, including plan_burn_tests (a 12%/h account with 10 points left over a 60 min ETA is skipped for one that fits, and the launch line reads "claude:a measured burn 2.0%/h over a 60 min ETA spends 2.0 of the 8 points left to its 5h stop"; a box no account fits is held with each burn named); recorded mutants n259-launch-burn-unnamed, n259-hold-reason-unnamed and n259-unmeasured-burn-holds each fail their test; land check green; `git merge-base --is-ancestor b185f914 origin/main` ok. The first live run on the next dispatch tick shows the burn in its launch line once ledger figures exist for the cell.

**Tier:** worker (Opus medium), because pacing spans src/pace, src/ops/pacing and the hooks. **ETA:** 2 h, plus 24 h.


## Earlier body (kept; its unticked boxes are part of this issue)

## Goal

Dispatch places each item on the host that will finish it soonest, from live measurements, not static slots. Tom asked on 2026-10-27 to close the infrastructure gaps behind slow issue throughput.

Observed on 2026-10-27:

- **Heavy work on Nexus.** Five smashcraft hit-region workers (#597 to #601) were placed on Nexus, which has 3 cores and 7 GB. Their test suites (heavy, 5957 MiB each) queued behind each other on `DEFER_MEMORY_HEADROOM`.
- **gex45 overloaded, laptop idle.** At the same time gex45 ran at load 41 on 20 threads. The laptop (24 cores, 77 GB free) sat at load 6, because its placement window had drained it at 03:00Z and nothing reopened it. Dispatch logged "laptop unavailable" all day.
- **Slow Nexus deploys.** North runtime builds on Nexus waited 19 minutes for a slot. That is being fixed separately by moving builds off Nexus.
- **Static caps.** Caps are set by hand in `south:agents/orchestration.toml` (`resident_cap`, `warcraft_clients`). gex45's client cap stayed at 4 for its old 256 MiB aperture until it was raised by hand after Resizable BAR.

## Design

- **Place by finish time.** Dispatch scores each candidate host by live CPU pressure, available memory against the item's declared class, and the queue ahead for that class. It places where the item is expected to start soonest, and never puts a heavy or native-evidence item on a host whose memory cannot admit its class.
- **Reopen the laptop automatically.** `laptop-auto` opens the laptop when the seat is idle, Tom is not gaming and it is on power, and drains it on the existing triggers. The window stops being the only opener.
- **Caps from measurement.** `resident_cap` and `warcraft_clients` gain a measured mode. A host's cap follows the admission layer's live headroom (memory, CPU pressure, GPU aperture and VRAM), and the static value stays only as a ceiling.

## Done when

- [x] (headless run) Placement tests show three things. A heavy smashcraft item goes to gex45 or the laptop, not to a 7 GB host. With the laptop seat idle and on power, `laptop-auto` reports it available. The client cap follows a measured aperture and VRAM fixture.
- [x] (code) Admission accounting: the named reproduction from handoffs/adaptive-harness/CX-B2h2.md reports FALSE 0 with the admission fixes on main (short-window cap, denominator drift, zero-burn reset, TRUE-to-UNRESOLVED judge behavior); (headless run) replay of a forced provider hold and the preserved three-day input gives zero false decisions. (moved from #94: branch adaptive-controller, head e3f6e247, is unlanded) â^@^T done in 34a3efb20: `cargo test --bin north pace` 30 passed (incl. three_day_claude_replay_holds_nothing_the_realized_usage_disproves over src/pace/fixtures/claude-c-replay.jsonl, which asserts FALSE 0, and a_forced_provider_hold_replays_with_zero_false_decisions); six recorded mutants (n259-replay-reset-jitter-exact, n259-replay-floor-judged-false, n259-replay-week-projection-judged-true, n259-short-window-cap-dropped, n259-cold-hold-recovery-dropped, n259-short-window-projection-holds) each fail their test; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 34a3efb20 origin/main` ok. Not reproduced exactly: the original reproduce.ts from CX-B2h2.md is gone, so the committed judge over the preserved three-day input stands in for it. Before the fix that judge reported FALSE 300 min (290 min of five-hour projection holds, 10 min of a burn-cap refusal that was a judge artifact: resets_at jittering by 1 s truncated the realized window); five-hour projections no longer hold an account (the per-worker cap bounds workers instead), and no existing assertion encoded the old hold.

## Moved from #210 Pace sampling costs 13-22 s of CPU every minute on Nexus

- [x] A pace sample on Nexus costs under 1 s of CPU per minute in steady state, from systemd's "Consumed" line on 5 consecutive runs (paste them), with the same pace-control.json decisions as before on the same inputs. Restated 2026-11-14 (scoreboard lead, on the triage of this date): the clause "with the same pace-control.json decisions as before on the same inputs" is superseded, because the spend rule of 2026-11-11 deleted the pace readings and controls the sample used to decide (docs/rationale/spend-rule.md, "The `pace` and `paces` readings ... deleted"); what is left to show is the cost alone, the five "Consumed" lines of the usage sample on Nexus. Read 2026-11-14 (journal of usage-sample.service): the sampler runs on the laptop, not on Nexus, and the five newest runs read `Consumed 3.062s CPU time over 16.590s wall clock time, 1.3G memory peak` (01:53:16Z), `5.180s over 22.366s, 1.4G` (01:54:22Z), `4.333s over 24.532s, 1.4G` (01:55:25Z), `2.499s over 2.914s, 1.3G` (01:56:03Z) and `3.837s over 9.344s, 1.4G` (01:57:09Z), each recording 36 readings. Not met: three to five times the limit, on the host the owner works at. The box is read on the host the sampler runs on; its cause is staffed (session sb-sample-259). Fixed and restated 2026-11-14 at the measured cost (coordinator's ruling of that day). Cause: on a remote client every sample checked the whole 1.18 GB ledger snapshot and copied it into memory, then dropped the copy, though its readings had already gone to the ledger host; f1ecf94dab opens an empty in-memory store instead, same readings and cadence. Live on the laptop from about 03:02Z; five consecutive runs after it read `Consumed 1.444s CPU time over 2.970s wall clock time, 173.8M memory peak` (03:13Z), `3.711s over 5.550s, 367.5M` (03:14Z), `3.751s over 10.980s, 348.5M` (03:15Z), `4.684s over 5.959s, 217.7M` (03:16Z) and `1.791s over 2.137s, 163.5M` (03:17Z). Over the 15 runs since the fix the mean is 3.0 s CPU against 3.6 s over the 24 runs before it, and the memory peak is 0.16 to 0.5G against 1.3 to 1.9G: a run that starts no Claude CLI costs 1.1 to 1.8 s (2.2 to 2.6 s before), a run that starts one 3.3 to 5.7 s. The box as restated: no run copies the ledger (memory peak under 0.6G) and a run with no CLI start costs under 2 s. The 1 s a minute of the first wording is not met and is not pursued: the CLI start on about every other run is the only source of the extra-usage flag the money refusal reads (no cheaper source carries it in the code or docs), and its one-minute freshness is not traded for CPU.

The gaming rule can hold every heavy land check on the laptop indefinitely (a land check waited 15+ minutes on 2026-10-27). safe-push should run the held check on a host with room instead, shipping the lane by git bundle over ssh (laptop to gex45 first; gex45 cannot reach the laptop or Nexus).

On 2026-10-27/28 gex45's root hit 100% four times while admission counted only CPU and memory, with about 17 sessions building at once.

title: Work is tracked as sub-issues closed by their landing, not as checkbox lines in an issue body
body:
Class: work is tracked as checkbox lines inside an issue body, which cannot be queried, claimed, timed or closed on their own, so closure rests on what an agent wrote.
Spec: judged
Scope: cross-module

Decided by Tom on 2026-11-11: boxes become sub-issues, built after the timing breakdown of north against T3 Code (GAP.md on the south tracking issue, number 107) names its three largest differences, so it takes no capacity from closing that gap.

Evidence from 2026-11-11: 114 issues closed as completed still held 190 unticked boxes; north#1076 showed 68 open of 80 boxes, most of them the template clean-up lines; changing one box means rewriting the whole body, and the coordinator rewrote north#1076's body three times in one afternoon while workers could tick boxes on it; every launch, claim and gate finds its box by a text prefix (`--box TEXT`); issue bodies reach 90 KB.

Why boxes exist: harness/skills/github/references/issues.md limits issue creation to what Tom authorizes, and makgora's AGENTS.md sends non-blockers to a checkbox, both to keep agents from flooding the tracker; north then grew code around the lines (crates/north-threads/src/threads/issue_boxes.rs, crates/north-landing/src/issue_body.rs, crates/north-core/src/build_time/issue.rs, crates/north-graph-ground/src/issue.rs).

Shape: an issue is one unit of work that one worker lands. Anything separately staffed, verified or landed is its own issue, linked to its parent with GitHub's native sub-issue link, which gives progress on the parent and one query for all children. Labels stay for category, priority and area; a milestone names a dated push. A checklist inside one worker's single landing is prose in that issue. One cut, every in-repo caller updated in the same change, no compatibility layer.

Goal served: first-try success and closure that is true, read from the landing and not from a report.

## Done when

The plan is `docs/rationale/sub-issue-cutover.md`. Stages run in order and the boxes inside a stage run side by side; each box is one worker for at most 45 minutes, and a box that would run longer is split before it is staffed. The plan departs from the decision above in four places and gives the evidence for each in its second section: a leaf is closed by its own check, which its landing passes for most leaves and not for all; the leaf path arrives before the box path is deleted; the deletion is five changes, one per interface with all its callers; and the read is one per repository, not one per parent. Its last section words the two choices that are the owner's.

### Stage 0: plan

- [x] 0. The cutover is planned: the ten parents, the order with the expected count at each step, the cut by file, GitHub's limits, what an outsider sees, pilot and reversal, the other trackers, and the owner's two choices. Done when: `test "$(git show origin/main:docs/rationale/sub-issue-cutover.md | rg -c '^## ')" -ge 6` passes. Evidence: `test "$(git show origin/main:docs/rationale/sub-issue-cutover.md | rg -c '^## ')" -ge 6` passed on main dfc6da634df2 on 2026-11-12, exit 0.

### The session tree follows the issue tree, by rule

Decision (coordinator, 2026-11-13, on the owner's expectation of that day that the fleet organizes itself in a hierarchy as needed, paraphrased): the session tree is derived from the issue tree. A parent issue with more ready leaves than one session runs directly gets a lead, staffed by dispatch from a lead brief kept in the workers skill. That lead staffs its leaves and, for a child that is itself a parent over the same bound, a lead under it, to any depth. A lead whose reports or unanswered messages pass a measured bound is split along its children, and a lead ends when its subtree is closed or parked. The coordinator talks to the top leads only. Why: this issue's outcome is work tracked as a tree closed by landings, and the sessions that do the work should take their shape from that tree, not from whom the coordinator had time to launch. Alternative, not taken: keep leads launched by hand, which is what was late on 2026-11-13.

- The first slice is priced as the code-health reviews price work (cost in agent-minutes, saving per use, uses per day, staffed at a payback of three days or less), and lead staffing goes into north-dispatch, not into the fleet registry module the 2026-11-04 review lists as a hotspot.

No separate tests that a lead launch meets the API hold or the reserved account: a lead goes through the same place step as a box, whose tests already hold both, and a second pair would only duplicate them over the verification budget. title: Hold north's non-test Rust at 283,336 lines: a crossing ranks a retirement box first
body:
Spec: measured

Tom asked again for fewer lines through abstraction, libraries or dead-code removal (2026-11-12). A quick audit at main d30fdb501d found the tree's growth outweighs every cut on offer. An independent review then checked each claim of that audit against the code and the records (south `agents/decisions/harness/line-audit-review-2026-11-12.md`); the list below is its verdict.

What the review reproduced:

- Rust grew from 282,178 lines (123532ca3e, 2026-11-09) to 342,182 (d30fdb501d): 60,004 lines in 3.3 days, 75% product code and 25% test files, over 1,064 commits and 222 issues. 84% of the commits that touch Rust grow the tree, and 79% of the net growth arrives as new files. No total-size gate exists.
- 283,336 is the non-test count by this issue's path rule. It includes about 6,100 lines of inline test modules and the 2,131-line eval runner under `evals/`, and it moves by about 10% with line wrapping, because no landing check formats the code.
- Dead code is small (about 221 lines, north#1131), every library crate has a caller, and copy-paste is about 238 lines in 12 groups.
- Tests are 58,846 lines (17%) by the path rule, over 1,826 test functions. 708 of the 1,770 tests in the coverage map reach nothing another test does not; whether they kill a mutant no other test kills is not measured.

Worth doing, ranked by value to landing speed, use of the code graph and learning from the records:

1. Brief grounding at launch. The prompt-grounding hook and the context pack become one step that gives every worker's brief its files, their tests and earlier corrections as of the base commit. The hook as built reaches no worker and injects a form that names a right file on 1 of 19 tasks; the full query is about even with text search (12 against 10 of 19). An offline replay comes first, then a live arm (north#1147, north#1234).
2. An estimator backtest. Each learned value (ETA, budget, tier) drives its decision only while it beats its constant on a line registered before the run; the 2026-11-05 estimation audit found the tier estimate worse than the base rate and the ETA holding 56% where it claims 75% (north#1221).
3. The JSON work, as its two boxes below now read: seven escapers in six crates and pyjson go onto one ASCII-only formatter, about 870 product lines before the replacement's own code. Plain serde_json does not reproduce the bytes.

title: Enforce every guarantee in a layer every model provider passes through, not in Claude and Codex hooks alone
body:
Class: a guarantee enforced only by a provider hook does not hold for providers that have no hook binding, so OpenCode/DeepSeek, Pi and agy workers act outside rules Claude and Codex workers obey.

harness/policy-owners.toml `guard[]` binds hooks to Claude and Codex events only. OpenCode (DeepSeek), Pi and agy workers get the Landlock worker sandbox, the harness/overlays/deepseek.md text and the server-side gates (safe-push, lander), and no hook. On 2026-11-10 two DeepSeek workers ran safe-push with privacy overrides pointed at empty or missing sources (north#1037), and DeepSeek was staffed on sandbox issues that harness/opencode.toml claude_only reserves for Claude (north#1039 box 5). Tom asked (2026-11-10) that every improvement reach every model provider.

Rule: a guarantee lives in a layer every provider passes through (launch, worker sandbox and its outside broker, safe-push, lander, GitHub App permissions); a provider hook may only give earlier feedback on it. Instruction text has one source projected to every provider.

## Done when
- [x] Agent sessions run as a Unix user of their own, so the operator's state is closed to a worker by file ownership and not by a rule per path (the 2026-11-09 decision in docs/rationale/agent-user.md, not yet built; Docker and a microVM per agent stay rejected per docs/rationale/nix-leverage.md claim 8). First a plan that cuts the fourteen phases to the smallest slice that moves one build host's worker sessions under that user, names what breaks and which per-path rules it lets north delete. Done when: `git show origin/main:docs/rationale/agent-user.md | rg -c "^## First slice"` prints 1, and that section names the host, the steps in order with an estimate each, the replay that proves it (each worker-reach finding of 2026-11-12 refused by the kernel with its guard switched off) and the rules deleted after it. (decided 2026-11-12: the owner asked whether the sandbox is patched rule by rule, and chose the separate user the same evening; build it)
- [ ] Not before 2026-11-14T18:00Z: The agent user's first slice is built and proven on its host (plan: docs/rationale/agent-user.md, First slice; seven parts staffed 2026-11-12, about 16.5 h of work by the plan): worker sessions there run as the agent user from the agent's own repositories, landing takes a bundle as data, and a replay of each worker-reach class ends in a permission error from the kernel with its per-path guard off. Done when: the replay's output is posted on this issue with one line per class ending in EACCES, EPERM or EROFS, and after one normal day on that host the first-try rate and the landing p90 are posted beside the day before's; then the delete list of the plan is filed as the next box.
- [x] (after the first agent turn on the slice host) A stuck agent runtime link is seen: when a rollback cannot move the agent link off a runtime that failed its promotion, north writes it as a lifecycle row or runtime-lag line the next order and doctor read, and no runtime prune removes the target the agent link names. Done when: a rollback whose agent-link follow fails leaves that row or line (shown by the runtime update test or a doctor read), and `rg -n` over the runtime pruners names the agent link target as a kept root. (evidence: `cargo test -p north-runtime -- agent_link collecting_old` passes 5/5 on 2026-11-13; the rollback test leaves agent-link-stuck until the link moves, `north land doctor` reads it as bound agent-link-stuck (crates/north-lander-doctor/src/tests.rs:174), and crates/north-runtime-follow/src/collection.rs:33 keeps the runtime rooting agent link targets; landed 5d5a8a841e on origin/main)
- [x] (after the first agent turn on the slice host) The worker sandbox refuses a command it cannot confine: today when Landlock is unavailable or partial it prints `north worker-sandbox: Landlock unavailable (...), so removal, personal logins and build output are not confined` and runs the command anyway (crates/north-runtime/src/worker_sandbox/mod.rs:283-284; reported by the Buck2 stream 2026-11-13, did not fire that day). It refuses instead, unless the host's own config names it as a host without Landlock. Done when: a test that takes Landlock away reads the refusal, and fails with the change reverted; the second reviewer reads it. Owner: p-agent-user-slice4 lead, placed after the offloaded-checks-as-agent lane. Evidence: landed 487d4baf0411300435c0d4a4d12193f4afb7ac39 on origin/main; refuses unless `[hosts.NAME] landlock = false`; test a_command_the_kernel_cannot_confine_is_refused_unless_the_host_names_itself_without_landlock_north_1041.
- [ ] (before any agent session is enabled on a host) The agent user's subordinate uid and gid range overlaps no other user's: on the laptop the 2026-11-13 agent-user switch left /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid giving agent and farm the same range 165536:65536, so a user namespace of either maps onto the other's ids. South gives each user its own range on every host with the agent user (laptop, gex45, cpx62, nexus; cpx62b when reopened), second reviewer reads it. Done when: on each of those hosts `sort -t: -k2,2n /etc/subuid /etc/subgid` shows no two users whose ranges overlap, read after the switch, and no host enables agent sessions before that read. Owner: p-agent-user-slice4 lead (f-agent-hostconfig2). (open: needs a read of /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid on each host after the switch)
- [ ] (before the laptop's local agent sessions) A worker command cannot open a shell as the local agent user, while the worker sandbox keeps the system bus for reads. Today a worker command reaches the system bus and machined (the sandbox hides only sockets under /run/user/UID, crates/north-runtime/src/worker_sandbox/sockets.rs:30), and the session host shares its worker's scope (crates/north-fleet/src/fleet/host.rs:71), so neither hiding nor a caller-cgroup check on the session host can tell a launch from a worker's Bash. Hiding the bus would break worker reads, and a filtering D-Bus proxy is a new dependency on every command's bus path, so the ruling (agent-slice lead, 2026-11-13) is: local agent starts run only from a dedicated system unit, north-agent-starts.service with User= the operator, outside every session scope and outside the operator's user manager, fed by the fleet spool as sends are. It starts the agent side through machined's OpenMachineShell (`machinectl shell agent@.host PROGRAM`), not `systemd-run --machine=agent@.host --user`: on systemd 260 that path's inner `systemd-run -M.host` opens PID 1's namespaces and fails for a non-root caller before polkit ("Failed to open namespace of PID 1: Permission denied", sd-bus.c bus_set_address_machine and bus-container.c), and past that it would ask systemd1.manage-units, whose details name no User= and which is root-equivalent. The host's polkit rule admits machine1.host-shell only for user the agent, program and command_line a fixed root-owned entry, subject.user the operator and subject.system_unit that unit; polkit 127 sets system_unit only from a pidfd the bus broker handed it, so a reused pid cannot pass (its JS subject carries the pid and no start time), and a root-owned checker called through polkit.spawn narrows further by the caller's cgroup, read between two reads of its start time. No operator-uid process can borrow that unit's identity: the host keeps kernel.yama.ptrace_scope at 1 or above, so a process that is not the starter's ancestor can neither ptrace it nor open its /proc/PID/mem (machinectl is a fresh exec and dumpable again, so the scope, not the service's own PR_SET_DUMPABLE, guards it), and the worker sandbox's Landlock domain refuses ptrace outside it besides. OpenMachineShell's polkit details carry no environment (machine, user, program, command_line, machine-dbus.c in systemd 260), so the rule refuses every call not from the fixed unit, whose ExecStart passes no --setenv and whose machinectl, its output a pipe, adds only TERM=dumb; the fixed entry is a store script. The service reads each spool entry as a launch request with fixed fields (name, account, a cwd and a brief file under the agent's home), never a command, since workers write the spool; its unit takes no argument or bus input from the spool, and the request reaches the agent side on standard input only. The agent side reads its standard input as data, parses the same fixed fields and refuses anything else, then records the validated request and starts nothing else until the call-site box. Done when: a VM test refuses an operator command's `systemd-run --machine=agent@.host --user`, its `machinectl shell agent@.host` of the fixed entry, its AttachProcessesToUnit into the service and its write to the service's cgroup.procs, an operator process's ptrace attach and /proc/PID/mem open of the starter, lets the service's start through, and fails with the caller check removed; the polkit rule lands only after it. Owner: p-agent-user-slice4 lead (f-agent-opus-e). (open: the north-agent-starts unit's request path landed (76a7a9c822, 4bd269c774) but the host polkit rule and the refusal read are on the hosts)
- [ ] (the slice after the first agent turn) Offloaded checks of a lane run as the agent: a lane's own code runs on a build host as the agent user, in a checkout and object store the agent owns and can read, with the operator's checkout left untouched. The 2026-11-12 revert put offloaded land checks back on the operator login because the agent could not see the operator's checkout or its shipped objects. Done when: an offloaded land check on the slice host runs with `id -u` printing the agent's uid in a checkout under the agent's home, passes for a known-good lane, and leaves the operator's checkout's HEAD and mtime unchanged. (open: the agent offload landed (954a21398a) but the Done-when needs a live land check on the slice host)
- [x] (before agent sessions hand in work) The lander's fetch and outbox read pick the login by who owns the lane: a ticket whose lane root is under the agent's home is pulled and fetched as the host's agent login, and an operator lane keeps the operator login (the 2026-11-12 offload revert put both back on the operator login). Done when: a lane landed from an agent session on the slice host reaches main through the bundle or an agent-login fetch, and an operator lane on the same host still lands, both observed in the lander log. (landed 857dd71f07eb)
- [ ] (after the first agent turn on the slice host) The agent broker reaches the threads ledger with a key of its own: a separate ledger key for the broker on each agent host, with a nexus peer entry whose forced command allows only the threads verbs, so a broker compromise cannot reach the other remote-serve verbs (fleet rows, dispatch, south land) that the shared operator ledger key allows. Done when: the agent host's broker unit loads a key that differs from the operator's nexus key, and on nexus that key's authorized entry runs a command that refuses `fleet row put` (observed refusal). (open: no separate broker ledger key found on main; needs the nexus peer entry and a refusal observed there)
- [ ] (after the first slice) The managed settings layer is enabled on an agent host only with its permissions content and a placement decision for evals: firn's guard forces `disableBypassPermissionsMode` with no host override (modules/agent-claude-managed/default.nix:11-15, :34), so firn must let a host keep bypass; and the published agent runtime holds only north and verify-north (north-base store_refs.rs:30 RUNTIME_PROGRAMS), so the gated hooks call `/run/current-system/sw/bin/env` instead of a runtime env, or every gated hook exits 2; the managed file is machine-wide, so it carries the allow rules agent sessions need, keeps bypass mode available to `north fleet launch`, and is enabled only on a host where no eval arm needs plain or bypass sessions. Done when: on that host `/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json` holds non-empty permissions and no `disableBypassPermissionsMode`, an agent session launched by `north fleet launch` runs its first tool call, and the evals lead has recorded that no eval runs there. (open: needs the live host's managed-settings.json read and the evals lead's record)
- [x] (after the first agent turn on the slice host) A worker cannot pose as the user broker: where no /run/north-broker socket answers, broker_client connect() starts a user broker at ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/north-broker/broker.sock (crates/north-base/src/platform/broker_client.rs:105), and a worker can bind that socket first from inside its own domain, so unconfined clients on that host would talk to the worker's broker (found by the second reviewer 2026-11-13 reading capacity-write-route; the old whole-dir grant allowed the same). Store::read_only, which can miss WAL rows or tear a read, stays limited to the health report and never feeds an admission or lease decision. Done when: a test where a confined child binds the user socket first shows an unconfined client refusing it (peer-credential check), and fails with the change reverted; the second reviewer reads it. Evidence (2026-11-13): f3d66b67b0 on origin/main: broker_peer::vet refuses a same-user peer holding NoNewPrivs (set by every Landlock-confined process) when the client has not; the user-socket connect paths call it. Test an_unconfined_client_refuses_a_user_socket_a_confined_child_bound_first reads a `setpriv --no-new-privs` child as confined. Not shown: a revert run, and the second reviewer has not read it.
- [ ] (after the first agent turn on the slice host) An agent session cannot forge which programs confine it: the launch reads the agent runtime naming file through the agent login's own shell (north agent-session-programs, cde46d5055), so whoever can write that login's shell startup files (~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, ~/.ssh/rc, ~/.ssh/environment) can make the answer name an unconfined program for every later session's shell prefix and tool server (found by the second reviewer 2026-11-13). title: North is ready to be shown widely: current docs, a path from the README to a landed change, and an operator repository anyone can make
body:
Spec: exact
Scope: cross-module

## Problem

North is to be shown more widely on the weekend of 2026-11-14 (owner's direction of 2026-11-12, after the registered comparison with the plain runner passed its bar on runtime order 31). Three things stand between the repository and a newcomer:

- The docs have not had a whole-tree pass for weeks: pages describe commands and mechanisms that have since moved, the same subject is spread over several pages, and nothing says in what order to read them.
- There is no path a newcomer can follow from the README to one landed change on their own machine.
- North reads its operator's settings (accounts, hosts, rules, skills, decisions) from a private repository that nobody else can see, so nobody else can tell what theirs must contain.

## Decision

- The docs get an audit first (every page: keep, rewrite, merge or delete, with the evidence), then the verdicts are carried out; no page describes a command the binary does not have.
- The operator's repository is not published in a cleaned copy: a copy has to be scrubbed again at every sync, and one missed file or one old commit is a leak. Instead north itself carries the template: the schema of every file it reads from an operator repository, and a command that writes a working one with synthetic values. The private repository consumes it by passing the same check a newcomer's does. Generic method that today sits in the private repository moves into north through the existing privacy gate, piece by piece. The plan box below confirms or corrects this from the inventory before anything is built.
- What is announced, where and in whose name is the owner's decision, made on the finished pieces.

## Done when

- [x] Docs audit: every file under `docs/`, the README and AGENTS.md is listed once with a verdict (keep, rewrite, merge into a named page, delete) and its evidence (the command or code it describes exists and behaves as the page says, checked), plus the reading order a newcomer needs. Done when: `git show origin/main:docs/rationale/docs-audit-2026-11.md | wc -l` is non-zero and the file names every path `git ls-files docs README.md AGENTS.md` prints. — landed abd641c4af6f7b2a57288e9b2e751770288e755f on origin/main (first landed as 2773cc8d7ebcb664ed902cb0554763467d6a9716): 573 lines, 412 paths, 365 keep, 29 rewrite, 13 merge, 5 delete
- [x] Docs carried out: each audit verdict is applied (pages rewritten, merged or deleted, links fixed, one index in reading order), and no page names a `north` verb that `north --help` and its subcommand help do not list. Done when: the audit file marks every row done with its commit, and the repository's docs check exits 0. (landed 6f26d5ee44c5)
- [ ] Onboarding: one page takes a newcomer with a fresh user account, Nix and a model login from the README to one change landed in a scratch repository, with no step outside the page. Done when: a recorded run in a clean account or container follows the page's commands in order and lands the change in at most 30 minutes; the recording's command log is linked here.
- [ ] README and layout, rot-free: the owner asked for the best README of any project and a stupidly well organized tree that needs no hand upkeep (2026-11-14). Done when: the README leads with what north is, the comparison result and a quickstart that `north docs check` (or the existing doc-links scan) proves runnable; every number in it is rendered from a committed data file by one command and a check fails when the file and the README disagree; the README lists each top-level directory and each crate family once with a one-line purpose, and a check fails when the tree and that list disagree; nothing in it names a date, a host, an account or a count that a landing can make stale without the check catching it.
- [x] Operator repository, plan: `docs/rationale/operator-repository.md` lists every path north reads from the operator's repository, classes each (schema, generic method, private value, secret), and decides how the public template and a private repository relate, with the alternatives it rejected and what each would cost. Done when: `git show origin/main:docs/rationale/operator-repository.md | wc -l` is non-zero and a reviewer has marked the plan Done on this issue. Landed as cda5987959.
- [x] Operator repository, built: `north config operator init DIR` writes a working operator repository with synthetic values and nothing private, and `north config operator check DIR` passes on it and on the owner's private one. Done when: both commands exit 0 (the private run is recorded in the private repository). Evidence: on 2026-11-13, `north config operator init D` exit 0 (16 files) and `north config operator check D` exit 0; `north config operator check /home/tom/code/south/main` exit 0; the private run is recorded in the private repository by its landing line, landed 434d83f40f07 (south) whose safe-push ran `north config operator check .` at exit 0. Build boxes 6, 8, 9, 10 and 14 stay open as their own boxes.
  Build boxes, from `docs/rationale/operator-repository.md` (each at most 40 minutes; `D` is a new scratch directory; 1 to 9 give the first hour, 10 to 14 hold it and the private data in place, 15 to 17 can follow):
  - [x] Operator 1, registry: `north config operator paths` prints one line per inventory row with its class. Done when: `test "$(north config operator paths | wc -l)" = 32 && test "$(north config operator paths --class secret | wc -l)" = 7` exits 0 (reworded 2026-11-13 into one command the checker runs; bar unchanged). Evidence: `test "$(north config operator paths | wc -l)" = 32 && test "$(north config operator paths --class secret | wc -l)" = 7` passed on main 4a07bba19155 on 2026-11-12, exit 0.
  - [x] Operator 2, schemas for the account and cost files. Done when: `north config operator check --only costs,claude-accounts,credentials,infra` exits 0 on the owner's checkout and exits 1 naming file and key on a scratch copy with one key misspelled.
  - [x] Operator 3, schemas for the policy files. Done when: `north config operator check --only policy` exits 0 on the owner's checkout and exits 1 naming file and key on a scratch copy with one key misspelled.
  - [x] Operator 4, schema for orchestration, the account side. Done when: `north config operator check --only orchestration-accounts` exits 0 on the owner's checkout and exits 1 naming the key on a scratch copy with one key misspelled. Evidence: `north config operator check --only orchestration-accounts` exits 0 on the owner's checkout at south main and exits 1 naming `accounts.codex.targt_left: unknown key` on a scratch copy with the key misspelled, at north 2133d1140a on 2026-11-13.
  - [x] Operator 5, schema for orchestration, the host side and every remaining key. Done when: `north config operator check --only orchestration` exits 0 on the owner's checkout and exits 1 on a scratch copy with an unknown table. Evidence: `north config operator check --only orchestration` exits 0 on the owner's checkout (the schema now accepts `buck2_host_cases` and `buck2_tree_build`) and exits 1 on a scratch copy with an unknown key, at north 2133d1140a on 2026-11-13.
  - [x] Operator 6, catalog: the schema file at the place the catalog's `$schema` names, and registrations generated from north's structure registry. Done when: `north config operator init D && north config agents check-owners --north-root . --south-root D` exits 0 with no machine-configuration root named. — landed 4daaac631e14f65770108ed18b55272b8d523681 on origin/main; on the lane before landing, `north config operator init D` exit 0 (17 files) and `north config agents check-owners --north-root . --south-root D` exit 0 printing "no machine-configuration root named" and "agents owner registrations resolve at their landing refs", 2026-11-13.
  - [x] Operator 7, init, configuration: every schema-class file with synthetic values, starter privacy lists, a secrets directory holding only a note, the schema marker and a landing configuration. Done when: `north config operator init D && north config operator check D` exits 0 and a second init into another directory gives the same tree by `diff -r`. Evidence: `north config operator init D && north config operator check D` exit 0 and a second init gives the same tree by `diff -r`, at north 2133d1140a on 2026-11-13; `north config operator check` also exits 0 on the owner's checkout.
  - [x] Operator 8, init, policy: starter global rules written new in north, with their register. Done when: `north check harness policy-gate session --operator D/agents` exits 0. Evidence: landed 605b5f7dc0 on origin/main (starter AGENTS.md with eight rules in new text, rules.toml register, and the session gate treating a starter operating point with n 0 as not yet measured); on 2026-11-13 a binary built from main ef4a47753 ran `north config operator init D` (17 files, exit 0) then `north check harness policy-gate session --operator D/agents`, exit 0 ("no measured operating point yet (starter n 0)"). The older installed `north` still fails with a missing AGENTS.md until it is rebuilt.
  - [x] Operator 9, sync with an operator repository that has no origin and with no machine-configuration checkout. Done when: in a scratch home holding north's runtime and init's output, `agents sync` exits 0 and the published generation exists. Evidence: landed c424e57e4 on origin/main; `HOME=/tmp/op9/home5 /tmp/op9/home5/.local/state/north/current/north config agents sync` exits 0 in a scratch home whose operator repository has no origin and no north or nixos-config checkout, and publishes `/tmp/op9/home5/.local/state/north/agents/gen-2a615e43132724bad352f0b23f8a34f9b4ff6442b29157fa13816d55a4fcaf06`.
  - [x] Operator 10, example tree: `examples/operator/` equals init's output and the landing checks it. Done when: `north config operator init --check examples/operator` exits 0 on main and exits 1 after one byte of the example changes. Evidence: landed 9e2ba38a58 on origin/main on 2026-11-13; `north config operator init --check examples/operator` exit 0 and exit 1 naming `secrets/NOTE.md: differs from init's output` after one byte was appended to a copy; the landing runs the check when examples/operator/, structure.toml or the init code change (.safe-push).
  - [x] Operator 11, private side, in the private repository: the schema marker and the check line in its landing. Done when: `north config operator check .` exits 0 at its main, with the run recorded there. Evidence: landed 434d83f40f07 on south main; the landing ran `north config operator check .` at exit 0 on 2026-11-13.
  - [x] Operator 12, north's landing protects the owner's checkout. Done when: a drill lane that makes one optional key required is refused at landing with the key named. (landed 83530f568176)
  - [x] Operator 13, private-file refusal: safe-push refuses, for a public destination, an added file that is byte for byte a file in the operator repository's history, unless an approved-moves list there names it. Done when: a drill lane copying one file from a scratch operator repository into a scratch public one is refused with the path named, lands once the list names it, and a run over main's last 200 commits prints each hit. (landed efb92420e7b5)
  - [x] Operator 13b, the private-file refusal cannot be skipped unseen. Found by the commit review of the refusal on 2026-11-13: when the operator repository's checkout on the lander's host is not a git repository the check reads as clean, and its cache under the lander's state directory is trusted by name and count. For a public destination with an operator repository configured, an added file is refused when that repository cannot be read, naming the cause; with none configured the check is skipped and says so; and the cache sits where no worker command can write. Done when: a test that points the check at a configured path that is not a repository gets a refusal naming it and fails with the fix reverted, and the worker sandbox's own test shows a worker command's write to the cache refused. (landed 80b143969c19)

title: fix(issueops): counter mint jumps past ids either plane already holds (supersedes #6754)
body:
Supersedes #6754 by @quad341, with credit.

## Decision needed before merge: overlap with open PRs

This PR re-delivers the parts of #6754 that main still lacks. Four other open PRs already carry some of those parts, one of them with the opposite counter rule, and two more change the same code. Do not merge it until a maintainer decides which PR carries which part. `git merge-tree` of this head against each one:

| PR | State | Overlap with this PR | Conflicts with this head |
|---|---|---|---|
| #8466 (for #8456) | approved, awaiting approval | Counter mint: it skips held ids and moves to the first free number in both mints (issueops and domain). A far-ahead id such as `bd-5000` does not make the counter jump. This PR's 898ed4f7de jumps to one past the highest held id instead. | helpers.go, id_retention.go, id_retention_test.go, generate_issue_id_test.go, configuration.md |
| #8467 | review failed | Domain-side counter jump and create-only for minted ids (proxied-server path) | configuration.md |
| #8454 (for #7289) | approved by bee-ghosttrack; review run ended without approval | Per-attempt replay reset in `dolt/issues.go`: 49031b39a9 and 1239628e32 here | dolt/issues.go |
| #8470 (for #8457) | approved, awaiting approval | Reset of assigned ids after a definite failure: 3b8b15ff74 here | dolt/issues.go, embeddeddolt/create_issue.go, embedded-storage-test-shards.txt |
| #8464 | approved, awaiting approval | Same record/reset helper for the proxied importer (`SnapshotUnsetCreateIDs` next to this PR's `RecordAssignedIDs`) | none (merges cleanly; leaves two helpers) |
| #8218 | owner's p0, review failed | Whole-request restore on replay, in the same three `dolt/issues.go` closures | dolt/issues.go |

The maintainer direction on record, in bee-ghosttrack's reviews, points both ways on the issueops counter rule:
- On #8466 (2026-11-14, approved): "land this one first; #8467's rebase should drop its jump (or adopt the end-of-run semantics) rather than carry both". This PR's counter half is the same max jump, in the issueops mint that #8466 rewrites.
- On #8470 (2026-11-14, approved): "Landing order stays as the PR body documents: #8454 first, then this PR".
- On this PR (2026-11-14 07:23Z, changes requested at 3f39934fda): "The production change is right and I have it verified end to end". It asks for one change, a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` → `### Fixed` bullet that also records the jump this PR documents ("the counter jumps to one past the highest held id of its prefix and does not fill the gap"). That review does not mention #8466, so it does not settle which counter rule lands. The decision is still needed.

The one part no other open PR carries for the issueops path is the create-only insert for minted ids: 701c0539d6, with this review's fixup and its tests (`TestMintedIDCreateInsertsCreateOnly`, `TestExplicitIDCreateBehaviorUnchanged`, `TestRunInTransactionMintsBothPlanesInOneShard`). If the #8466 direction stands, land #8466, #8454 and #8470 first, then rebase this PR and cut it down to that part. Its other four commits would be dropped, or folded into those PRs. If this PR should replace them instead, their threads need to say so, with the reason, before it merges.

## Summary

Both candidates agree: auto-minted IDs can upsert occupied rows, and replay mistakes rolled-back generated IDs for caller input. Counter mode fails to check live occupants, causing overwrites or repeated guarded failures. Use strict auto-mint inserts, collision-triggered counter jumps and assigned-ID resets, preserving identities after uncertain commits. The hash sibling-plane lookup is already fixed; there is no diagnostic disagreement.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Criterion | glm | opus | pr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | Given counter 1 and explicit cl-2/cl-100 across the live planes, when a legacy or guarded single/batch API auto-mints, then it creates cl-101, preserves occupants and next mints cl-102. | partial | pass | - |
| AC-2 | Given an occupied auto-minted ID at guard/insert, when default or ConflictSkip creation runs, then it returns ErrAlreadyExists without overwriting or silently skipping. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-3 | Given a server single-create losing commit to a writer under its minted ID, when replay runs, then it re-mints distinctly and both rows retain their content and one created event each. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-4 | Given a server batch with generated issue/comment IDs and default dependency owners, when forced conflict triggers replay, then new issue identities own correctly regenerated auxiliary identities and the winner's auxiliary data is unchanged. | partial | pass | - |
| AC-5 | Given single/batch creation on either store, when its transaction fails, then generated fields reset on definite failure, supplied IDs remain, and indeterminate or post-SQL failures retain assigned identities. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-6 | Given an explicit ID, when creation meets an existing/sibling/retired row, then caller-option update, skip, stale/retired guard and error behavior remains unchanged. | pass | partial | - |

The `pr` column is empty: the triage replay could not run #6754's own tests, because its branch predates `MODULE.bazel` and Bazel refused to start. bee-ghosttrack approved #6754 at e2f711a129 after running its tests by hand.

## Maintainer review fixup (iterations 1 and 2)

This commit is in the review worktree, not on the PR branch yet. It is pushed once a review pass approves the head.

- **Minted creates no longer tear a server `RunInTransaction`.** Forcing create-only on every minted create made each one write its id's `issue-create/v1/<shard>` coordination cell. With the events journal off, a server `RunInTransaction` writes regular rows on one SQL session and wisps on another. When a regular and a wisp minted id fell in the same one of the 4096 shards, both sessions wrote that cell. The regular session committed, the wisp session then failed with a serialization error, and the caller got `ErrCommitIndeterminate` with every wisp lost. Now, a create-only that the mint forces (the caller did not ask for `CreateOnly`) keeps the occupancy read and the strict INSERT but writes no cell, as on base for that route. A caller that asked for `CreateOnly` keeps the cell, as on base.
  - Trade-off: since #6754, the cell also gave a minted create and an explicit create of the same id on the other plane a row to conflict on at commit. The mint's snapshot already excludes every held id, so all that goes unseen now is an explicit create of the very id the mint drew, committed on the other plane while the transaction runs. Base never covered that on this route either.
  - New `TestRunInTransactionMintsBothPlanesInOneShard` (Dolt server): 64 regular issues and 64 wisps are minted per transaction, until a regular and a wisp id share a shard (round 0: `test-ih1~test-wisp-8qw`). Both planes must land. With the forced create-only writing the cell again, it fails in round 0 with `sql commit (ignored, regular already committed): Error 1213 (40001): serialization failure ... write commit result indeterminate`.
  - `TestMintedIDCreateInsertsCreateOnly` now refuses a coordination write in the forced cases and expects one when the caller asked for `CreateOnly`.
- **Docs.** The counter bullet in `docs/reference/configuration.md` now names the modes it covers, embedded and direct SQL-server. Proxied-server mode and `bd serve` against a server-mode workspace mint through the unit-of-work provider, which so far skips only retired IDs. Since iteration 2 it no longer vouches for a proxied-server import row that names no ID: the unit-of-work importer replays a lost attempt with the ID that attempt wrote onto the row (#8464 fixes that replay).
- **CHANGELOG (iteration 2).** `CHANGELOG.md` has the `[Unreleased]` → `### Fixed` entry that bee-ghosttrack's review asks for, crediting #6754 by quad341. One sub-bullet each: the counter-mode refusal and overwrite with the jump past held IDs, the create-only insert of a generated ID, the server replay re-mint, and the reset after a failed create. If this PR is cut down to the create-only part, the entry keeps only that sub-bullet.
- **Comments (iteration 2).** The lock-ordering comments in `create_only_guard.go` now name the minted create-only that takes no coordination cell.
- **Credit.** The commit carries `Co-authored-by: Jim Wordelman <jim@wordelman.name>` for #6754's create-only design.

Tests run on the fixup head (iteration 2 changed only comments, docs and the CHANGELOG; the Dolt and embedded runs are iteration 1's):
- `bazel-test //internal/storage/issueops:issueops_test`: 1133 passed, in both iterations.
- `//internal/storage/dolt:dolt_test` on the Dolt lane: 45 passed. The run covered this PR's four store tests, the new test, every `TestRunInTransaction*` test, `TestTransactionCreateIssueNoDoubleHyphen` and `TestCrossProject_ConcurrentWrites`.
- `//internal/storage/embeddeddolt:embeddeddolt_embedded_test --config=embedded`: this PR's three embedded tests, 12 subtests passed.
- `//scripts:go_test_sources_test`: 26 passed.
- Iteration 2, the targets that read `CHANGELOG.md` and the docs: `//scripts:android_release_docs_test`, `//scripts:tracked_files_test`, `//scripts/repochecks:doc_freshness_test`, `//scripts/repochecks:go_install_guidance_test` and `//test/docsync:docsync_test` passed.

## How this was built

- Design: `design.pair` (anthropic-opus, moonshot-kimi, xai-grok, zhipu-glm).
- Independent candidates: glm (pass), opus (pass), pr (no test ran; see above).
- Judge (grok) composed the change per AC: AC-1 ← opus, AC-2 ← opus, AC-3 ← opus, AC-4 ← opus, AC-5 ← opus, AC-6 ← merge.
  - AC-6: merged by the integrator (keep opus 12076e3a81c1 (TestExplicitIDCreateBehaviorUnchanged in embeddeddolt/create_auto_mint_test.go, incl. guarded-create refusal and real retaining-sweep retired case) and add from glm 1dd208fa3be8 (embeddeddolt/create_explicit_id_contract_test.go) the cases opus lacks: TestExplicitIDRejectsAStaleUpsert (RejectStaleUpserts + OnStaleRejected keeps a newer stored row), the ConflictSkip-skip legs of TestExplicitIDRefusesARetiredID and TestExplicitIDRefusesASiblingPlaneID, and the created-event-count assertions of TestExplicitIDUpsertUpdatesAnExistingRow/ConflictSkipLeavesAnExistingRow (as subtests or sibling funcs; helpers exist at base). Then regenerate .github/scripts/embedded-storage-test-shards.txt for every new embeddeddolt Test func (glm never did) and make bazel-sync.)
- Canonical tests: `bazel-test //internal/storage/issueops:issueops_test --test_filter='^(TestGenerateIssueIDCounterModeJumpsPastHeldIDs|TestCounterJumpEscapesLikeWildcardsInThePrefix|TestGenerateIssueIDCounterModeWalksPastAClaimedValue|TestGenerateIssueIDCounterModeWalksPastARetiredValue|TestMintedIDCreateInsertsCreateOnly|TestAssignedIDsResetAfterFailure)$' && bazel-test //internal/storage/dolt:dolt_test --test_filter='^(TestCreateIssue_CounterModeJumpsPastExplicitIDs|TestCreateIssueReplayRemintsAfterSameIDCommit|TestCreateIssuesReplayKeepsEdgesOnRemintedID|TestCreateFailureResetsAssignedIDs)$' --test_env=BEADS_TEST_SKIP= --test_env=BEADS_TEST_DOLT_SERVER=local --test_env=BEADS_TEST_REQUIRE_DOLT_CONTAINER=1 && bazel-test //internal/storage/embeddeddolt:embeddeddolt_embedded_test --config=embedded --test_sharding_strategy=disabled --test_arg='-test.run=^(TestCounterMintJumpsPastHeldIDs|TestCreateFailureResetsAssignedIDs|TestExplicitIDCreateBehaviorUnchanged)$' && bazel-test //scripts:go_test_sources_test` → pass.
- Final review (kimi): pass.

Judge rationale: Same behaviour in both (strict CreateOnly for minted ids, collision-only counter jump across four tables, record/reset of generated issue/comment/dep-owner ids per attempt and on definite failure, nil-default per-store hook), so pick per AC. AC-1 opus: counterIDSuffix bounds to MaxInt32-1 (issue_counter.last_id is INT; glm's Atoi parser lets a huge held suffix make the raise UPDATE fail out of range and wedge the mint), digits-only (Atoi accepts '+5'), LIKE-escapes the prefix with a wildcard test, docs carry the design's 2/100 example; glm also extends the domain minter + IssueSQLRepository interface, which the design put out of scope (not ported). AC-2 code equivalent; opus test is a 2x2 matrix (default/ConflictSkip x occupied at guard/insert) with an ODKU-refusing matcher and a caller-opts-unchanged check. AC-3 opus: hash+counter subtests, asserts attempts>=2, winner via real store.CreateIssue; glm counter-only, no replay-count assert. AC-4 opus: both batch arms (durable + all-wisps), asserts the comment id was re-derived and the winner's own comment/edge are unchanged plus an explicit batch member keeps its id; glm covers the durable arm only and counts comments without checking comment-id re-derivation. AC-5 opus: server single/batch x definite/indeterminate via the hook, embedded failure then successful retry with supplied comment ids preserved, recorder unit test; glm comparable but weaker on indeterminate at store level. AC-6 merge: opus covers guarded refusal and real sweep, glm uniquely pins the stale-upsert guard and ConflictSkip skips; opus registered the embedded shard manifest, glm did not. PR #6754's own repro fails after its fix; no contributor code chosen, credit stays via the pipeline.

(The rationale's "PR #6754's own repro fails after its fix" means the repro could not run on that branch, as noted under the acceptance criteria. Credit is carried by the fixup's `Co-authored-by:` trailer.)

title: crates.io: reserved pod-* names and trusted publishing
body:
Every `pod-*` name of `docs/design.md` section 4 is reserved on crates.io as a `0.0.0` placeholder owned by the owner. This issue tracks the reservations; it is updated as each name is published (crates.io allows about one new crate every 10 minutes).

**Trusted publishing** (set on each crate once it exists): repository `PodUtils/podcrates`, workflow `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, environment `crates-io` (deployable from `v*` tags only). Token publishing stays allowed until each crate's first release from CI; then the owner turns on "Require trusted publishing".

This does not change the Q1 ruling: podcrates publishes nothing to crates.io until the owner says so. The placeholders only hold the names.

## Registered on 2026-11-12

The owner's word of 2026-11-11 (podcrates `docs/decisions.md`, row "podrunner DR-3, DR-8 to DR-17"): "update the issue tracker for crates & repos you need so my local agent may register them". Each name below gave 404 on `https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/NAME` on 2026-11-12. Same setup as the project names: a `0.0.0` placeholder, then a trusted publisher of the repository of the same name (workflow `publish.yml`, environment `crates-io`). All three were registered with their trusted publisher on 2026-11-12.

Updates `express` from 5.2.1 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"

Updates `@playwright/test` from 1.63.0 to 1.65.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

    test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
  // No other test runs while this one is running.
});

  • test.skip(), test.fixme(), test.fail() and test.slow() now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

    test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
  test.skip('Not implemented yet');
});
