Updates `express` from 5.2.1 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

title: fix(list): register --include-all-types and read it onto ListRequest
body:
## Summary

Both designs agree: `bd list` cannot set `ListRequest.IncludeAllTypes`, and `--all` help overstates what it includes. Register and wire the union flag, admit it in the wisp-type guard, and clarify help without changing existing selectors or backend semantics. Preserve contributor PR #8191, which already implements this approach, including its tests and attribution; accept and document the existing HTTP refusal. Resolve the candidates' documentation disagreement in favor of release-pinned CLI reference pages and an Unreleased CHANGELOG entry.

## Relationship to #8191

Contributor PR #8191 by kyoto-bonsai, opened and approved in review on 2026-11-07, carries the same production change: its `cmd/bd/list.go` and `cmd/bd/list_input.go` hunks and both command-tree goldens are line-for-line identical to this PR's. This PR also carries #8191's `cmd/bd/list_include_all_types_test.go` and CHANGELOG entry byte for byte, and adds four checks of its own in `cmd/bd/list_all_types_union_test.go`, with the `//internal/httpapi/apigen` test dep they need. The two PRs therefore merge cleanly in either order, and whichever lands second adds only what the first lacks. The production change, its tests and the CHANGELOG entry are kyoto-bonsai's work, credited in every commit here.

Landing order: #8191 lands first, then this PR. On 2026-11-14 at 05:48Z `bee-ghosttrack` approved both PRs and named that order. On this PR: "My preference is that #8191 lands first, as the contributor's fix, and that this PR then rebases to its remaining delta". On #8191: "this PR first, as the contributor's fix; #8480 then rebases to its test-only and CHANGELOG-wording delta". This PR is held until #8191 has merged. After that it adds only `cmd/bd/list_all_types_union_test.go` and its two `cmd/bd/BUILD.bazel` lines (the srcs entry and the `//internal/httpapi/apigen` dep). If a maintainer decides instead that this PR lands first, #8191 is closed as superseded with the credit this PR carries, and that note goes on #8191 before this PR merges.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC-1:** Given `bd list` with no other selectors, when `--include-all-types` is parsed and the request/filter built, then `IncludeAllTypes` is true, the four narrow include fields remain false, and default type/template/wisp-plane suppressions are absent; without the flag the union is false.
- **AC-2:** Given a list invocation and the same invocation with `--include-all-types`, when their requests and filters are built, then only default type/plane suppression changes, with status/pinned defaults, effective limit and explicit predicates preserved.
- **AC-3:** Given `--wisp-type heartbeat` without another plane selector or an explicit type, when combined with `--include-all-types`, then gathering succeeds and carries both intents; without the union it retains the current reachability error.
- **AC-4:** Given `bd list --help`, when rendered, then `--all` accurately names default status/pinned/limit behavior and points at the union, the union names issue types and the wisp plane while preserving status/pinned defaults, and unrelated help rows do not change.
- **AC-5:** Given an HTTP list reader using the current v0 wire, when it receives the union request gathered from the new flag, then it returns the existing typed IncludeAllTypes refusal instead of returning issue rows; the user-facing CHANGELOG documents this limitation.

Candidate grades:

| AC | glm | opus | pr8191 |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | pass | pass | - |
| AC-2 | pass | pass | - |
| AC-3 | pass | pass | - |
| AC-4 | partial | pass | - |
| AC-5 | partial | pass | - |

## How this was built

- Design: `design.pair` (anthropic-opus, moonshot-kimi, xai-grok, zhipu-glm).
- Independent candidates: glm (pass), opus (pass), pr8191 (untested).
- Judge (grok) composed the change per AC: AC-1 ← opus, AC-2 ← opus, AC-3 ← opus, AC-4 ← opus, AC-5 ← opus.
- Canonical tests: `bazel-test //cmd/bd:bd_test //internal/workapi:workapi_test //internal/httpclient/encode:encode_test --test_filter='^(TestListIncludeAllTypesReachable|TestListRegistersIncludeAllTypes|TestGatherListInput_IncludeAllTypesReachesTheFilter|TestGatherListInput_IncludeAllTypesChangesOnlyTheTypeAxis|TestGatherListInput_ExistingFlagsKeepTheirRequestIdentity|TestGatherListInput_WispType.*|TestListIncludeAllTypesUsageKeepsTheStatusAxis|TestListAllUsageIsStatusOnly|TestListHelpIsByteIdenticalOutsideIncludeAllTypes|TestIncludeAllTypesOverHTTPRefusesWithTheLedgerRow|TestListRegistersIncludeEphemeral|TestCommandTreeGolden|TestCommandHelpGolden|TestIncludeAllTypesLiftsEverySuppression|TestEncoderHonorsEveryTableDisposition)$'` → pass.
- Final review (kimi): pass.

Judge rationale: Production code (cmd/bd/list.go flag + --all help, cmd/bd/list_input.go gather + wisp-type guard) is byte-identical across opus, glm and contributor PR #8191 (both candidates are faithful ports with Co-authored-by kyoto-bonsai); behaviour is not divergent, only tests/CHANGELOG differ. AC-1 opus: same code and Reachable test as glm, but opus's AC-1 commit re-pins the tree/help goldens with the flag so it is green on its own; glm's AC-1 commit registers the flag without the golden update (goldens only fixed in its AC-4 commit), breaking bisect. AC-2 opus: adds TestGatherListInput_IncludeAllTypesChangesOnlyTheTypeAxis, which DeepEquals the whole IssueFilter with/without the flag after clearing only SkipWisps/ExcludeTypes/IsTemplate, a strictly tighter 'only the type axis moves' pin than the PR's per-field checks that glm keeps; all PR subtests (explicit limit, exclude-type, narrow flags, --all, infra type, custom statuses) and ExistingFlagsKeepTheirRequestIdentity are preserved. AC-3: identical guard change and identical PR test in both; opus for coherence of the single test file. AC-4 opus: TestListIncludeAllTypesUsageKeepsTheStatusAxis asserts the union help names 'issue types', 'wisp plane', 'pinned', 'still apply', '--all' as AC-4 requires; PR/glm only check 'status'/'still apply'; byte-identical-help and --all wording tests preserved. title: fix(list): register --include-all-types and say what --all lifts
body:
Closes #5694

## What changed

`ListRequest.IncludeAllTypes` lifts every type suppression (gates, templates, infra, wisp plane, any added later) by skipping `applyTypeSuppressions`, but `bd list` had no flag for it. `bd list` now registers `--include-all-types`; `--wisp-type` works with it (it admits the wisp plane). The default status and pinned exclusions and the default limit still apply. `--all`'s help now says what it lifts (the default status and pinned exclusions and the default limit) and that the type and plane suppressions still apply. The `bd serve` HTTP transport refuses the new flag with its existing typed error, as it does for every other caller of the field.

## Evidence it works

Scratch store (nocgo bd, `--proxied-server`), run on the first commit; the second changes only help text, comments, tests, goldens and the CHANGELOG: 2 open tasks, a gate, an ephemeral and a closed task.

```

bd list --json --limit 0           2               2
bd list --include-all-types        unknown flag    4 (+gate +wisp)
bd list --all --include-all-types  unknown flag    5
```

Tests: `cmd/bd/list_include_all_types_test.go` (`//cmd/bd:bd_test`). Five of its six tests fail on main and pass here; the invariant test passes on both.

- No-change test: `TestListHelpIsByteIdenticalOutsideIncludeAllTypes`: help minus the flag's line equals help with the flag hidden, byte for byte.
- Invariant test: `TestGatherListInput_ExistingFlagsKeepTheirRequestIdentity`: twelve existing flag sets build the same `ListRequest`, effective limit and filter with or without it; passes on main too.

- Mutant 1: drop the `include-all-types` read -> `TestGatherListInput_IncludeAllTypesReachesTheFilter`
- Mutant 2: drop `!in.IncludeAllTypes` from the `--wisp-type` guard -> `TestGatherListInput_WispTypeWithIncludeAllTypesIsAccepted`

- Mutant 4: a backticked usage word (pflag turns it into a value placeholder) -> `TestListRegistersIncludeAllTypes`; `TestListHelpIsByteIdenticalOutsideIncludeAllTypes` also fails once the placeholder widens the flag column
- Mutant 5: `--all` also sets `IncludeAllTypes` -> `TestGatherListInput_ExistingFlagsKeepTheirRequestIdentity`

title: fix(storage): treat same-database cross-prefix dependency targets as local
body:
Closes #8299.

## Problem

A dependency on an issue with another prefix was stored as external even when that issue was **present in the same database**. `bd ready`, `bd blocked`, and hierarchy checks then missed a real local blocker.

## Change

- Classify targets by visible issue/wisp presence across single, batch, import, embedded, Dolt, UOW and server-mode writes. An active wisp takes precedence; explicit `external:` references and absent foreign IDs remain external.
- Propagate failed target-presence probes rather than silently filing an unverified external edge. Only the missing optional `wisps` table is treated as absence.
- Before removing a hydrated repository, preserve cross-prefix dependencies onto its departing issues as external edges, including their type and metadata.
- Preserve the distinct doctor repair from #8400: truly unverified cross-repository targets are not orphans. The compatibility fix updates that code's prefix check.

## Compatibility and limitations

- **Existing misfiled edges are not rewritten.** Remove and re-add an edge with its original type/metadata to make it local. Re-syncing a formerly absent target does not automatically reclassify the stored edge.
- An unrelated existing issue remains: syncing a changed target's status may leave dependent `is_blocked` state stale. This PR does not change that recomputation.

## Verification

- Prior maintainer validation covered issueops, Dolt, embedded Dolt, UOW, command behavior and regression mutants; see the [review discussion](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/8300#pullrequestreview-5855573593).
- Head `208513ab`: removed the obsolete doctor call introduced by merging #8400. Bazel built `//cmd/bd:bd`; focused doctor classification tests and four Dolt-backed orphan cases ran and passed (four shards). `gofmt` and diff checks pass.
- Fork-gated workflows need maintainer authorization. No claim of complete CI success.

## Model Used

Original authoring: Anthropic Claude Code (exact model unrecorded). Subsequent analysis, corrections and review: OpenAI GPT-6. The Gas City pipeline contributed an independent implementation; its exact model provenance is not established here.

## Checklist

- [x] Linked issue, compatibility, risks and focused validation documented.
- [x] User-facing behavior and change notes documented.
- [ ] Full Bazel CI and required integration suites green on latest head (maintainer-gated).

### Beads v1.3.1

**v1.3.1** — the first patch release on the 1.3 line. Released 2026-09-30, cut from `hotfix/1.3.1`
at `c1c4b642a`. It ships exactly the code that was qualified as `v1.3.1-rc.2`; the only change since
that candidate is the version stamp.

There is **no schema migration**. Upgrading from v1.3.0, v1.3.1-rc.1 or v1.3.1-rc.2 is a binary
swap. If you are still on v1.2.2 or earlier, read the
[v1.3.0 release notes](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/tag/v1.3.0) first — everything
in them applies, and this release adds to it.

The release is mostly about proxied-server mode, which became the default topology in 1.3.0: it gets
a backup path, honors `dolt.auto-commit`, can watch a bead, and stops reporting a dead backend as
running. Alongside that it fixes a fan-in stall that hid ready work, gives orchestrators a bounded
wisp-retention sweep, and corrects several commands whose exit codes or output scripts could not
trust. Several of those corrections change behaviour a script may depend on, so read the upgrading
notes.

#### Highlights

- **A proxied-server workspace has a backup path** ([#​6582](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6582), [#​6584](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6584), [#​6694](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6694), [#​6879](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6879)). In v1.3.0 `bd
  backup` was refused outright on a proxied workspace, which was listed as a known issue. On a
  proxied workspace whose Dolt server bd runs itself, `bd backup init`, `sync`, `remove`, `status`
  and `restore` now work, and an explicit `backup.enabled=true` turns on the same throttled
  auto-backup direct mode takes. Auto-backup stays off by default. On a proxied workspace pointed at
  a Dolt server bd does not own, the family stays refused by design, because a backup remote
  registered there would be global to every client of that server.
- **Fan-in no longer stalls ready work** ([#​6716](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6716); [#​6719](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6719), [#​6942](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6942)). Closing two blockers of one
  dependent at the same time — formula fan-in with parallel workers, or a close racing a `bd dep
  remove` or a delete — could leave the dependent `is_blocked=1` and missing from `bd ready` until
  someone ran `bd recompute-blocked`. Every write that takes a blocker away now rechecks its
  dependents after it commits, on the Dolt store, on every proxied-server write route, and inside
  `RunInTransaction`.
- **`bd purge` can run an orchestrator's wisp retention sweep** ([#​6883](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6883)). `bd purge --wisps-plane --older-than 168h --force` replaces a raw `DELETE FROM wisps` step. `--limit` drains a large
  backlog in bounded transactions, `--older-than` takes hours, and a closed bead that live work
  still depends on is always kept.
- **Proxied-server mode catches up with direct mode.** `dolt.auto-commit=batch`/`off` take effect and
  `bd dolt commit` works ([#​6499](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6499)). `bd show --watch` works ([#​6933](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6933)). `bd dolt start` no longer launches
  a second sql-server over the proxy's data directory, and `bd dolt status` reports the proxy and
  its backend truthfully ([#​6580](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6580)). The proxy retires when its Dolt backend exits cleanly instead of
  staying up in front of a dead store ([#​6937](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6937)). Refusals that remain now say whether they are
  permanent (`reason: design`) or a gap with an owner (`reason: unimplemented`) ([#​6582](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6582)).
- **The smart migrate gate stops wedging clones that are behind the remote** ([#​6575](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6575); [#​6659](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6659), [#​6695](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6695)).
  A clone level with the remote on schema but behind it on data used to auto-migrate in place,
  after which every `bd dolt pull` refused ([#​6368](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6368)). The gate now stops and tells you to run `bd dolt
  pull` first, and `bd dolt pull` is allowed to run from that state.
- **Exit codes and output scripts can rely on.** A `bd close` batch with a refused id exits non-zero
  ([#​6740](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6740), [#​6771](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6771)). A piped `bd query` is no longer silently capped at 50 rows ([#​6744](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6744)). `bd sql` no
  longer drops the rows of CTE queries or `CALL` result sets ([#​6932](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6932)).

#### Upgrading Notes

- **No migration, but behaviour changes.** The list below is everything in this release that can
  change what a script sees. Each item is described in full under **Changed** or **Fixed**.
- **`bd show --watch <id>` exits 1 when the id cannot be found**, on both the direct and proxied
  routes. It used to exit 0 ([#​6933](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6933)).
- **`bd sql` output changed in two places** ([#​6932](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6932)). In direct server mode, a multi-statement write,
  or a write the parser cannot classify, now prints `OK` / `{"status":"ok"}` instead of `OK, N rows
  affected` / `{"rows_affected":N}`. Proxied mode already did this. `bd sql --readonly` now refuses a
  statement it cannot parse (for example `PRAGMA`) instead of running it as a read.
- **A failure to read the custom issue types is now an error** ([#​6934](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6934)). `bd types`, `bd create --graph` and `bd config set storage-class.*` fail instead of continuing as if there were no custom
  types.
- **`BEADS_DIR` must point at the `.beads` directory itself** ([#​6938](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6938)). A `BEADS_DIR` that names a
  project root (`BEADS_DIR=$repo` instead of `BEADS_DIR=$repo/.beads`), or a `.beads` that does not
  exist yet, used to work by accident because discovery walked up to the nearest workspace. It now
  fails with "no beads database found". Fix the variable; behaviour with `BEADS_DIR` unset is
  unchanged.
- **`bd purge` always keeps closed beads that a live bead depends on** ([#​6883](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6883)). This covers
  `parent-child`, `tracks` and `blocks` edges, and there is no flag to turn it off. The held-back
  count is reported as `live_dependent_skipped`. `bd prune` does not apply this protection.
- **`--older-than` on `bd purge` and `bd prune` is exact at hour precision** ([#​6883](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6883)). `12h` used to
  round up to one day and now means 12 hours, so **`bd prune --older-than 12h` deletes rows closed
  12–24 hours ago that it used to keep**. `36h` used to floor to one day and now means 36 hours. Day
  values (`7`, `7d`, `2w`) are unchanged.
- **`bd close` with several ids exits non-zero when any of them fails to close** ([#​6740](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6740), [#​6771](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6771)). The
  ids that can close still close, and a final `Error: N of M issues failed to close` line is added.
  An id that was already closed still counts as success.
- **An unflagged piped `bd query` is no longer capped at 50 rows** ([#​6744](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6744)). It follows `bd list`'s
  policy: an explicit `--limit` wins, piped stdout is unlimited, agent mode on a terminal gets 20,
  and a terminal gets 50. Pass `--limit` if a pipeline relied on the cap.
- **On a proxied workspace with `dolt.auto-commit` set to `batch` or `off`, writes stop being
  committed to Dolt history one at a time** ([#​6499](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6499)). The setting used to be ignored there. Changes
  now accumulate in the server's working set until `bd dolt commit`, and `dolt log`, `dolt push` and
  backups do not see them before that. The default, `on`, is unchanged.
- **`bd dolt status --json` has a new shape on a proxied workspace** ([#​6580](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6580)). The always-false
  `{"running": false, "pid": 0, "port": 0}` is replaced by `running` (now describing the proxy) plus
  `proxy_*` and `backend_*` fields. `pid` and `port` are gone. This is the rc.1 change most likely to
  break a parser. Other topologies keep their output.
- **`bd config set <dotted.key>` writes a nested mapping** ([#​6578](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6578)). Where `.beads/config.yaml`
  already had the flat spelling (a top-level `dolt.host: ...`), that entry is removed and re-written
  under `dolt:`. Two writes that used to exit 0 without a visible effect now exit 1: setting a dotted
  key under a parent that holds a scalar, and setting one in a file whose top level is not a mapping.
  If another tool writes flat dotted keys to the same file, check for a duplicated key after `bd
  config set` ([#​6594](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6594), open).
- **`bd ready` and `bd list --ready` grow for workspaces with custom `active`-category statuses**
  ([#​5918](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5918)). Those issues were always meant to be ready work and now appear. Counts and dashboards will
  read higher.
- **`bd list --wisp-type <t>` without `--include-ephemeral` is now refused** instead of printing an
  empty listing for every input ([#​6098](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6098)).
- **Opening a store against an unreachable Dolt server now waits before failing**, up to about 40s
  per open ([#​6003](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6003)). This applies only to proxied-server workspaces and to `bd serve`. Embedded
  workspaces, and ordinary CLI commands in a server-mode workspace, are unaffected. Bad credentials,
  an unknown database and an unresolvable hostname still fail immediately.
- **`bd backup sync` fails after 5 seconds if another backup of the same workspace is running**,
  rather than overlapping with it. A backup sync that would leave the manifest ahead of its chunk
  files now fails at that point instead of corrupting the backup quietly ([#​5931](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5931)). A backup already in
  that state is not repaired by upgrading and has to be re-seeded.
- **`bd doctor` warns about a missing `.beads/dolt-server-config.yaml` gitignore pattern** on every
  workspace created before this release ([#​5978](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5978)). Run `bd doctor --fix` once to add it.

#### Added

- **The `bd backup` family on a proxied-server workspace bd runs the Dolt server for** ([#​6584](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6584),
  [#​6694](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6694)). `init`, `sync`, `remove`, `status` and `restore` are routed over the proxied provider.
  `bd backup restore` stops the proxy and its Dolt child before replacing the database, so the next
  command relaunches against the restored data. On a proxied workspace pointed at an external host,
  socket, or team-server database, the family is still refused with code
  `proxy.backup.unsupported`, now carrying `"reason": "design"`. `CALL DOLT_BACKUP('add', …)` would
  register the remote on the server for every client, and a `file://` destination would resolve on
  the server's filesystem.
- **Opt-in auto-backup on a managed-local proxied workspace** ([#​6879](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6879)). With `backup.enabled=true` (or
  `BD_BACKUP_ENABLED=1`) the post-command hook takes the same change-detected Dolt-native backup into
  `.beads/backup` that it takes in direct mode. It is off by default, as on every server-mode
  workspace. It does nothing on an external or team-server topology, under strict `--readonly`,
  `bd serve`, `--dry-run`/`--inspect`, or a migration freeze. `bd backup status` now reports `auto:
  off in proxied-server mode; set backup.enabled=true to opt in` instead of blaming a missing git
  remote. A per-workspace `.beads/backup.lock` stops auto-backup and `bd backup sync` from running
  at the same time.
- **`bd purge --wisps-plane`, `--limit`, and hour-precision `--older-than`** ([#​6883](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6883)).
  `--wisps-plane` selects every closed row in the wisps table, including `--no-history` beads. It
  works on embedded, server and proxied workspaces, and requires `--older-than` or `--pattern`.
  `--limit N` caps one run at N beads, oldest-closed first. With `--json` the output then adds
  `remaining` and `has_more`; loop while `has_more` is true. `--older-than` accepts `36h`, `168h`,
  `90m`, and values down to `1s`. A value too large to represent (for example `213504d`) is refused
  instead of wrapping to a tiny age.
- **`bd list --include-ephemeral`** ([#​6098](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6098)). This is the flag `--wisp-type` needs to reach any rows.
  `bd list --include-ephemeral --wisp-type heartbeat` is the working form. It is off by default, so
  the default listing is unchanged.
- **`bd types` lists system types** ([#​6934](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6934)). A new "System types" section shows `message`,
  `molecule`, `gate` and `event`, and `bd types --json` gains an additive `system_types` field.

#### Changed

- **Proxied-server refusals carry a `reason`** ([#​6582](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6582)). The JSON a refused command prints gains
  `reason: design` (expected to stay: shared history, multi-repo routing, destructive admin, strict
  `--readonly`) or `reason: unimplemented` (a gap with a named owner). Codes, messages and exit
  statuses are unchanged. A command with no proxied route now fails with the typed
  `proxy.store.unrouted` instead of an internal string.
- **`bd backup restore --json` prints `{"restored": true, "source": "<dir>"}` on every topology**,
  where it used to print nothing. On failure, `bd backup init`/`sync`/`remove`/`restore` now print a
  single error line instead of the error followed by the full usage text. Exit statuses are
  unchanged.
- **`dolt.auto-commit=batch`/`off` take effect on a proxied workspace, and `bd dolt commit` works
  there** ([#​6499](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6499), [#​4995](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/4995)). Commands that are explicit commit points (`bd batch`, `bd mol
  bond`/`pour`/`squash`, `bd mol wisp create`, the wisp half of `bd mol burn`) still commit, and
  `bd serve` writes still commit per write. `bd vc commit`'s proxied refusal now points at `bd dolt
  commit`.
- **`bd purge` keeps closed beads a live bead depends on, and `--older-than` is exact** ([#​6883](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6883)). See
  Upgrading Notes.
- **`bd ready` / `bd list --ready` include custom `active`-category statuses** ([#​5918](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5918), [#​5831](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5831)). Custom
  `wip`/`done`/`frozen`/unspecified statuses and `in_progress` stay out. The `--ready` footer and
  help text still describe the default as open-only, which now understates the set ([#​6187](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6187), [#​6188](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6188),
  open).
- **The `--ready` footer names the status selector that applied** ([#​5924](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5924)). With an explicit
  `--status` it now reads `<selector> only`.
- **Store opens retry transient connection failures for up to 30s** ([#​6003](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6003)), with each attempt
  capped at 10s, so about 40s is the realistic worst case for one open. A provider open pings twice,
  so a narrow ordering can reach about 80s. Only proxied-server workspaces and `bd serve` take this
  path.
- **The Dolt bump rejects a backup manifest update that references a missing table file** ([#​5931](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5931),
  [#​4070](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/4070)). This catches the corruption when it happens instead of at some later sync. It is a
  mitigation: backup publish is still not atomic.
- **`bd dolt status --json` reports the proxy and its backend separately on a proxied workspace**
  ([#​6580](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6580)), and **`bd config set` writes dotted keys nested** ([#​6578](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6578)). See Upgrading Notes.

#### Fixed

- **An explicit `BEADS_DIR` is authoritative during workspace discovery** ([#​6938](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6938)). A `BEADS_DIR`
  naming a directory with no project files used to be ignored. Discovery then walked up from the
  current directory and rebound to the parent workspace, so `bd init` refused with "already
  initialized" and `bd create`/`bd list` used the parent's store. `bd init` now initializes the named
  directory, and `bd import`, `bd setup` and `bd bootstrap` target it.
- **Concurrent unblocking no longer leaves a dependent stuck as blocked** ([#​6716](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6716); [#​6719](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6719), [#​6942](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6942)).
  Covered: the Dolt store write transactions; every proxied-server write route (`bd close` single
  and batch, `bd update --status`, `bd dep remove`, `bd delete`, `bd batch`, `bd serve`);
  `RunInTransaction` (`bd batch` direct, `bd cook`, `bd mol squash`/`burn`, SDK callers); the wisp
  writers; and the legacy dependency removal behind `bd duplicates --merge`.
- **`bd close` reports a partial batch failure** ([#​6648](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6648); [#​6740](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6740), [#​6771](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6771)). In `--json` mode the summary
  is a compact JSON line on stderr naming the failed ids, matching `bd update`, and each `failed[]`
  entry carries the same refusal text on both routes. `--claim-next` still claims when part of the
  batch closed, and the summary names the claimed id.
- **`bd sql` classifies statements with the Dolt SQL parser** ([#​6932](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6932)). In proxied mode, `WITH ...
  SELECT` and `WITH RECURSIVE` queries were misread as writes and printed `OK, 0 rows affected`; they
  now return their rows. Statements that may both write and return rows (`CALL`, `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`
  of a write, `RETURNING`) are committed and their rows printed, so `CALL DOLT_BRANCH(...)`-style
  result sets are no longer discarded.
- **`bd query` applies `bd list`'s piped-output limit policy** ([#​6229](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6229), [#​6744](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6744)).
- **`bd show --watch` works under `--proxied-server`** ([#​6933](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6933)). It was refused with
  `proxy.watch.unsupported`. It now shares the direct route's loop: re-read every 2s, redraw on a
  status or `updated_at` change, stop cleanly on Ctrl+C/SIGTERM. Each poll uses its own short unit
  of work, so a long watch does not hold a transaction open.
- **A proxy retires when its Dolt backend exits cleanly** ([#​6937](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6937)). It used to notice only a non-zero
  exit. A gracefully stopped backend left the proxy adoptable in front of a dead store, and with
  `--proxied-server-idle-timeout 0` that never cleared. `bd dolt status` now reports such a proxy as
  "not serving" (`running: false`, with `proxy_pid` still set), including one started by an older bd.
- **`bd dolt start` is refused on a proxied workspace** with `proxy.dolt_start.conflict` ([#​6580](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6580)).
  It used to launch an unsupervised sql-server over the proxy's data directory or adopt the proxy's
  own Dolt child, which was a v1.3.0 known issue. **`bd dolt status` now reads the proxy's own
  records** instead of a PID file proxied mode never writes, so it no longer says "not running" while
  the proxy is serving.
- **The smart migrate gate stops a data-behind clone instead of auto-migrating it** ([#​6575](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6575); [#​6659](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6659),
  [#​6695](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6695)). A clone that has commits left to pull, whether or not it also has its own, is told to
  run `bd dolt pull` first, and is told when that pull will merge rather than fast-forward. `bd dolt
  pull` opens leniently for this one refusal, which changes the v1.3.0 upgrade note that said the
  gate refuses `bd dolt pull` too. Commands that keep working (`bd list`, `bd ready`, `bd show`,
  `bd dolt commit`) print the pull-first guidance instead of the migrate-or-adopt bullets. `--json`
  callers get a single `pull-first` option and a `data_behind_shape` of `fast-forward` or
  `diverged`. For a fast-forward on a non-shared store, `human_decision_required` is `false`. On a
  shared server the guidance names `bd migrate schema --force` as the consent step. A proxied
  workspace reaches the same stop, with the guidance naming the host the pull has to run on
  (`pull-first-on-server-host`). `BD_SMART_GATE=0`, `bd migrate --force` and
  `BD_ALLOW_REMOTE_MIGRATE=1` behave as before.
- **A clone missing its local `events`, `bd_events_journal` or `bd_events_seq` table recreates it on
  open** ([#​6547](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6547)). These dolt-ignored tables could be absent on a clone that was otherwise at the
  latest schema, and bd never created them. That was the write-dead store listed under v1.3.0's known
  issues ([#​6142](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6142)). The migration runner now replays the creating migrations from each table's own
  floor.
- **Deleting or purging a wisp removes its dependent rows on stores without the wisp foreign keys**
  ([#​6487](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6487); [#​6563](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6563), [#​6627](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6627)). Wisp deletes (including `bd purge`, `bd mol burn` and wisp GC) left
  `wisp_dependencies` edges and `wisp_labels`, `wisp_events`, `wisp_comments` and
  `wisp_child_counters` rows behind. This is a forward fix: orphans already in a store are not
  cleaned up.
- **A server-mode workspace with an empty `.beads/dolt` is no longer refused as legacy** ([#​5682](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5682),
  [#​6935](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6935)). When the gitignored `.local_version` witness was missing, every command, including
  `bd init`, was refused and nothing could repair it. An empty root is now admitted and the witness
  written. A pre-1.0 witness, or a non-empty `.beads/dolt`, is still refused.
- **`bd types` lists exactly the types `bd create --type` accepts** ([#​6934](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6934)). Server mode dropped
  `config.yaml` custom types once the database had any, and proxied `bd config set storage-class.*`
  ignored types registered in the database. Every mode now uses one rule.
- **A dotted config key round-trips** ([#​6578](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6578)). `bd config set sync.remote` wrote a top-level key
  whose name contained the dot, which `bd config get` found and bd's direct reader did not, so `bd
  init --remote` recorded a remote that was then not found. `bd config unset` now removes the nested
  form too.
- **`bd list --status <s> --ready` honors `--status`** ([#​5832](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5832), [#​5924](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5924)). It used to drop it and return
  the unfiltered ready set.
- **`bd gate check` resolves bead gates whose target lives in a prefix-routed rig** ([#​5859](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5859)), reading
  the owning store through `routes.jsonl` without writing to it.
- **Smaller fixes.** `bd doctor` and the gitignore template cover the generated
  `.beads/dolt-server-config.yaml`, which holds a per-machine port and path ([#​5978](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5978)). The
  missing-prefix error points at `bd init --prefix` / `bd bootstrap` instead of a `config.yaml` key
  that has no effect ([#​5916](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5916), [#​5936](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5936)). `bd create --file` says it creates one issue per `##` heading
  and suggests `--body-file` ([#​5921](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5921)). The list truncation hint no longer leaves a padded blank line
  under the prompt ([#​5685](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5685), [#​5927](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5927)). `bd setup claude` and `bd init` stop rewriting
  `.claude/settings.json` when nothing changed ([#​5693](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5693), [#​5944](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5944)).

### [`v1.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#130---2026-09-15)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/compare/v1.2.2-rc.1...v1.3.0-rc.2)

The first tested release off `main` since the 1.1 line. \[1.2.2] was a recovery
release that re-shipped the v1.1.2 code under a higher version number, so a
v1.2.2 user is running 1.1-era code and meets **everything** below at once:
the changes listed here, plus the \[1.2.1] changes that release deliberately
withheld. Read the upgrade notes before installing.

##### Upgrade notes

**On an embedded or local store, the first invocation migrates your schema, in
place, from v53 to v66.** A v1.2.2 (or any 1.1.x) database sits at main-series
schema v53; this binary knows v66, so the first command that opens the store
applies 13 main-series migrations, `0054_add_lease_columns` through
`0066_add_events_journal_actor`. Two of those passes rewrite rows rather than
just reshaping tables — the aux-row id rekey and the `events` dolt\_ignore flip
described under **Changed** — so on a large store the first invocation is
*noticeably* slower than the ones after it. It is crash-resumable and picks up
where it left off, but do not interrupt it if you can avoid it.

**A shared Dolt sql-server is never auto-migrated** ([#​5920](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5920), [#​6048](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/6048)): migrating it
promotes the schema for every client at once, so it waits for explicit consent
via `bd migrate schema`. Remote-backed stores keep their existing
designated-migrator gate. Upgrade all of that server's clients *first* — see
[Shared servers](https://beads.gascity.com/getting-started/upgrading#shared-servers).

**The counter restarts partway through, and that is not a loop.** The
clone-local (dolt\_ignored) series runs after the main one, through the same
printer and its own numbering, and it moves 0011 → 0026 on this upgrade. So the
run is about **28 migrations**, not 13, and what you see on stderr is 13 lines
counting up to 0066 followed by 15 lines starting again at 0012:

```
Applying migration 0065: widen_wisp_comments_text…
Applying migration 0066: add_events_journal_actor…
Applying migration 0012: create_leases…      ← clone-local series, not a restart
```

A counter that jumps backwards is the signature operators kill runs over. Let
it finish.

Progress prints only when stderr is a terminal. Piped and CI runs see nothing
at all, which is deliberate — a silent-looking CI upgrade is not a stuck one.

**Back up first, with the binary you have now.** Take the backup *before* you
install 1.3.0. Under the new binary `bd export` triggers the auto-migration
before it exports, so a snapshot taken afterwards is a post-migration snapshot
and cannot protect you against the migration going wrong. On a remote-backed
store, finish syncing with the old binary too: once 1.3.0 is installed the
pending-migration gate refuses `bd dolt push` and `bd dolt pull` as well, not
just `bd migrate`.

```bash

# with your CURRENT bd, before installing 1.3.0:
bd dolt push                                                   # remote-backed stores only
bd export --all -o .beads/backup/pre-1.3.0-$(date +%Y%m%d).jsonl
```

A JSONL export is cheap, issue-complete, and importable by any bd version. If
you want a Dolt-native snapshot that keeps history and config, configure a
destination and sync it — **bare `bd backup` takes no backup**, it is a command
group that prints help and exits 0:

```bash
bd backup init <path-or-dolthub-url>   # once, to configure a destination
bd backup sync                         # take the snapshot
```

**Upgrade every client that shares a store, together.** The forward schema-skew
guard means an older co-resident binary — a second `bd` earlier in `PATH`, a
long-running `bd serve`, another clone's cron job — refuses a database migrated
past what it knows, rather than proceeding blind. That is the guard working, not
a bug, but it makes a mixed-version fleet a broken fleet: one machine running
1.3.0 takes the whole store forward and every 1.2.2 client stops. Run
`which -a bd` after installing, and on a remote-backed store follow the existing
designated-migrator procedure (one clone migrates and pushes; the rest pull or
re-clone). See
[Upgrading](https://beads.gascity.com/getting-started/upgrading) for the
per-install-method recipes and the multi-clone flow.

**If you need to go back**, the rollback is a schema-cursor rollback, not a
downgrade of the data: the procedure is written up in the
[recovery runbook](https://beads.gascity.com/recovery/accidental-1-2-1-release)
(repo copy: `docs/recovery/accidental-1-2-1-release.md`). Its worked example is
the v53↔v65 case from the accidental 1.2.1 release; the steps are the same for
v66, with the version numbers adjusted.

##### Breaking changes for v1.2.2 users

**This is a highlights list, not the complete set.** A v1.2.2 user is crossing
two releases at once, and the breaks below are the ones most likely to stop a
script or a service. The full set is the `[1.2.1]` section further down plus the
**Changed** section here — read `[1.2.1]` in full before upgrading, since
\[1.2.2] withheld it and v1.2.1 itself was pulled, so nobody on the supported
line has seen it.

After upgrading, `bd upgrade review` prints exactly the entries between the
version you were running and this one. (Prefer it to `bd info --whats-new`,
which dumps the entire release history.)

**Carried from \[1.2.1] — never shipped to v1.2.2 users:**

- **`bd update --status <done-status>` now enforces close policy.** Moving an
  issue to `closed` (or any configured done-category status) via `bd update`,
  `bd batch update`, or the issueops facade refuses when the issue has open
  children or a live direct blocker, matching `bd close`. Override with
  `bd update --force` (`update <id> status=closed force=true` in `bd batch`;
  `UpdateRequest.ForceClosePolicy` for facade consumers). An unforced refusal
  rolls back the entire batch.
- **`bd search` includes closed issues by default** (bd-t5yex). The dominant
  query is "was this already found/filed/fixed?", where excluding closed issues
  produced a false "no". Narrow with `--status open` to get the old behavior.
  `bd list` keeps its open-only default.
- **The no-ID "last touched issue" fallback on `bd update` / `bd close` is
  interactive-only** (bd-m00pb,
  [#​4839](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4839)). A scripted
  `bd update $ID …` with an empty `$ID` now refuses in argument validation
  instead of mutating whatever was touched last. The fallback requires a
  terminal stdin; `BD_NON_INTERACTIVE=1` and `CI=1/true` also disable it. Set
  `BD_LAST_TOUCHED_FALLBACK=1` if a script genuinely relied on it.
- **`bd human list` hides done/frozen and pinned beads by default, and
  validates `--status`** ([#​5332](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5332)). It previously passed `--status` through
  unvalidated and showed closed beads. A `--status` typo is now an error rather
  than an empty list. Every bead *type* still shows.
- **`bd dolt push` and `bd sync` no longer adopt a git-origin-derived Dolt
  remote without consent** ([#​5068](https://redirect.github.com/gastownhall/beads/issues/5068)). Both used to silently derive a remote from
  `git remote get-url origin`, persist `sync.remote`, commit that config change
  under your git identity, and upload the full issue history — which published
  a whole issue database to a public origin on a command the user believed
  targeted an already-configured remote. Adoption now prompts (defaulting to
  no) and fails closed non-interactively. `--yes`/`-y` consents ahead of time.
- **`bd --readonly serve` is refused instead of binding a server that cannot do
  what it advertises.** On a Dolt SQL-server workspace the flag was previously a
  silent no-op and the server came up fully writable, so anything scripted as a
  "safe" read-only server **does not start after this upgrade** — drop the flag.
  Worth checking before you restart a long-running `bd serve` as part of the
  fleet upgrade above.
- **`bd config list` and `GET /v0/beads/config` no longer enumerate the `kv.`
  plane**, which is where `bd remember` memories live. That closed an
  unauthenticated `GET /v0/beads/config` handing out every stored memory. A
  script that read memories out of `bd config list` now gets empty output rather
  than an error; use `bd kv` / `bd remember` instead.
- **The published `backend` package drops orphan handling** (bd-gwryr).
  `backend.OrphanHandling` and its four constants, the `storage` originals they
  aliased, `BatchCreateOptions.OrphanHandling`

title: fix(domain): counter mint skips held ids and advances past a lagging run (supersedes #6845)
body:
Supersedes #6845 by @quad341, with credit.

## Summary

In proxied-server mode, and for `bd serve` creates in any server-backed mode (the domain create path), a top-level counter mint could hand out an ID that a row already holds. The counter walk probed only tombstones, and explicit creates and imports never move the counter. The upsert writer then overwrote that issue, or wrote a twin of a wisp's ID in the other plane. A create-only caller got `ErrAlreadyExists` instead. This PR:

- **Probes `Taken` in the counter walk.** `Taken` covers live rows of both planes and both tombstone tables. On the first held candidate, the walk advances the counter once past the highest held top-level numeric ID (`AdvanceCounterPastHeldIDs`). A held run longer than the walk's 1000-value bound is therefore crossed in one step. A bounded walk would fail every retry on such a run, because the failed transaction rolls its progress back.
- **Inserts every minted top-level ID create-only.** This covers counter and hash IDs, issues and wisps, through the existing coordination-cell guard and strict writer. If another writer takes the ID between the mint's probe and the insert, the minting attempt is refused or conflicts at commit instead of overwriting (a replay of that conflict is covered under Limitations).
- **Checks assignee and owner length before either insert branch,** so the create-only branch returns the typed `ErrFieldTooLong` before it writes anything.

The report's hash-minter cross-plane claim is already fixed on main: `mintTopLevelID` probes `Taken`. The CLI's own creates in server and embedded mode (`issueops`) are unchanged here, and so are `bd import` rows that name no ID in proxied-server mode: the unit-of-work importer mints them through `issueops`.

## Decision needed before merge: one counter rule for both engines

**Reviewer direction, 2026-11-14:** bee-ghosttrack, approving #8466 at `cb5783631e` ([review](https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/8466#pullrequestreview-5900102160)), asked to land #8466 first and for this PR's rebase to drop its jump (or adopt #8466's end-of-run semantics) rather than carry both rules. On that path this PR must not merge before #8466. Once #8466 is on main, this PR rebases down to AC-3 and AC-4 plus their tests, as the first landing order below describes. The rest of this section is the comparison that direction settles, unless a maintainer overrides it.

#8466 (for #8456) changes the same counter mint with a different rule, in both the domain and the `issueops` mint. At its published head `cb5783631e`, it walks held values one probe at a time. Past 1000 of them it reads every held ID once (`AdvanceCounterPastHeldIDsTx`, which the domain reaches through `IssueSQLRepository.AdvanceCounterPastHeld`) and moves the counter to the first free number. It also deletes `Retired`, `IDRetiredInTx` and `idRetiredSQL`. Both PRs now cross a held run of any length, so the choice left is dense numbering against the jump.

`git merge-tree` of this PR's head and `cb5783631e` reports conflicts in four files: `docs/reference/configuration.md`, `internal/storage/domain/db/issue.go`, `internal/storage/domain/issue.go` and `internal/storage/domain/issue_counter_retired_test.go` (`CHANGELOG.md` too with the unpushed fixup under Known gaps). Both PRs add a scan of the same four tables under nearly the same method name, with different targets, and their docs bullets contradict each other. The two rules number a lagging counter differently:

| Counter at 1, held IDs | This PR (jump) | #8466 (first free) |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 3 | 3 |
| 2 and 4 | 5 | 3 |
| 2 through 1102 | 1103 | 1103 |
| 2 and 90000 | 90001 | 3 |
| 2 and 2147483000 | 2147483001, and every mint fails once the counter reaches the `INT` maximum, about 650 mints later | 3 |

Each PR's tests pin its own rule. This PR's AC-1 tests (held 2 and 4, want 5) fail under first free, and #8466's held-run store tests fail under a max+1 jump, per its body. By trace, #8466's `CounterModePassesOverLiveIDs` and this PR's AC-2 test pass under both rules, because their held IDs are contiguous with the counter.

The two rules:

- **The jump (this PR).** quad341's #6845 and #6754, the oldest open PRs on this bug, use it. It matches how the counter already seeds itself from the highest existing numeric ID, and how `NextChildID` takes the highest used child suffix. The first held value costs one probe and one scan. The cost: one far-ahead held ID moves the counter there for good, so numbering is no longer dense, and a held ID just below the `INT` maximum leaves the prefix a few hundred mints from failing every mint. At this PR's head a held ID above the `INT` maximum is worse: the first advance fails, and so does every later counter mint for the prefix (see Known gaps).
- **First free (#8466).** It keeps numbering dense and has no `INT`-ceiling edge. A held run longer than 1000 costs up to 1001 probes before the one-read skip (#8466 measured such a walk at about 4 s on an embedded store); later creates start past the run.

Whichever rule wins, AC-3 and AC-4 and their tests overlap no #8466 hunk:

- If #8466 lands first, this PR rebases down to AC-3 and AC-4 plus their tests. It drops `AdvanceCounterPastHeldIDs`, its tests and the docs bullet, and carries the credit and the create-only text of the unpushed fixup (see Known gaps).
- If this PR lands first, #8466 rebases its domain half onto the jump or replaces it deliberately, and its `issueops` half follows the same rule, so the two engines never number a lagging counter differently for the same database.
- AC-3 must not land alone on base. Base's walk hands out a held candidate, so forcing create-only there would turn the silent overwrite into an `ErrAlreadyExists` on every `bd q` and `bd todo add`: the rollback undoes the counter bump, so each retry meets the same ID.

## Related work

- **#6845 (quad341)** is the PR this supersedes. It has the same design: the counter jumps past held IDs, minted IDs insert create-only, and the length guards move ahead of both branches. The pipeline built its own implementation, because #6845 put the jump inside `NextCounterID`, which the design rejected. The create-only field-length tests keep #6845's `bd-fl-co-*` shape. No commit on this PR's head carries `Co-authored-by: Jim Wordelman <jim@wordelman.name>` yet; the unpushed maintainer fixup does (see Known gaps).
- **#6754 (quad341)** is the same fix for the server and embedded `issueops` path, also a jump. Still open.
- **#8466** is the first-free rule described above, for #8456 (the same overwrite on the classic Dolt create path). Still open; its CHANGELOG entry covers both engines.
- **#8218** restarts creates and imports from the request when a commit conflict is replayed, which closes the replay gap under Limitations. **#8454** does the same for the classic Dolt create path (it supersedes #6831).

## Limitations

- **Commit-conflict replay (pre-existing).** `bd q`, `bd todo add` and tracker pulls that assign no ID of their own, such as `bd jira sync`, build their `*types.Issue` outside the transaction closure that a commit conflict replays, and `create()` writes the minted ID into it. Suppose a concurrent create of the same number wins, and this one loses with a 1213 serialization failure at commit. The replay then sends that ID back as a named one, and the upsert writer overwrites the winner's row. This PR's guarantees cover the attempt that mints the ID; #8218 re-mints on replay. `bd create` clones its parameters per attempt and `bd batch` builds its issues inside the closure, so neither is affected. With AC-3 the minting attempt of those three callers also loses commit races to writers that coordinate a different ID in the same shard, such as a retaining sweep or another create-only insert (probed on a Dolt server: Error 1213). The replay then commits the minted number as a named ID and leaves the counter one behind, so the next ordinary mint jumps past the highest held numeric ID: with `rp-90000` held, a replayed `rp-3` made the next mint `rp-90001`. Under #8466's first-free rule the same replay costs one number.
- **Counter seeding (pre-existing).** `seedCounterFromExisting` and `issueops.SeedCounterFromExistingIssuesTx` still parse ID suffixes with no upper bound. A `<prefix>-3000000000` row in `issues` therefore makes the first counter mint for that prefix fail with Dolt's "Out of range" error, in both engines. This PR does not change seeding, and at this PR's head the new advance does not ignore such suffixes either (see Known gaps).
- **The CLI in server and embedded mode**, and `bd import` rows that name no ID in proxied-server mode, can still get a number that a live row holds (#6754, #8466). Until one of them lands, a server-mode workspace numbers a lagging counter two ways: `bd serve` creates jump past held IDs, while the CLI's own creates meet them.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Criterion | glm | opus | pr |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | Given an initialized counter last at `P-1` and explicit live holders at `P-2` and `P-4` across the issues and wisps planes, when the domain use case mints a top-level issue without CreateOnly, then it creates `P-5`, preserves both original holders, and creates no duplicate ID across planes. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-2 | Given an initialized counter followed by more than 1000 consecutive held numeric IDs, when the domain use case mints a top-level issue, then it succeeds beyond the highest held suffix without exhausting the skip bound or changing any held row. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-3 | Given a top-level domain create with no supplied ID and CreateOnly unset, when it mints in any supported mode and plane, then insertion uses the existing strict-create guard and writer, evidenced by a changed create-coordination cell rather than an unguarded upsert. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-4 | Given an assignee or owner longer than 255 characters, when the domain repository inserts with CreateOnly, whether caller-selected or forced by minting, then it returns an error matching types.ErrFieldTooLong before writing the issue or its coordination cell. | pass | pass | - |
| AC-5 | Given an existing explicit ID and CreateOnly unset, when the domain use case creates that explicit ID again with a changed title, then the existing upsert behavior succeeds and the title changes; caller-selected CreateOnly still refuses an occupied ID. | pass | pass | - |

## How this was built

- Design: `design.pair` (anthropic-opus, moonshot-kimi, xai-grok, zhipu-glm).
- Independent candidates: glm (pass), opus (pass), pr (fail). The pr result means no test ran: the triage repro did not build on #6845's older base (the linker exited with status 2).
- Judge (grok) composed the change per AC: AC-1 ← opus, AC-2 ← opus, AC-3 ← opus, AC-4 ← opus, AC-5 ← opus.
- Canonical tests (pipeline head `931bd8991a`): `bazel-test //internal/storage/domain:domain_test --test_filter='^TestCounterModeMint' && bazel-test //internal/storage/domain/db:db_test --test_filter='^TestDomainDB$/^(TestIssueUseCase_MintTopLevelID|TestFieldLengthGuards|TestIssueSQLRepository)$' --test_env=BEADS_TEST_SKIP= --test_env=BEADS_TEST_DOLT_SERVER=local --test_env=BEADS_TEST_REQUIRE_DOLT_CONTAINER=1` → pass.
- Final review (kimi): pass.

Judge rationale: Both candidates implement the same production behaviour (mintedTopLevel forces CreateOnly; nextUnretiredCounterID probes Taken and calls AdvanceCounterPastHeldIDs once on the first held value; UNION ALL scan of issues/wisps/both tombstone tables with literal CutPrefix filter and GREATEST upsert; length guards hoisted ahead of both Insert branches) and both pass the independent run. Opus's triage-repro 'fail' is a patch-apply artifact (repro patch conflicted at the end of issue_usecase_test.go: 'expected declaration, found <<'), not a behaviour failure; its own AC-1 tests cover the same scenario. AC-1 opus: the use-case test covers three plane layouts (both issues, both wisps, across planes), asserts the counter really lags at 1 before minting (a design test-plan requirement glm omits), and asserts the exact per-plane occupancy map; its LIKE pattern is escaped and the repo test covers both _ and %; its docs line is correctly scoped to proxied-server mode, whereas glm's docs line claims every generated ID skips explicit IDs, which is false for the unchanged direct/embedded issueops path. Glm also commits a redundant MintCounterLag repro test. AC-2 opus: the held run spans both planes with an explicit lag precondition, and the unit fake keeps a retired/live split plus an advanceTo knob, so TestCounterModeMintAdvancesOnlyOnce proves the single-advance rule (glm has no equivalent). AC-3: equivalent shard-cell value-change evidence; opus is one table-driven test over counter issue, hash issue and hash wisp. AC-4 opus: assignee and owner both assert an unchanged coordination cell and no row, with an at-limit round trip for both fields (glm checks the cell for assignee only). AC-5 opus: table over ExplicitID and prepopulated Issue.ID, each also asserting caller CreateOnly refuses with ErrAlreadyExists and that explicit creates never create the counter row. Contributor PR #6845 puts the jump in NextCounterID (the design rejected this) and re-adds hash cross-plane tests already covered at base, so none of its code is picked; its credit rides the pipeline.

## Known gaps: an unpushed maintainer fixup

The adopt-pr review of this PR made one maintainer commit on top of the pipeline's five, `fix(domain): keep the counter advance inside the INT counter's range` (`f06ea3fada`, written in review iteration 1 and amended in iterations 2 and 3). The review loop ended without approving a head, because of the counter-rule direction above, so the fixup was never pushed. This PR's head has these gaps, which the fixup closes:

- **INT range.** `AdvanceCounterPastHeldIDs` parses every held suffix with `strconv.Atoi` and no bound, but `issue_counter.last_id` is a signed 32-bit `INT`. With a held `<prefix>-3000000000`, live or retired, the advance fails with Dolt error 1264 ("Out of range value for column 'last_id'") once the walk meets a held value, and every later counter mint for the prefix fails the same way. A held `<prefix>-2147483647` pins the counter at its maximum. The fixup ignores suffixes of 2147483647 or more, in the store and in the unit fake; its `IgnoresChildHashAndForeignIDs` case fails with error 1264 when the advance is mutated back to this head's parse.
- **Docs scope.** The docs bullet says that in proxied-server mode an auto-generated ID never reuses a held number. The fixup scopes it by route (every mode skips retired values; creates in proxied-server mode, except `bd import` rows that name no ID, and `bd serve` creates in any server-backed mode also skip held ones), limits it to the attempt that mints the ID, says retired IDs count toward the jump target, and states the `INT` bound.
- **CHANGELOG.** This head has no entry. The fixup adds a `### Fixed` entry under `[Unreleased]`: the proxied-server commands that overwrote, twinned or refused a held ID on base, how the jump changes numbering, `bd history <id>` to check for an overwrite, and the replay limits above.
- **Comments.** The fixup's `create()` comment names the replay-exposed callers and the cost this PR accepts (one coordination-cell write and one probe per minted create, and more commit-conflict retries under concurrent mints). Its `ExplicitID` comment replaces the #7931 rationale that this PR reverses.
- **Credit.** The fixup carries `Co-authored-by: Jim Wordelman <jim@wordelman.name>` for #6845.

On the fixup head, `//internal/storage/domain:domain_test` and `//internal/storage/domain/db:db_test` with the Dolt server flags above passed (`TestDomainDB`: 751 tests). If #8466 lands first, the rebase keeps the fixup's comments, its create-only CHANGELOG sentence (as "Every minted top-level ID also inserts create-only") and the credit, and drops the `INT` bound with the advance.

title: Small tasks land in half the plain runner's time: the worker runs before the task, the answer carries only new lines, the verdict is ready when the answer ends
body:
## Problem

On a small task with the model held equal, north lands a change in 12 s at one worker and 15 s at five (2026-11-12, load ladder on the live runtime), against 13 s and 18 s for the plain competitor given the same file text. The task already costs one model request. Where the 12 s goes: the request leaves 2.5 to 4.7 s after the launch command (longer when the control host is busy), the first byte comes 2 to 3 s later, the answer streams for 3.8 s, and the finish call, the private-kind verdict and the landing take about 3 s more. It had been taken as given that a harness cannot be far ahead here, because the model's answer is most of the time. That is only true while the harness waits for the task before it starts anything, makes the model repeat text the lane already holds, and starts judging after the answer has ended.

## Decision (coordinator, 2026-11-12, on the owner's direction of that day to keep climbing with unusual ideas)

Treat every second outside the model's own first byte and new lines as the harness's to remove: the worker is running before the task exists, the answer carries only new lines, and the verdict and the check are under way while the answer still streams. Why: it serves the registered bar (north's time at most two thirds of the plain competitor's) on the one workload where the lead is thinnest. Alternative, not taken: accept parity on small tasks and show the lead only on large tasks and on safety, which leaves the most common kind of work undecided.

Class: the harness starts its own work only after the model has finished, and makes the model wait for work the harness could have done before the task arrived
Category: feature
Spec: measured
Scope: cross-module
Surface: rust
Verify: live-run

## Done when

- [x] Every hand-in records, per lane, the seconds of each part of its call: the wait for a build slot, compile, clippy, tests, each scan and gate by name, and the ticket write; and `north ledger tempo --split` prints the median and p90 of each part over its window, so the largest part is named from records and not inferred (on 2026-11-12 the call could only be split for 49 of 206 lanes, and one stage was counted under another's name). Done when: `north ledger tempo --window 120 --split | rg -o "[0-9]+% of the call median" | awk '{p=$1+0} END{exit !(p>=90 && p<=110)}'` exits 0 on the live runtime (one row per part, medians summing to 90-110% of the call median; reworded 2026-11-13 into a command the checker can judge, bar unchanged). Not before 2026-11-13T00:15Z: e4bb9f0368 went live at 5:12 AM and the 120-minute window must hold only records taken after it (at 5:20 AM it still read 177% from earlier records).
- [x] The finish and hand-in calls waste no turn and no serial second (2026-11-12: 5 of 13 landings in 45 minutes met a refusal first): the checks before queueing run `cargo metadata --locked` so a manifest change without its lock is refused before main, not after (it turned main red twice on 2026-11-12); clippy and the tests run side by side, not one after the other; a hand-in that names only some of the lane's changed paths is completed from the lane's own diff instead of refused; and a lane behind main that rebases without conflict is rebased by the call. Done when: a case shows each of the four, and the finish log's timings line shows clippy and tests overlapping. (landed 931e3a73c87b)
- [x] The each-fact-once change is back on main (reverted as 00c08aebb8 on 2026-11-12 because the secret scan's refusal could arrive after a write under the state directory): re-landed with the refusal ordered ahead of any state write, and `land_enqueue::secrets::enqueue_refuses_a_lane_a_deny_list_or_secret_scan_flags_and_writes_no_ticket` passes on GitHub's Cargo job. Done when: that test is green on a main commit that contains the re-landed change. Landed as cf057a8e67 (Cargo run 43194189535 green) with the deny-list freshness fix-forward 7af1c218f5.
- [x] Two sessions are given the same request anatomy and asked for ranked ideas to cut small-task time further, one on the largest model at its highest effort and one a tier below; this issue lists each session's ideas with expected seconds, and marks which ideas only one of them found, so the staffing record can say whether the larger model earns its place for this kind of question. (verified 2026-11-12 from the three comments named in item 1 of https://github.com/tompassarelli/north/issues/1239#issuecomment-6864663651)
- [x] The second session of the pair above, a tier below the largest model, has posted its own ranked ideas from the same brief without reading the first session's; the comparison in the box above is drawn from both. (verified 2026-11-12, item 1 of https://github.com/tompassarelli/north/issues/1239#issuecomment-6864663651)
- [x] Not before 2026-11-14 (coordinator ruling 2026-11-12: the eight load-ladder readings are folded into this one ladder run, one run on the evals lead's queue on subscription accounts only, because separate runs under load were ruled out): One ladder run at 1, 5 and 21 workers, with fresh verdicts and unseen text, answers every sub-point below. The ladder binary kept under /tmp was removed on 2026-11-12, so the run first rebuilds it from the repository into a state directory under the home and records its rows there, not under /tmp, which lane reclaim trims.
  - A launch takes a worker that is already running: its client process is up with hooks and policy loaded, its prompt's shared part is in the provider's cache, and a lane at current main is ready; the launch hands it the task. On the load ladder the first request leaves within 0.5 s of the launch command at one worker and at five, with the control host's load not in the path. A worker that was started and never used costs nothing but its idle process, and is retired when main's policy changes. (waits:runtime: 781081f41d, not yet in the live runtime, order 29 d21582cf30)
  - The verdict is ready when the answer ends: the commit's prose is the finish call's first field, and the deny-list scan and the private-kind verdict start as soon as it has streamed, keyed by its text, so the finish call finds the verdict instead of waiting for it; nothing is queued on a verdict for other text. On the load ladder the time from the end of the stream to landed is at most 1.2 s with fresh verdicts. (waits:runtime: b5cfd37343, the hand-in keeps the private-kind ask open while its checks run so the verdict rides on the ticket and the lander does not ask again; not yet in the live runtime, order 29 d21582cf30)

Measured 2026-11-12 on an idle lander and a one-file change: median 4 s at one worker and 3 s at five from the finish call to main (runtime fd83e17323), with 1.1 to 4.6 s between hand-in and main at one worker and 1.1 to 7.2 s at five. Verify: live-run (the coordinator's box, after promotion).

The fresh-verdict part of that time is the verdict box above; the owner's question in #1214 about judging on a held copy of the deny-list is answered by the validated-not-fetched box above, which keeps the strict order, so nothing is decided or built on a stale list.
  - The lander's queue wait at 21 workers at once is under 3 s at the median and under 6 s at p95, recorded here from one live run (folded from #1199, 2026-11-12). Measured before: median 11 s, p95 23 s, from the serial verdict asks inside the serve loop; they now run on one thread per lane (194185cc40, with a test of three lanes handed in together). The after-landing run was never the hold.
  - On the load ladder at one worker and at five at once, at least 4 of 5 sessions per level make one model request before their ticket is queued, and every landed change passes the hidden check (folded from #1218, whose code landed: the brief carries the files it names 26d0c41b9f, the finish call carries whole files 7ffee41367 and replacements 3a030a4077). The launch-to-landed medians of that issue (12 s and 13 s) are superseded by the 7 s and 9 s of the last box above.
  - Done when: the worker's instructions name that call as the way to finish (met on fd83e17323: 10 of 10 eval sessions used it), and an accepted call is the session's last model request: over ten load-ladder sessions on the live runtime none makes a request after the call's result, and tokens per landed task are no higher than on the runtime before the call (about 37k). Measured 2026-11-12 on fd83e17323: 6 of 10 sessions made a closing request of about 13,000 tokens after the result, and the one-worker median from launch to landing did not move (20 s before and after), because the turns the call removes come after the landing is queued and were never on that clock; this box's earlier wording (a 6 s fall in that median) is withdrawn for that reason (coordinator, 2026-11-12). (landed d70a6858b1d0)
- [x] One round trip per fact at the finish call's start: the destination fetch, one repository lookup that answers both archived and visibility, and the deny-list validation start side by side at the call's first instant, and the enqueue reads their results and starts none of them again. The landing spans show each fact fetched once per hand-in; the deny list is the one designed exception, read again at the scan's own start so a scan never reads a list older than itself (7af1c218f5), and the test asserts that second read (reworded 2026-11-13 by the issue's lead). (Split from the verdict box on 2026-11-12, after its mechanism became a verdict asked at launch on a commit message the brief proposes, landed ae46d6a550.) (waits:runtime: 817bc55508, not yet in the live runtime, order 29 d21582cf30) (read 2026-11-12 from the lander queue spans: 12 hand-ins on the live runtime each show one fetch, one archived lookup and one scan, https://github.com/tompassarelli/north/issues/1239#issuecomment-6864667574) (Unticked 2026-11-13: ticked 2026-11-12 at 10:52 PM with no runnable check; the brokered checker found the reading cites a commit later reverted, and the box names no command whose output shows each fact fetched once per hand-in.) (landed d312a0ce7a39)
- [x] The lander wakes on a check's exit and on a new ticket instead of on its poll tick, with a slow tick kept behind as a backstop; a case shows a ticket landing with the event dropped. The spans show no wait for a tick on the landing path. (landed 48d8014e91ad)
- [x] A one-shot model ask skips an account that already answered at its limit until its limit resets (folded from #1141): the account that answered last is tried first (landed in 4068cfe1d1), but nothing skips an account found at its limit, so two accounts at their limit ahead of a third in the roster cost about 5.5 s of an 8.3 s ask (2026-11-11). Done when: with two accounts at their limit ahead of a third in the roster, the second of two `north check privacy judge --text FILE` runs on fresh texts starts `claude` once, shown by a test that counts the starts and fails on today's code. (landed 6957dae4839c)

The charge is chosen per check command from the day's records with margin, the usage log records the command and not its wrapper, and a command with no record keeps today's charge. ## Not required

- Any change to the acceptance check, a landing check or what the private-kind verdict decides: all run on the applied tree before anything is queued.
- A direct call to the provider outside the client the accounts are for.

### Landing queue p90 from 38 min toward 60 s: one owner for the number, by design (was #902)
