title: fix(dolt): re-mint auto IDs on create retry replay (supersedes #6831)
body:
Supersedes #6831 by @quad341, with credit.
Fixes #7289

## Summary

Both candidates agree that rolled-back auto-minted IDs survive in caller structs, so replay can overwrite a competing writer. Keep Kimi's local wrapper fix and Opus's verified comment-ID reset, counter recovery and wisp coverage. Replay must allocate again, but may legitimately obtain the same unoccupied ID. Scope is the three create retry closures and focused tests.

## Related open PRs

Three older open PRs change the same retry closures in `internal/storage/dolt/issues.go`, and each conflicts with this PR there. Which replay rule lands, and in what order, is waiting on a maintainer decision.

- **#6754** (by quad341; #6831 is stacked on it). Its commit `e2f711a129` already empties an auto-minted ID at the top of each `createIssue` retry attempt, the rule this PR's first commit applies, so this PR re-delivers that hunk under the credit above. The rest of #6754 is not here: it forces `CreateOnly` for auto-minted IDs and jumps the issue counter past explicit IDs (now tracked as #8456). Main has since gained the both-planes check for hash mints that #6754 also adds (`IDTakenInTx`).
- **#8218** restores the caller's whole request at the top of the same three closures (`issueops.SnapshotCreateInputs`). It also covers routes this PR leaves alone: the proxied import batch (#8455), the proxied `bd todo add` and `bd q` creates, the tracker store, and lost `DOLT_COMMIT` responses. The two PRs set different hash-mode rules. #8218 puts back the caller's `CreatedAt` (zero for a new issue), so each attempt stamps a new one and the hash mint draws a new candidate. This PR keeps the first attempt's `CreatedAt`, and its subtest `hash mode reuses its own unoccupied id` would fail under #8218's restore (traced, not run). #8218's hash-mode create test checks only the comment ID.
- **#7583** (draft) is the earlier form of #8218's create restore and conflicts in the same places.

## Acceptance criteria

Grades are per candidate. The contributor PR had no test run (see below).

- **AC-1:** Given seeded counter mode and a singular auto-ID CreateIssue rolled back before a competitor auto-mints its aborted ID, when retry succeeds, then the competitor retains its title and the caller's different final ID names its own row. (glm partial, opus pass)
- **AC-2:** Given a durable auto-ID CreateIssues batch with a backfilled dependency and fresh comment, rolled back before a competitor occupies its ID, when retry succeeds, then the competitor is unchanged, the caller and dependency use the new issue ID, and the stored comment ID derives from its final owner/content/timestamp. (glm pass, opus pass)
- **AC-3:** Given seeded counter mode and an auto-ID singular create rolled back without a competitor, when replay and a subsequent auto-ID create succeed, then both have distinct IDs and retain their respective titles. (glm pass, opus pass)
- **AC-4:** Given an all-ephemeral auto-ID batch rolled back before a competitor occupies its wisp ID, when retry succeeds, then the competitor is unchanged and the caller's different final ID names its own wisp. (glm pass, opus pass)
- **AC-5:** Given singular and batch creates with supplied issue, dependency-source or comment IDs, when rolled back and replayed, then supplied values remain unchanged in caller objects and the records each API normally persists. (glm partial, opus pass)

## How this was built

- Design: `design.pair` (anthropic-opus, moonshot-kimi, xai-grok, zhipu-glm).
- Independent candidates: glm (pass), opus (pass), pr (no test ran: #6831's branch predates `MODULE.bazel`, so the triage replay found no Bazel workspace).
- Judge (grok) composed the change per AC: AC-1 ← opus, AC-2 ← opus, AC-3 ← merge, AC-4 ← opus, AC-5 ← opus.
  - AC-3: merged by the integrator (take opus 81da12725b1d (its counter-mode test on installReplayFault/enableSeededCounterMode); add glm d7f33e0c1b75's 'hash mode reuses its own unoccupied id' subtest (no counter config, no competitor; onFault records caller.ID; assert replay ID == aborted ID and the row holds the caller title), ported onto opus's installReplayFault/assertReplayed/requireTitle harness. That subtest is the design's 'hash replay without an ID change' guard against a fix that forces a new ID on every attempt; opus omits it. Do not take glm's createCommitFault harness or its create_issues_retry_remint_test.go.)
  - AC-4: apply fell back to glm `29bf21e154`, whose test needs a harness this branch lacks, so the integrator replaced it with the judge's pick, opus `e3d580046b`. Commit `fcc119bb80` is that cherry-pick.
- Canonical tests (at `b75b1b78ae`): `bazel-test //internal/storage/dolt:dolt_test --test_filter='^(TestCreateIssueReplayRemintsAutoMintedID|TestCreateIssuesReplayMovesBackfilledDependencyToRemint|TestCreateIssueReplayKeepsCounterAheadOfReplayedID|TestCreateIssuesAllWispsReplayRemintsWispID|TestCreateIssueAndCreateIssuesReplayKeepCallerSuppliedIDs)$' --test_env=BEADS_TEST_SKIP= --test_env=BEADS_TEST_DOLT_SERVER=local --test_env=BEADS_TEST_REQUIRE_DOLT_CONTAINER=1` → pass.
- Final review (kimi, at `b75b1b78ae`): pass.

Judge rationale: Both candidates carry the same production fix: a snapshot of the initially empty issue/dependency/comment IDs, reset first in all three retry closures in dolt/issues.go. Opus's helper comment is tighter, and both passed the independent run. The differences are in the tests. AC-1 opus: it seeds the counter as the AC requires, asserts the competitor really minted the aborted ID (proves the race), and adds a rollbacks=2 case. glm leaves the counter unseeded and checks the race only implicitly. AC-2 opus: every issue in a 1- and 3-issue batch carries a dependency and a comment, a competitor takes each issue's aborted ID, and the test asserts the aborted attempt filled the backfills. It also places the PrefixOverride-outside-allowed-prefixes subtest on the batch path, where prefix validation actually applies; glm put it on the singular path, which skips validation. AC-3 merge: opus's counter test plus glm's hash-mode reuse subtest from the design's test plan. AC-4: the two are equivalent; take opus for harness consistency. AC-5 opus: it covers the design's explicit dependency source on an auto-ID issue and checks the persisted edges and comments. glm only claims that case in a comment. Opus's fault also fires only on transactions that wrote an issue row and counts only create commits, which pins the replay more precisely than glm's first-commit-of-any-transaction fault. glm's extra create_issues_retry_remint_test.go, which runs a CreateIssue inside OnSkippedDependency while the transaction is open, duplicates the deterministic harness; drop it. The contributor PR #6831 failed the triage repro and contributes no AC code; its approach (CreateOnly plus autoMint) differs from the approved design. The pipeline handles credit.

Correction: #6831 did not fail the triage repro. The repro could not run on its branch, which predates `MODULE.bazel`.

## Known gaps

- This head has no CHANGELOG entry for the fix, and none of its commits carries a `Co-authored-by` trailer for Jim Wordelman, the author of #6754 and #6831. A maintainer review commit adds both: an entry under Unreleased, Fixed, and the trailer. It was reviewed but not pushed, because the review ended with maintainer decisions still open (see Related open PRs).

## Limitations

- Other create paths still replay with what an aborted attempt wrote back, and this PR does not change them: the proxied import batch (#8455), the proxied `bd todo add` and `bd q` creates, and the proxied `bd jira` and `bd linear` pulls and syncs, which create through the tracker store. #8218 covers all of them.
- Two related bugs are tracked separately. A counter-mode mint can still overwrite an explicit row that sits ahead of the counter (#8456), and a replay reaches that bug too: when the concurrent writer named the aborted ID itself (`bd create --id`, an import row), the counter has not moved past it, so the re-mint draws the same value and upserts over that writer's row. A create that fails for good leaves its minted ID on the caller's issue (#8457).
- When a replay re-mints because another writer took the ID, an import row that has no ID and whose dependency target is missing is reported as skipped twice, once under the aborted ID. Only the skipped-dependency report (stderr and `--json skipped_dependencies`) is affected.

---
Source bead: `bd-p6skpo` · checkpoint pipeline v0

title: fix(schema): do not record a migration whose dropped default survives
body:
## Summary

The candidates agree on the bug—marks lack DDL verification—but differ on repair timing. Extend PR #8151 to verify new marks, repair recorded drift through explicit `bd migrate schema`, and diagnose it through doctor. Direct DDL avoids replay and preserves ordinary-open behavior/consent. The historical trigger, including any prepared-statement failure, remains unproven; flatten causation was withdrawn.

## Acceptance criteria

Grades are the pipeline's independent runs of each candidate (glm · opus · pr8151).

- **AC-1** (pass · pass · -): Given an applying migration whose body succeeds but leaves a dropped default, when its direct correction succeeds, then absence is verified before writing the mark, and the main step commits its tracked correction with that mark.
- **AC-2** (pass · partial · -): Given an applying migration with multiple unmet conditions and a failed probe or unsuccessful correction, when post-checking completes, then its error identifies affected conditions and failures, and neither its cursor row nor step commit is written.
- **AC-3** (partial · pass · -): Given a current database with recorded default drift on clean tracked tables, when explicit bd migrate schema runs, then it durably repairs only those shapes, preserves rows/cursor records, reports repairs in text/JSON, and a repeat creates no repair commit.
- **AC-4** (pass · pass · -): Given a tracked repair target with uncommitted user changes, when explicit repair runs, then it refuses before altering any target, names the dirty table and remedy, and neither changes nor commits user data.
- **AC-5** (pass · pass · -): Given a current database with a recorded default obligation on an ignored table, including post-0062 events or ignored-0010 wisp tables, when explicit repair runs, then the default is removed without changing rows, staging the table, or committing it into shared history.
- **AC-6** (pass · pass · -): Given a healthy current store, when an ordinary open or no-work MigrateUp runs, then this change adds no dropped-default probes, repair DDL, or commits and preserves the convergence fast path.
- **AC-7** (partial · pass · -): Given a healthy, drifted, or uninspectable database, when doctor checks it in server or embedded mode, then it respectively reports OK, all applicable violations with the repair hint, or could-not-check, without changing schema, cursors, or history.
  At this head the check handles both modes (`doctor.CheckMigrationPostConditions`, tested in both), but the `bd doctor` command runs it in direct server mode only: bare `bd doctor` is gated off in embedded mode (beads issue 3794), and a proxied-server workspace refuses `bd doctor`.

## How this was built

- Design: `design.pair` (anthropic-opus, moonshot-kimi, xai-grok, zhipu-glm).
- Independent candidates: glm (pass), opus (pass), pr8151 (untested).
- Judge (grok) composed the change per AC: AC-1 ← merge, AC-2 ← merge, AC-3 ← opus, AC-4 ← merge, AC-5 ← opus, AC-6 ← opus, AC-7 ← opus.
  - AC-1: merged by the integrator (take opus ebaa2eb150 as the code base (stripSQLComments: the design requires ignoring comments while keeping literals, which glm lacks; probeDroppedDefault/dropDefaultAndVerify are the helpers opus's AC-3/AC-7 repair+check reuse); from glm 5e8664f740 take the typed failure shape: return a *PostConditionError{Failures []PostConditionFailure{Source(cursor table),Version,Table,Column,Observed,Cause}} from verifyDroppedDefaults (fed by opus's droppedDefaultFailure list plus src/version threaded from runMigrations) so the error carries source/version provenance as the design asks; keep both candidates' same-step-commit embedded tests)
  - AC-2: merged by the integrator (take glm 7bfe1f4339 tests (sqlmock TestRunMigrationsPostCheckReportsEveryUnmetConditionAndWritesNothing asserting per-failure Source/Version/Observed/Cause, and the real-engine TestEmbeddedMigrateUncorrectableDefaultFailsLoudlyWithoutTheMark_5269 with refusingCorrectionConn + re-run stays failed) adapted to the merged AC-1 code; keep opus 13d7cb7afc's TestRunMigrationsReportsEveryUnmetDroppedDefaultAndWritesNoMark too; register new embedded Test funcs in .github/scripts/embedded-storage-test-shards.txt)
  - AC-4: merged by the integrator (take opus 6bea76687c (code from opus f7ce5408d2: PostConditionRepairDirtyError refused before any ALTER); add glm 5d5200c9b9's CLI arm in handleSchemaMigrate: errors.As the dirty-repair error and return HandleErrorWithHint naming the commit-first remedy (bd dolt commit / CALL DOLT_COMMIT over sql-server), plus glm's cmd/bd embedded test asserting the refusal text, adapted to opus's type name)
- Canonical tests, at the pipeline head `1f75d6a043` (before the review changes below): `bazel-test //internal/storage/schema:schema_test //cmd/bd/doctor:doctor_test --test_filter='^(TestRunMigrationsDoesNotRecordAMarkWhoseDroppedDefaultSurvives|TestRunMigrationsRecordsTheMarkWhenTheDroppedDefaultIsGone|TestRunMigrationsCorrectsALeftoverDroppedDefaultBeforeTheMark|TestRunMigrationsChecksEveryDefaultAMigrationDrops|TestDroppedDefaultsOfTheShippedMigrations|TestDroppedDefaultsIgnoresCommentsAndKeepsLiterals|TestShowColumnDefaultNullVersusEmptyAndExactField|TestRunMigrationsReportsEveryUnmetDroppedDefaultAndWritesNoMark|TestRunMigrationsPostCheckReportsEveryUnmetConditionAndWritesNothing|TestObligationsAtCursorsFollowsEachSourceAndRetirement|TestCheckMigrationPostConditions_NoDatabase|TestCheckMigrationPostConditions_CouldNotCheck|TestCheckMigrationPostConditions_Embedded|TestCheckMigrationPostConditions_RealDolt)$' --test_env=BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 --test_env=BEADS_TEST_SKIP= --test_env=BEADS_TEST_DOLT_SERVER=local --test_env=BEADS_TEST_REQUIRE_DOLT_CONTAINER=1 && bazel test //internal/storage/embeddeddolt:embeddeddolt_embedded_test //cmd/bd:bd_embedded_test --config=embedded --test_sharding_strategy=disabled --test_arg='-test.run=^(TestEmbeddedMigrateDoesNotRecordVersionWhoseDDLDidNotApply_5269|TestEmbeddedMigrateCommitsTheDroppedDefaultCorrectionWithItsMark_5269|TestEmbeddedMigrateCorrectionCommitsWithTheMark_5269|TestEmbeddedMigrateUncorrectableDefaultFailsLoudlyWithoutTheMark_5269|TestEmbeddedMigrateSchemaRepairsRecordedDefaultDriftOnTrackedTables_5269|TestEmbeddedMigrateSchemaRepairRefusesDirtyTrackedTarget_5269|TestEmbeddedMigrateSchemaRepairsIgnoredTablesWithoutCommitting_5269|TestEmbeddedHealthyCurrentStoreHasNoPostConditionWork_5269|TestEmbeddedMigrateSchema_RepairsRecordedDefaultDrift_5269|TestEmbeddedMigrateSchemaRefusesDirtyTrackedTarget_5269)$' --test_arg=-test.skip= --test_output=errors && bazel-test //scripts:go_test_sources_test` → pass.
- Final review (kimi): pass.

Judge rationale: Both candidates build on #8151 and pass the independent run; behaviour matches the approved design, so this is per-AC composition. AC-1: near-identical probe/ALTER/re-probe; opus strips SQL comments (design requirement) and its helpers are reused by the repair, glm's typed PostConditionError carries the source/version provenance the design asks for -> merge. AC-2: glm's tests are stronger (typed per-failure provenance, real-engine uncorrectable correction, retry stays failed); opus is sqlmock-only and its error lacks source -> merge onto merged AC-1. AC-3: opus keeps the server retry/backoff wrapper (initSchemaOnDBWithRetryAndGateBootstrapHeal + WithPostConditionRepair option) where glm calls MigrateUpWithRepair directly and loses retry; opus emits a deterministic [] repaired list (glm emits null), sets commandDidWrite on partial success (design requirement glm misses), and registers its embedded tests in the shard manifests (glm does not, which reds //scripts:go_test_sources_test). AC-4: equivalent refusal; opus code, plus glm's dedicated CLI hint. AC-5: equivalent; opus for consistency with its repair code. AC-6: opus's test also proves a fresh store reports zero violations (guards un-retired obligations) and that ordinary MigrateUp leaves recorded drift alone. AC-7: opus pins one session, reports every violation even when some probes fail (glm hides all violations behind one probe error), and has a real Dolt server-mode test alongside embedded. pr8151 contributes the foundation both candidates ported; credit must be kept (Co-authored-by kyoto-bonsai).

## Changes after the checkpoint pipeline

Two maintainer review passes added one commit on top of the pipeline head:

- The server-mode repair path is pinned by two tests: a strict sqlmock test (the repair runs under the migration lock, after a MigrateUp that finds no work) and a real Dolt server test (only the tracked table lands in the repair commit, the main pool is rebuilt, and a repeat is a no-op).
- The correction notice and the per-column repair lines go to stderr even when it is not a terminal (bd serve, systemd, CI and agents), since a correction firing is the only field evidence of the trigger.
- A failed post-check names what to do next, in order: re-run `bd migrate schema` first; in server mode, drop the default over SQL, commit it, then re-run; otherwise (embedded mode, or the drop does not take), report the error with the Dolt version.
- A repair whose stage or commit fails is never reported as repaired. `bd migrate schema` fails, lists those columns under `uncommitted` in its `--json` error output, and names the commit that finishes them. That error is never retried: a retry found nothing left to repair and reported success with nothing committed.
- Through a gateway server, which owns the schema, `bd migrate schema` does not repair. It makes the same `ApplySchemaMigrations` call as before this change, so a converged database takes no lock, DDL or commit. The doctor check names the server administrator's fix instead of `bd migrate schema`.
- On a proxied-server workspace, `bd migrate schema` says the repair does not run there.
- A guard test requires every `DROP DEFAULT` in a shipped migration to be in the form the obligation regex recognizes.

## Limitations

- A proxied-server workspace gets neither the repair nor the doctor check yet.
- A repair interrupted between its `ALTER` and its commit is not found again: the dropped default stays uncommitted in the working set until a commit takes the table. This happens when the process is killed, or in server mode when the connection drops after the server applied the `ALTER`: the retry then finds nothing left to repair and exits 0. A failed stage or commit within the run is reported, as above.
- The doctor tests against a real Dolt engine (`migration_post_conditions_dolt_test.go`) run in no CI lane yet; the file says how to run them by hand.

title: bug: never-started pending-create lease (10 min) keeps aging while the controller's own wake budget / async-start limit defers the start; 482 of 487 polecat rollbacks on a 49-rig city had no start attempt
body:
### Before you continue

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate. Closest: #7680 (open, 2026-10-12: the wake budget has no priority for routed pool work, so polecats wait behind idle rigs' patrol restarts). This report is the next failure after that wait: the never-started pending-create lease keeps aging while the controller itself defers the start, so the reconciler rolls the session back as `lease expired and no live runtime` although no start was ever attempted. Also related: #772 (closed, Apr 2026: 5-per-tick cap and stuck `creating` zombies), #6576 (closed: terminal-provider-error rollback), #7170 (no load-aware wake budget on cold start).
- [x] I read `docs/reference/config.md` (`max_wakes_per_tick`, `[session] startup_timeout`).

### Gas City version

`gc version --json`: `{"commit":"84e7084c6","date":"2026-10-12T09:02:57Z","version":"edge"}` (`84e7084c6a9810c9fd902836e2db755c093b82c2`). The code cited below is unchanged on `main` at `903df100f` (2026-10-12 20:14Z): `pendingCreateNeverStartedTimeout = 10 * time.Minute`, `DefaultMaxWakesPerTick = 5`.

### Environment

- macOS (Darwin 27.2.0), Mac Studio, 28 cores, 96 GiB, tmux provider, Dolt-backed beads (`bd 1.3.0 b630f96f5`, `dolt 2.4.2`, one proxied sql-server per scope)
- One city, 49 rigs (35 suspended today as a mitigation), stock `max_wakes_per_tick` (5), stock `startup_timeout` (60s)
- Supervisor on `gc supervisor run`; load average 50-77 during the morning incident, 28-36 in the afternoon (28 cores)

### What happened

A pool polecat session bead for `payroll/gastown.nux` (`ha-wisp-2h7ytj`) was created at 14:14:57Z with `state=start-pending`, `pending_create_claim=true`, `pending_create_started_at=2026-10-12T14:14:45Z`. The controller never attempted to start it. Its only lifecycle line is:

```
2026/10/12 10:23:34 session lifecycle: op=start wave=0 session=gastown__polecat-ha-wisp-2h7ytj template=payroll/gastown.polecat outcome=deferred_by_wake_budget
```

(local time, UTC-4). Twelve minutes later the reconciler rolled it back:

```
2026/10/12 10:35:54 session reconciler: rolling back pending create gastown__polecat-ha-wisp-2h7ytj: lease expired and no live runtime
```

The session bead's event history (`.gc/events.jsonl`) shows `state=start-pending`, `last_woke_at` empty and the same `pending_create_started_at` on every update until the close at 14:35:56Z with `state=failed-create`. The routed work the session existed for went back to the pool and waited for the next polecat, which hit the same queue.

### This is systematic, not one session

From `~/.gc/supervisor.log` (2026-10-08 to 2026-10-12):

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| `rolling back pending create ...: lease expired and no live runtime` lines | 882 (636 on 10-10, 17 on 10-11, 159 on 10-12) |
| Distinct **polecat** sessions rolled back | 487 |
| ... that had a `deferred_by_wake_budget` lifecycle line before the rollback | **482** |
| ... that had any other `op=start` outcome (an actual start attempt) | **0** |
| Only `op=start` outcomes ever logged for those 487 sessions | `deferred_by_async_start_limit` 2,887; `deferred_by_wake_budget` 2,319 |
| Minutes from a session's first deferral to its rollback | min 5.0, median 9.9, max 92.6 (n=482) |
| `deferred_by_wake_budget` lines on 2026-10-12 alone | 2,166 (peak 864 in the 14:00 local hour) |

The remaining rollbacks are always-mode witnesses and refineries of idle rigs (15-19 each), the same sessions that take the start slots in #7680.

### Why (source, `84e7084c6`)

1. `createPoolSessionBead` stamps `pending_create_started_at` when the bead is created (`cmd/gc/session_beads.go:2565`; also `:602`, `cmd/gc/session_name_lookup.go:380`). That timestamp is the lease anchor for a never-started create: `pendingCreateNeverStartedExpiredAt` (`cmd/gc/session_reconciler.go:1460`) returns true once `now > anchor + pendingCreateNeverStartedTimeout` and `last_woke_at` is empty.
2. `pendingCreateNeverStartedTimeout = 10 * time.Minute` (`cmd/gc/session_reconciler.go:1408`). Its comment says the window exists so "never-started creates need enough time to sit behind a busy pool start queue", so the queue was anticipated, but the value is fixed and nothing refreshes the anchor while the session sits in that queue.
3. The two places that decline to start a session, `deferred_by_wake_budget` (`cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go:4018`, `:4046`) and `deferred_by_async_start_limit` (`:114`), only log. They write nothing to the bead, so from the lease's point of view a session the controller refused to start for 10 minutes is indistinguishable from a provider that took the start and died.
4. The rollback sites (`cmd/gc/session_reconciler.go:2179` and `:2960`) check `pendingCreateLeaseExpiredForRollbackInfo` and the rate-limit guard only; there is no "did we ever try" term.
5. With `max_wakes_per_tick=5`, 49 rigs' always-mode witnesses and refineries ahead in `sortCandidatesByWakeFairness` order (#7680), and ticks that took 27-43 s on average and up to 854 s in the incident hours (`cycle_result.duration_ms` in the reconciler trace), a fresh pool session routinely waits more than 10 minutes without a single attempt.

### Expected behaviour

A lease is a guard against a start that was handed to the provider and went dark. A session the controller never tried to start should not be rolled back for "no live runtime"; it should keep waiting for a slot (or be reported as starved), and the routed work should stay with it. Any of these would do:

- Treat a controller-side deferral as keeping the lease alive: refresh `pending_create_started_at` (or a new `last_deferred_at`) when a start is deferred by the wake budget or the async-start limit, and anchor the never-started timeout on that.
- Or exclude never-attempted sessions from `pendingCreateNeverStartedExpired` altogether, with a separate, longer starvation alarm (`session.start_starved` event) instead of a rollback.
- Or scale the never-started window by queue position / `max_wakes_per_tick` instead of a fixed 10 minutes.

### Reproduction

1. City with stock `max_wakes_per_tick` (5) and enough always-mode sessions (witness + refinery per rig, 20+ rigs) that a reconcile wave has more than 5 start candidates every tick, on a host where ticks take more than a few seconds.
2. Route work so a pool polecat bead is created.
3. Watch `supervisor.log`: the polecat logs `deferred_by_wake_budget` each wave; `gc bd show <session bead>` keeps `state=start-pending`, `last_woke_at` empty.
4. About 10 minutes after `pending_create_started_at`, the reconciler logs `rolling back pending create ...: lease expired and no live runtime` and the bead closes `failed-create`, with no start attempt in between.

### Evidence retained

Full-day supervisor excerpt, per-session first-deferral-to-rollback timing (482 rows), the session bead's event history, and the reconciler tick summary are retained in the reporting project with SHA-256 receipts; happy to attach any of them here.

title: test(grid): the inbox's stand-in box refuses another grid's delivery, as a wisp does
body:
Flake seen on #762, run 42675522318, `full / test (ubuntu-latest, node 22)`: `test/grid-inbox.test.js` 'url_verification, box up…' failed at `g.got(ada).length`, **4 !== 1**.

## Cause
Each test boots its own grid, and they all stay up until `after()`. A grid whose box is slow to listen (the `NEVER` tests, `bootMs`) keeps probing that box's port. `freePort()` can hand the same port to a box another grid is starting. The first grid's probe then gets that box's `/api/health`, marks its own box running there, and delivers what it held. `test/fixtures/inbox-box.mjs` wrote down every delivery without checking `x-wisp-proxy-secret`, which a real wisp checks (`server/http/trust.js`).

## Fix (test only)
The stand-in box answers 401 to a delivery without its own `WISP_TRUSTED_PROXY_SECRET` and keeps nothing, as a wisp does. The inbox treats a 4xx as refused, so the stray grid stops trying.

## Proof
New test: 'a delivery from another grid that landed on this box's port is refused, not kept'. It points a second grid's hostd at the first grid's box port, which is what the probe ends up believing.
- Without the fixture change: fails, `actual: 1`.
- With it: `node --test test/grid-inbox.test.js` passed 60/60 in 5 of 6 runs on macOS (Node 25.8.1, load around 13, other agents running). One run had 1 failure whose name I didn't capture, and 5 reruns didn't reproduce it. `test/grid-route.test.js` (also uses the fixture) passed 87/87.

Note: production hostd has the same probe race between two users' boxes on one grid. The other box's wisp refuses requests carrying the wrong secret, so nothing leaks. But the slow box is marked running on a port that isn't its own. That's worth its own fix, not this PR.

QA/test only, no CHANGELOG entry.

title: fix(storage): advance child_counters for caller-named children on the proxied path (supersedes #8138)
body:
Supersedes #8138 by @kyoto-bonsai, with credit.

## Summary

Both independent candidates identify the same bug: proxied creates with caller-named hierarchical IDs bypass the parent's child counter, permitting suffix reuse after a hard delete. Add a small counter-repository wrapper around the existing `issueops.ReconcileChildCounters`, called after a successful caller-named insert in the shared domain create body. Keep the advance in the insert's existing transaction, cover explicit and preset IDs, and update the affected history-off golden. The candidates disagree about whether a hypothetical non-atomic fallback is acceptable; this synthesis requires atomicity and adds a rollback check.

## Known limits

- A proxied batch create (the unit-of-work `BatchCreator`) that lists a caller-named child before its parent, as in `[P.8, P]`, still leaves P's counter behind. Each item advances right after its own insert, when P does not exist yet, and the advance skips a missing parent. The dolt and embedded `BatchCreator` bodies reconcile the whole batch once after every insert, so they handle either order. Parent-first batches advance (`ParentFirstBatchRaisesCounter`).
- The new create-path tests start at the shared domain create body (`IssueUseCase().CreateIssue` with the id set by the test), and the repository tests call `AdvanceForChild` directly. No test drives the advance through `uow.issueOperations.Create`, the route `bd create --id P.8` takes on a proxied server; that this route reaches it is shown by reading the code (`createParams` sets `ExplicitID: issue.ID`).

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Criterion | glm | opus |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | Given an existing durable parent P with no higher used suffix, when a proxied create successfully names P.8 and commits, then its counter is 8 and, after hard deletion without a tombstone, a subsequent parent-based create mints P.9. | pass | pass |
| AC-2 | Given an existing parent with no counter row, when a unit of work creates its caller-named child and then returns an error, then neither the new child nor its counter row persists after rollback. | pass | pass |
| AC-3 | Given an existing parent whose counter is already higher than a caller-named child suffix, when that child is successfully created, then the counter retains its higher value. | pass | pass |
| AC-4 | Given an existing wisp parent W, when a proxied create names W.3 and commits, then wisp_child_counters contains (W, 3) and child_counters is unchanged. | pass | pass |
| AC-5 | Given the unchanged history-off scenario and the deliberately re-recorded uow golden, when the uow differential test runs, then it passes and its child_counters fingerprint equals both existing storage-leg goldens, with no other table delta from base. | pass | pass |

The contributor's PR #8138 has no column: its independent test run timed out, so no run graded it. The judge found its fix code equivalent to both candidates' fix code, and this PR keeps its absolute-digest golden test verbatim (AC-5).

## How this was built

- Design: `design.pair` (anthropic-opus, moonshot-kimi, xai-grok, zhipu-glm).
- Independent candidates: glm (pass), opus (pass), pr #8138 (untested: its run timed out).
- Judge (grok) composed the change per AC: AC-1 ← glm, AC-2 ← glm, AC-3 ← merge, AC-4 ← merge, AC-5 ← merge.
  - AC-3: merged by the integrator: take glm a4005583f2 (repository AdvanceForChild cases: never-lowers, equal/no-op byte-identical fingerprints, flat/.0/nonnumeric/missing-parent, grandchild, leading zero, minted-once) and add opus 8e93c3095de0's create-path TestIssueUseCase_CallerNamedChildNeverLowersTheCounter (counter 10: explicit .8 keeps 10, explicit .12 raises to 12) to issue_usecase_test.go, rewritten onto glm's requireCounterRow/requireCounterTable helpers instead of opus's childCounterValue.
  - AC-4: merged by the integrator: take glm 151b6e3c22 (repository wisp-parent routing + wisp child under a durable parent) and add opus fe4c5deaf57a's create-path TestIssueUseCase_CallerNamedWispChildAdvancesWispCounter (CreateWisp cn-w then cn-w.3; wisp_child_counters=3, whole child_counters table unchanged), using glm's counterTablesFingerprint/requireCounterTable helpers in place of opus's counterTableRows/childCounterValue.
  - AC-5: merged by the integrator: take glm 032b1abfa4's golden/uow.json and historyoffequiv/BUILD.bazel (go_test with the blank line before the managed go_srcs block; opus's lacks it), but use the contributor PR #8138's (c5e2e185f406, by kyoto-bonsai) golden_test.go verbatim, marked `Derived-From: pr/c5e2e185f406`: it pins every leg to the absolute (ho-epic, 1) digest via the package's digest(), which also catches all three legs drifting together; glm/opus only compare legs to each other.
- Canonical tests: `bazel-test //internal/storage/domain/db:db_test --test_filter='^TestDomainDB$/^(TestIssueUseCase_CallerNamedChildAdvancesParentCounter|TestIssueUseCase_CallerNamedChildNeverLowersTheCounter|TestIssueUseCase_CallerNamedWispChildAdvancesWispCounter|TestChildCounterSQLRepository)$' --test_env=BEADS_TEST_SKIP= --test_env=BEADS_TEST_DOLT_SERVER=local --test_env=BEADS_TEST_REQUIRE_DOLT_CONTAINER=1 && bazel-test //internal/storage/uow:uow_test --test_filter='^(TestCallerNamedChildCounterRollsBack|TestVersionedHistoryOffMatchesPreStackGolden_UOW|TestIssueOperationsCreateUnderAParentMintsTheNextChildID)$' --test_env=BEADS_TEST_SKIP= --test_env=BEADS_TEST_DOLT_SERVER=local --test_env=BEADS_TEST_REQUIRE_DOLT_CONTAINER=1 && bazel-test //internal/storage/domain:domain_test //internal/storage/historyoffequiv:historyoffequiv_test --test_filter='^(TestCallerNamedChildCounterGating|TestGoldenChildCountersFingerprintMatchesAcrossLegs)$'` → pass.
- Final review (kimi): pass.

Judge rationale: Fix code is equivalent in glm, opus and the PR (AdvanceForChild wrapper over issueops.ReconcileChildCounters, called after Insert under createIDNamedByCaller, same tx); glm and opus passed the independent run (both 'repro after: fail' are conflict markers from re-applying the repro patch onto a test they already extended, not a defect); PR untested (timeout). AC-1 glm: same fix plus the design's call/error-gate fake test (explicit+preset advance, minted/failed insert skip, advance error stops later writes), counter-at-7 immediate-reuse variant, preset, parent-first batch and upsert cases; opus lacks the gate test. PR's *types.Issue signature + ParseHierarchicalID precheck is the duplicate guard the design omitted. AC-2 glm: in-tx counter assertion via scanRawSQLValue (opus's fmt.Sprint of a raw value is weaker) and also checks the parent stayed committed; equivalent otherwise. AC-3/AC-4 merge: glm covers the design's repository matrix, opus alone exercises the AC wording through the real create/CreateWisp path; take both. AC-5 merge: glm's re-recorded golden (same sha as opus/PR) and clean BUILD, contributor's absolute-digest golden test.

title: Jet engine glow, afterburner flame and engine/wingtip trails
body:
# Jet engine glow, afterburner flame and engine/wingtip trails, from each airframe's own data

Head: `f6c92320f` (lighter look and gear up in flight), on top of `5cf6191cc` (every jet's exhaust from its own airframe data) and the merge `d8c674d68` (origin/staging `84be4dde3` merged in). Every earlier PR commit is kept.

## One shared rule, data-driven
- Every roster fixed-wing jet (25) gets glow, flame, engine trail, tip lines and the wing sheet from **one** system: `presentation.effects.jet_exhaust`. No jet is special-cased in code.
- **Geometry comes from the art itself.** `bun run --cwd web jet-airframes` reads each jet's source GLB (LOD0 named nodes) and writes `airframes.<appearance>` in `fixtures/presentation.json`:
  - **Nozzle exits:** the rearmost vertex inside each opening's outline, walled above and below.
  - **Wingtips:** at 97 % of the span.
  - **Wing planform:** stations from root (3 %) to tip.
  - `web/tests/sceneAssets/jetAirframes.test.ts` fails if the art and the fixture drift apart.
- **The only authored per-jet field is `engine`,** which is the honest engine type:
  - `afterburning_turbofan`: 23 jets, with flame.
  - `high_bypass_turbofan`: A-10C, no flame.
  - `turbojet`: Su-25, no flame.
- **The wing sheet** comes from one `wing_sheet_rule`: `{span: [-0.1, 0.4], rows: [[-0.1, 0.15], [0.3, 0.2]], spacing_m: 1.2, lift_m: 0.2}`, measured as span and chord shares of each jet's own wing.
  - Its strength is `(vapour − sheet_from)/(1 − sheet_from)`, so it forms only in the hardest pulls.
  - Fitted against the approved post 30 F-22 points: every approved point is within 0.22 m (mean about 0.19 m).
- **Landing gear** (new): every fixed-wing aircraft in flight has its gear stowed, from its flight state in the real pose driver (`units/driver/vehicle.rs`), not a capture helper.
  - Each model's `gear_*` legs fold away about their tops, with an eased 4 s travel.
  - A model at rest (labs, bakes) still stands on its gear.
  - Helicopters and ground vehicles are unchanged.

- At cruise the engine trail is now a faint haze, not smoke. The afterburner adds back opacity through `reheat`.
- I measured the share of near-white pixels in each frame (saturation < 0.08, value > 0.78):

Every jet now falls between 1.97 % and 3.10 %; the F/A-18E is the highest. The full list is in `look-metric.txt`.

The F-15E's nozzles sit 0.05 m apart fore and aft, which is how the art is built. Wingtips are symmetric to within 0.09 m. Wing-station asymmetry is 0.42 m on the F-22 and 0.38 m on the Su-57 (both at the root trailing edge, as the art has it) and 0.18 m or less on the rest.

## Checks (head `f6c92320f`)
- **Hooks:** every commit went through them, none skipped. That covers the size ratchet, eslint, oxlint, oxfmt, `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, all green.
- **Workspace tests** (all but renderer-core and native-client, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`): 116 test binaries, **2188 passed, 0 failed**.
- **GPU suites** (`cargo test --no-fail-fast -p renderer-core -p native-client`, under the GPU locks): **116 passed, 0 failed**. That includes native-client `counts`.
- **New tests:**
  - `presentation/tests/aircraft_gear.rs`: all 25 roster jets carry at least 3 gear legs; they are stowed in flight from the first frame, down at rest, partly showing halfway, and nothing else on the model scales.
  - `vehicle_poses`: a jet flies gear up, a downed jet keeps it up, and a helicopter and a tank keep theirs down.
  - `jet_airframes`: 6 tests.
  - `jet_exhaust`: 18 tests.
  - `jetAirframes` vitest: 2 tests.
- **Builds:** `bun run build:wasm` and `cargo build --release -p native-client` pass.

## Post 30 comparison
I re-rendered the posted post 30 F-22 shot (both halves, 18 s) with this head. The jet, cameras, timing, capture-only airframe lighting and SDR pipeline are post 30's; I dropped all of its capture-only vapour overrides, including the F-22-only sheet points. The result is a frame-aligned side-by-side mp4 plus still pairs at the side peak and the rear peak. The files are local for now (`post30-compare/` beside this body); they are not uploaded.

There are two known differences:
- The simulation was re-recorded with this branch's recorder. The flight path and the camera rig report are identical frame for frame.
- At the same frame the jet is drawn roughly 50–100 px further right than in post 30. The camera records are identical, so it most likely comes from how the current code places the drawn jet.

## Performance
Native, Apple M6, 1920×1080 offscreen, one pass each on the identical post 30 shot. Frame time is the larger of CPU and GPU time per frame.

| Shot | This PR median | post 30 recipe median | GPU median (PR / post 30) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| side half | 14.04 ms (71 fps) | 14.35 ms (70 fps) | 13.86 / 13.79 ms |
| rear half | 16.20 ms (62 fps) | 16.79 ms (60 fps) | 15.62 / 15.73 ms |

The medians are on par. The p95 and p99 tails were dominated by unrelated load on the machine (a dev server at 190–760 % CPU and a headless browser), so I am not claiming anything from them. A controlled off/on A/B on a quiet machine has not been run for this head; the v2 measurement was +0.052 ms GPU median with six jets.

## Evidence
- **25-jet stills**, all from the same capture: Market Town, 540 km/h, 80 m AGL, and the identical recorded 8.09 g pull on every jet. Side rig at 33 m, 30°, 95°. Hard pull at 3550 ms, F-22 level at 1000 ms. Release native-client with no capture-only environment.
- **Before/after sheets:** `contact-sheet-before-after.png` and `level-vs-hardpull-before-after.png`. These are local and not uploaded yet.
- **Vapour amount:** the median share of near-white pixels across the 25 hard pulls dropped from 4.43 % to 2.23 %. Per jet it now runs from 1.97 % to 3.10 %, against 2.94 % in post 30's frame. The F-22 level shot went from 1.36 % to 0.17 %.
- **Gear:** the gear that used to show in flight on the MiG-31, Su-25 and F/A-18E is gone.

## Known issues
- No heat shimmer. The sheet is soft billows, not a fluid simulation.
- The binary name `post30-recorder` collides in the shared cargo target: building the PR's recorder overwrites post 30's. The evidence uses its own copy (`pr33-recorder`).
- The browser cost of the second effect draw over the high-air plane has not been measured.
- Throttle reads speed against cruise, not the side's afterburner toggle.
- Fixed-wing aircraft never land in this game, so the gear's 4 s travel only shows if the flight state changes. A jet arrives already gear up.

title: fix(tracker): missing history at last_sync no longer hydrates older linked issues (#7294)
body:
## Summary

`bd compact` and `bd flatten` can remove the history row that a tracker pull reads at `last_sync` to tell a newly linked issue from an edited one. The pull then treated every linked issue as newly linked: it fetched the issue again and applied the remote copy past the conflict and overlap guards, so local edits made since the last sync were overwritten (#7294). Now, when a history-capable store (a direct-server or embedded Dolt workspace) has no row for a linked issue at `last_sync`, the pull re-fetches the issue only when it was created at or after `last_sync`, as a new pre-linked stub is. Older issues keep the normal conflict and overlap guards, and the pull prints one warning naming those of them changed since `last_sync`, whose links it could not verify. Linked ephemeral and `--no-history` beads, which never have history, are no longer fetched again on every pull either, and the warning does not name them. The storage interface signature, the sync cursor and compaction are unchanged.

## Changes after the checkpoint pipeline

A maintainer review commit on top of the pipeline's commits (review iterations 1 and 2):

- The creation-time boundary is inclusive. `last_sync` is a whole second and `created_at` is stored rounded to one, so a stub created within half a second after the stamp stores a `created_at` equal to it, and the pipeline's strict "after" refused it the hydration it had before.
- Linked wisps-plane beads (ephemeral and `--no-history`) live in the wisps table, which Dolt does not version, so they never have a history row, compacted or not. One created before `last_sync` is not re-fetched and does not count as unverified, so the warning does not name it on every sync. One created at or after `last_sync` is still re-fetched as a new stub. Before this PR every pull fetched these beads again and applied the remote copy over their local edits.
- The decision lives in the pure `prelinkDecision` helper, so a path that reads this history for many issues at once can decide each issue the same way.
- The warning lists only the missing-history issues updated after `last_sync`, at most five IDs and then a count: every update stamps `updated_at`, so an issue untouched since then still holds the link it had at that sync. It says the conflict checks decided their content, since conflict resolution can import the remote copy in the same run. Its advice depends on the run. A sync that pushes after its pull says its own push may write their local content; a pull-only or dry run says to check their links before a sync that pushes.
- The CHANGELOG entry is scoped to direct-server and embedded workspaces. After `bd compact` or `bd flatten` it recommends `bd <tracker> sync --dry-run` first, which changes nothing, and not a pull-only sync: a pull-only sync stamps `last_sync` after its conflict guard skipped the remote edits of locally edited issues, so the next sync no longer sees those conflicts, and its push can overwrite the remote.
- The real-Dolt test adds a stub created after `last_sync`, which is hydrated whether the compaction removed the baseline or kept it. It also adds a linked ephemeral and a linked no-history bead, edited after `last_sync`. The real store has no history row for them even when the baseline is kept, and they keep their edits without being named in the warning.

## Limitations

- Proxied-server workspaces are not covered. Their tracker commands hand the engine a store without the history capability, so their pull keeps the timestamp heuristic, which this PR leaves unchanged.
- An older issue linked to another remote issue since `last_sync`, while its history at `last_sync` is missing, is not re-fetched, and a push writes its local content to that remote issue. The warning names such candidates; the design keeps local content rather than granting an overwrite on uncertain evidence.
- An ephemeral or `--no-history` bead created before `last_sync` never has history, so the pull cannot tell when it was linked. It is not re-fetched and no warning names it, whether it was linked to another remote issue or linked for the first time since `last_sync`. So linking such an existing bead to an existing remote issue no longer pulls that issue's content, as it did before this PR, and a later sync that pushes the bead can write the bead's content over the remote issue. To pull a remote issue into the wisps plane, create a new linked bead: it is still re-fetched as a new stub.
- Issues a Jira or ADO pull creates take the local clock as their creation time, not the remote's (the GitHub, GitLab, Linear and Notion mappers copy the remote's). One such issue created in the last half second of a sync stores a `created_at` equal to that sync's `last_sync`. If its history at `last_sync` later goes missing, the next pull re-fetches it as a new stub and applies the remote copy past the guards, over any local edit made since. `prelinkDecision`'s doc states this assumption.
- The open batch-path PRs #8163, #7273 and #7298 re-encode this decision inline, and their change to the same code conflicts with this PR. Whichever lands second must decide each issue with `prelinkDecision` and keep the warning.

## Acceptance criteria

Each criterion with the judge's grades for the two built candidates. The pr7296 and pr7502 candidates have no grade here: no test ran (the triage replay found no test target), and both change compaction itself, a different fix (see the judge rationale).

- **AC-1:** Given a history-capable store that returns no historical rows for older linked issues, including issues edited after `last_sync`, when an incremental pull has no bulk remote changes, then it makes zero hydration fetches, adds zero hydration candidates, and preserves every local issue field. (glm pass, opus pass)
- **AC-2:** Given an older issue with missing history and unpushed local edits, when its remote counterpart is returned by either the overlap window or the normal incremental bulk fetch, then missing history grants no hydration exemption and the pull preserves the local edits through the existing conflict and overlap guards. (glm pass, opus pass)
- **AC-3:** Given a new pre-linked stub created after `last_sync` with no historical row, or an older stub with a historical NULL/different external ref, when an incremental pull encounters it, then it retains existing hydration behavior, including reuse of an overlap-only bulk row. (glm pass, opus pass)
- **AC-4:** Given multiple older issues with missing historical rows mixed with an issue having a known changed historical ref, when a real or dry-run incremental pull runs, then it warns exactly once about unverified older links, still hydrates the known changed ref, and retains the original incremental fetch cursor semantics. (glm partial, opus pass)
- **AC-5:** Given the existing exact-history, NULL-ref, storage-error, decorator-unwrapping and no-history-capability cases, when pre-link detection runs, then their prior outcomes remain unchanged except for the explicitly revised missing-row decision. (glm pass, opus pass)
- **AC-6:** Given a temporary Dolt store with an older linked issue and an unpushed local edit whose pre-sync baseline is removed by compaction, when the next incremental pull uses the original `last_sync`, then the real missing-history response does not trigger hydration and local content remains intact. (glm partial, opus pass)

The grades are for the pipeline's head. The maintainer review commit widened AC-3 to stubs created at `last_sync`, narrowed the AC-4 warning to the issues changed since `last_sync`, and keeps ephemeral and `--no-history` beads out of it (see Changes after the checkpoint pipeline).

## How this was built

- Design: `design.pair` (anthropic-opus, moonshot-kimi, xai-grok, zhipu-glm).
- Independent candidates: glm (pass), opus (pass), pr7296 (no test ran: the triage replay found no test target), pr7502 (no test ran: the triage replay found no test target).
- Judge (grok) composed the change per AC: AC-1 ← opus, AC-2 ← opus, AC-3 ← opus, AC-4 ← opus, AC-5 ← opus, AC-6 ← opus.
- Canonical tests, at the pipeline's head `96fa71fcdc`: `bazel-test //internal/tracker:tracker_test --test_filter='^(TestEnginePullMissingHistory.*|TestEngineExternalRefChangedAfter.*|TestExternalRefHistoryQuerier.*|TestEnginePullOverlap.*|TestDoltStoreCompactPullPreservesLocalEdits)$' --test_env=BEADS_TEST_SKIP= --test_env=BEADS_TEST_DOLT_SERVER=local --test_env=BEADS_TEST_REQUIRE_DOLT_CONTAINER=1` → pass.
- Final review (kimi), at `96fa71fcdc`: pass.
- Maintainer review commit: `bazel-test //internal/tracker:tracker_test` with the same three `--test_env` flags → 268 passed, 0 skipped.

Judge rationale (at `96fa71fcdc`, before the maintainer review commit): Both candidates implement the same design decision table (missing history => changed only when CreatedAt is after lastSync, else historyUnknown, with one warning per pull) and both pass the independent run; opus is tighter per AC. AC-1: opus asserts every local field via reflect.DeepEqual over an edited and an unchanged issue, in both dry-run and real pulls; glm checks only title/description/assignee. AC-2: opus covers the overlap-only and the post-cursor bulk row in both dry-run and real, pinning Candidates=1/Skipped=1, plus the ConflictExternal control; glm runs the post-cursor row as a real pull only. AC-3: opus runs a 3x2 matrix (new stub, older NULL ref, older different ref) x (single fetch, overlap-only row) with no-warning checks; glm has 4 cases. Both fix the TestEnginePullOverlapHydratesPrelinkedStub fixture identically. AC-4: the design requires real and dry-run, and opus runs both orders x both modes; glm runs only real pulls (glm's updatedIDs check is nice but not needed). AC-5: opus's FastPathNotFound table plus a KnownAnswers table (exact/different/NULL ref, error, decorator, no-capability with historyUnknown=false). glm's extra !CreatedAt.IsZero() guard is redundant. AC-6: opus's real-store test was run by the independent check (baseline_compacted_away + baseline_retained passed); it uses deterministic `@@dolt_committer_date` stamps on the shared server and asserts the found=false precondition. glm's AC-6 was never run by the independent command, uses wall-clock time.Sleep (which the design forbids), and starts its own container. CHANGELOG: opus is concise and correct; glm's names a nonexistent 'bd dolt flatten' and claims compact date preservation, which the design says not to promise. glm's [-] commit 9d289a4 (TestCompactReplayKeepsCommitDates) is not ported: base 5294d68 already preserves replay dates and tests it (TestCompactRestoresCommitMetadata, TestEmbeddedCompactKeepsReplayedCommitDates), the change is out of scope per the design, and it sleeps 2s. Contributor PRs: pr7296's date-preserving replay already landed in main, and pr7502 (compact main-moved race) addresses a different defect; neither covers any AC, so there is nothing to port.

title: Compile-time and coordinator-chain boxes left from the admission-by-burn issue (the burn governors were deleted 2026-11-11)
body:
Sweep 2026-11-12: the burn governor, circuit breaker, pooled reserve, operational floor and urgent cap this issue asked for were built and then deleted with every usage limiter (6c05a0836f, 62d3d1e046, 901b7ac8a1, ca46cb96f9 on origin/main; the `north usage` verb is gone), so the spend rule alone decides whether a worker starts. What is left here: the coordinator chain and posture boxes under "Three jobs" and the compile-time boxes. Capacity, host and laptop-load boxes moved to north#1036, disk boxes to north#1258; the build-time boxes wait on the build-once decision in north#1115 (Buck2).

Class: worker admission counts sessions instead of reading burn. `spend_worker_cap` (harness/defaults.toml, consumers crates/north-pace/src/spend/mod.rs, counted in crates/north-fleet-store/src/store/sessions.rs `refuse_past`) refuses any Claude launch once 5 sessions are `starting` or `working` fleet-wide. A count says nothing about spend: an idle-waiting Opus and a building Fable count the same, ghost rows count (2026-11-10: three never-started dispatch rows on gex45 filled the cap), and the coordinator spent the day working around refusals with retry loops while accounts had week to spare. Tom decided on 2026-11-10 that worker spawns are not limited by a fixed number: admission reads burn rate against the approved budget, with a circuit breaker, and otherwise spawns.
Spec: judged
Scope: cross-module

The burn machinery already exists beside the count: the pooled reserve and floor, `spend_trip_fleet_points` (the five-hour burn tripwire) and each account's window outlook in `north fleet usage`. The count is the only part that refuses without a reading.

Done when:
- [x] `spend_worker_cap` and every count-based worker refusal (the Claude cap and the DeepSeek session cap) are deleted with their config, callers and docs; Done when: `rg -n 'spend_worker_cap|spend cap:' crates src harness docs` prints nothing, and 12 concurrent Claude launches on an account with week and five-hour room all start; Evidence: `rg -n 'spend_worker_cap|spend cap:' crates src harness docs` passed on main d29de10ca4b8 on 2026-11-10, exit 1.
- [x] admission is one burn governor per account: a launch is admitted when the account's projected use at its next five-hour and weekly reset, at the measured fleet burn rate plus the new worker's expected charge, stays inside the approved budget (the reserve floor kept for the privacy judge, lander and canaries); the refusal names the account, the projection and the reset time; Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-pacing -E 'test(/admission_is_one_burn_governor_per_account/)'` exits 0 Evidence: `cargo nextest run -p north-pacing -E 'test(/admission_is_one_burn_governor_per_account/)'` passed on main d403b5593344 on 2026-11-10, exit 0.
- [x] a circuit breaker trips an account when its measured burn over the last 15 minutes would exhaust its five-hour window before reset, refuses new launches on it only, and closes on its own when the burn drops back; trips and closes are ledger rows the coordinator sees in the hourly digest, not pages; Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-pacing -E 'test(/a_circuit_breaker_trips_an_account_whose_fifteen_minute_burn_would_exhaust_its_window/)'` exits 0; Evidence: `cargo nextest run -p north-pacing -E 'test(/a_circuit_breaker_trips_an_account_whose_fifteen_minute_burn_would_exhaust_its_window/)'` passed (1 passed), landed as e68d1b99c0f1 on origin/main, 2026-11-10. Evidence: `cargo nextest run -p north-pacing -E 'test(/a_circuit_breaker_trips_an_account_whose_fifteen_minute_burn_would_exhaust_its_window/)'` passed on main f91c907968bd on 2026-11-11, exit 0.
- [x] An account whose week resets before, or within one hour after, its five-hour window resets is never tripped by the burn breaker's five-hour exhaust projection, because exhausting that window costs nothing its week would keep: on 2026-11-11 from 3:55 AM `trip` in crates/north-pace/src/spend/tripwire.rs tripped claude:e on that projection, so dispatch put every worker on d while e held 28 week points that its 10:00 AM weekly reset discards. The fleet-share and week rules still trip it. A test sees two urgent launches admitted past a holding governor, a third queue, and a normal launch still queue. title: fix(dolt): stop replaying a pooled read that ran its read deadline
body:
## Summary

In server mode bd gives every read from the Dolt server a per-I/O deadline (`dolt.pool-read-timeout` / `BEADS_DOLT_POOL_READ_TIMEOUT`, default 10s). When a pooled read ran past it, the MySQL driver closed the socket and returned `invalid connection`, and bd's managed retry sent the read again, up to three sends in about 30 seconds, while the server could still be running the first. Each resend could leave one more session busy on the server (#5258).

This PR stops that replay on the pooled read paths: `withReadTx`, `queryContext` and `queryRowContext`. An attempt that failed with `invalid connection` after running the deadline, or with a network read timeout, becomes a `*storage.ReadTimeoutError`. Neither the managed retry nor an outer `withRetryTxOn` replays it, and it counts once toward the circuit breaker. Its message names the operation, the deadline and both settings. It says "possible" when bd inferred the timeout from elapsed time, because the driver dropped the cause, and "pool read timed out" when the error kept a network read-timeout cause. A fast `invalid connection` (a stale pooled socket) is still retried. `bd list` exits 1 with empty stdout and one `Error:` line, with or without `--json`.

From the pipeline's design: the candidates agree on retry amplification but disagree about the returned error and JSON-only wisp probes; current code supports Opus on those facts. Neither establishes the original wedge or proves elapsed time identifies a socket timeout. Adopt the smaller read-only mitigation, distinguish confirmed from suspected timeouts, and retain exit code 1. Server reaping and downstream error laundering remain with their owners.

## Prior art and credit

- #6220 by ckumar1 (for #6219) introduced the discriminator this PR uses: elapsed time against the read deadline, read back off the store's own DSN with `mysql.ParseDSN`. #6220 applies it at schema init, whose production callers run over a pool with no read deadline, and names adopting it on the pooled path as the next step. This PR is that pooled-path adoption. As #6220's review asked, a DSN that does not parse disables the classifier, and an inferred timeout is worded "possible" instead of naming one cause.
- #6483 by A3Ackerman proposed the error that names `BEADS_DOLT_POOL_READ_TIMEOUT` / `dolt.pool-read-timeout`.
- #6168 asked to document both pool deadlines. The configuration reference now has both rows.

Those threads keep a deadline kill retryable and leave changing that to "a separate, measured decision". This PR makes that change for pooled reads: it does not replay a read that ran its deadline, because each replay can leave another session on the server.

Refs #6219, #6483, #6168

## Maintainer review commit (prepared, not pushed)

The adoption review of this PR prepared one maintainer review commit on top of this head, but did not push it: the review loop ran out of passes while the prior-art follow-up was still open (an explanation and credit on #6220 and a landing order for it, and the retry-policy decision on #6219 or #6483). The PR head is the pipeline head, so it does not have these changes yet:

- Here `withReadTx` classifies a `BeginTx` failure too, although only a pool wait, a login or `START TRANSACTION` was in flight there, never the read. The commit keeps the `BeginTx` retry, as on main, and times the callback from after `BeginTx`, so a slow begin followed by a fast stale-socket reset is retried too. Two `TestPooledReadTimeoutPolicy` subtests pin both, and each fails against the mutant it pins.
- Here a network read timeout counts as confirmed ("pool read timed out"), even when it failed fast. The pinned driver keeps one only from a TLS handshake, while a new connection logs in and before any query is sent. The commit gives it the same elapsed-versus-deadline test as `invalid connection` and the same "possible" wording, and removes `ReadTimeoutError.Confirmed`. `TestPoolReadTimeoutTLSHandshakeStall` drives the real driver against a server that offers TLS and never answers the client's hello.
- The commit reads the pool's read deadline from the store's DSN (`connStr`, which every pool rebuild reuses) when a read fails, instead of from a field that `newServerMode` sets. `TestReadTimeoutErrorNamesTheLoadedKnobs` sets both settings through `storage.PoolReadTimeoutEnv` and `storage.PoolReadTimeoutConfig`, the names the error prints, and checks that `applyPoolKnobs` reads them. `applyPoolKnobs` itself stays as on main, so contributor PR #7568's change to the same lines applies cleanly.
- A tripwire for the stacked PRs under Limitations: against a server that answers `SELECT @@autocommit` with 1, `GetConfig` and the text `bd list` page send a read that fails past the deadline once, and return the typed error.
- `isRetryableError`'s comment claims only what the predicate controls: no loop that consults it retries the typed error.
- Docs: here the troubleshooting entry says that a read command that fails keeps stdout empty, with or without `--json`, which holds only for `bd list`. The commit describes the failure output per command: `bd ready` and `bd count` with `--json` print a JSON error object on stdout. `bd show` usually reports a failed ID lookup on stderr as `Error fetching <id>:`, but a timed-out lookup can also end as `Issue <id> not found` (for an ID whose prefix contains `_`), so neither that nor the `no issues found` object it then prints under `--json` proves the issue is gone. After the lookup, its label, dependency and comment reads are best effort: a timeout there leaves that part out and exits 0, so a missing list or a count of `0` does not prove the issue has none. It also documents the server-pause case, what "possible" covers (a stalled login or TLS handshake included), that a command that looks an issue up by ID can still make several different reads, `bd import`'s 5m read default, and that waiting for a statement's reply counts against the read deadline, not the write deadline. It adds the CHANGELOG `Fixed` entry, which this head lacks.
- `gofmt` on `cmd/bd/list_read_timeout_test.go`: this head fails `//scripts/repochecks:fmt_test`.

## Limitations

- #5258's first ask stays open: what wedged the `--json` query, and why a restart cleared it. So does server-side session reaping. A read that hits the deadline can still leave its one session on the server, where resends could leave up to three.
- A server pause longer than the deadline (for example a long automatic garbage collection) now fails the read instead of succeeding on a resend. Raising the deadline avoids it.
- The clock includes taking a connection: in `queryContext` and `queryRowContext`, and here in `withReadTx` too, where it includes `BeginTx`. So a pool wait or a login (a TLS handshake included) that stalls past the deadline is classified too and not retried, although no query was sent. The unpushed commit above closes this for `withReadTx`.
- Writes (`execContext`, and `withRetryTxOn` statements before the commit) still resend a statement whose response read hit the deadline.
- Landing order with an approved contributor stack by scarson: #8236 adds a `withSingleRead` helper and moves `GetConfig` and several other config and metadata reads onto it, and #8237 moves the text `bd list` page and several other one-statement reads onto it. On a server that autocommits, as a default `dolt sql-server` does, the helper sends the read through `withRetry` alone and never calls `classifyPooledRead`, so once both stacks land those reads are sent again, as in #5258. Each PR merges cleanly with this one, so nothing forces the fix: whichever lands second must classify that read (`start := time.Now()`, then `return s.classifyPooledRead(ctx, fn(s.db), start, "")`). On the merge of the unpushed commit with #8237, which carries #8236, the tripwire above fails (the read is sent 4 times before its 5-second context ends) and passes with that change. #8238 and #8242 are stacked on #8236, and #8242 reads routing settings through the same helper.
- `bd serve` and the proxied-server route are unchanged. Both read through the unit-of-work provider's pool, whose DSN (`util.DoltServerDSN`) sets no read deadline and which never calls the classifier, so neither ever returns `*storage.ReadTimeoutError`, and `bd serve` cannot turn one into the retryable 503 `db_unavailable` that its HTTP client replays. A stalled served read is bounded by the request's 60-second deadline instead, and `bd serve` answers an expired deadline with a 500, which the client does not replay. Other served replay is out of scope here: the HTTP client still resends a read once when its response headers take longer than 15 seconds (`wire.DefaultResponseHeaderTimeout`).
- A command that looks an issue up by ID (`bd show`, `bd update` and the others that resolve IDs through `utils.ResolvePartialID`) still makes several different lookup reads: the resolver drops a failed exact-ID search and both prefix config reads and moves on to the next lookup. Each read is sent once, but on a stalled server each can run the deadline and leave a session behind. The unpushed commit's troubleshooting entry says so.

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | Criterion | glm | opus |
|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | Given a pooled read failing with invalid connection after its read deadline elapses, when each covered helper handles it, then it runs once and returns ReadTimeoutError with Confirmed=false, operation context, effective deadline, both override names and uncertain wording. | partial | pass |
| AC-2 | Given a fast stale-connection failure followed by success, when the pooled helper runs, then existing retry recovery succeeds without a ReadTimeoutError. | pass | pass |
| AC-3 | Given a classified failure and a breaker, when managed retry handles it, then exactly one failure is recorded and errors.As survives a breaker-trip wrapper. | pass | pass |
| AC-4 | Given a list reader returning the typed error, when JSON or text list runs, then code is 1, stdout is empty, and one application Error line conveys the operation, deadline, qualifier and configuration guidance. | pass | pass |
| AC-5 | Given a MySQL fake that completes setup but withholds SELECT, when the real pinned driver reads with a short deadline, then it submits one SELECT, closes that connection and returns the typed suspected error without resubmission. | pass | pass |
| AC-6 | Given the configuration/troubleshooting docs, when a user consults them, then both read/write knobs and 10s defaults, per-I/O semantics, inferred diagnosis and failure-versus-empty distinction are documented. | pass | pass |

The table grades the pipeline head, which is this PR's head. The unpushed maintainer review commit would remove AC-1's `Confirmed` field (see above), so that every classified failure is worded "possible".

## How this was built

- Design: `design.pair` (anthropic-opus, moonshot-kimi, xai-grok, zhipu-glm).
- Independent candidates: glm (pass), opus (pass).
- Judge (grok) composed the change per AC: AC-1 ← merge, AC-2 ← opus, AC-3 ← opus, AC-4 ← opus, AC-5 ← opus, AC-6 ← opus.
  - AC-1: merged by the integrator: opus 355435ddd890 verbatim (`internal/storage/read_timeout_error.go`, `internal/storage/dolt/pooled_read_timeout.go`, the `store.go` `poolReadTimeout` field and classify calls, the `isRetryableError` guard, `pooled_read_timeout_test.go`), plus only glm f153d00ab8ee's `TestIsRetryableError` row, the one test that fails if the outer-replay guard is removed.
- Canonical tests on the pipeline head: `bazel-test //internal/storage/dolt:dolt_test //cmd/bd:bd_test //test/docsync:docsync_test --test_filter='^(TestPooledReadTimeoutPolicy|TestClassifyPooledReadFailure|TestPoolReadTimeoutFromDSN|TestPooledReadStaleConnectionRetry|TestPooledReadTimeoutBreakerAccounting|TestPoolReadTimeoutClosesSocketOnce|TestListReadTimeoutStderrContract|TestPoolReadTimeoutDocs|TestIsRetryableError)$'` → pass.
- Final review (kimi): pass.
- Unpushed maintainer review commit, run locally (GitHub CI has graded only this head): the same filter plus `TestApplyConfigDefaultsAppliesPoolTimeoutLadder`, `TestPoolReadTimeoutTLSHandshakeStall` and `TestReadTimeoutErrorNamesTheLoadedKnobs` → pass. The whole `//internal/storage/dolt:dolt_test`, `//internal/storage:storage_test`, `//cmd/bd:bd_test`, `//test/docsync:docsync_test` and `//scripts/repochecks:fmt_test` targets and the CHANGELOG and docs gates pass under `--config=ci`, where the Dolt-backed tests skip. Mutants that leave the TLS-handshake timeout unclassified, skip the elapsed test for a network read timeout, or rename the loader's setting names each fail the new tests. `TestPoolReadTimeoutDocs` also requires the `bd show` wording; the earlier docs fail it.

Judge rationale: Both candidates passed the independent run and share one design shape; no behavioural ambiguity in the design. AC-1: opus's classifier follows the design exactly (errors.Is ErrInvalidConn or exact ': invalid connection' suffix, ctx.Err() check, no re-wrap of an already-typed error), and its tests drive the real SearchIssuesWithCounts (healthy wisp probe then a slow reset) through a scripted driver, pin connection-reset and mid-text matches as unclassified, and keep a deterministic classifier table. glm also classifies slow 'connection reset' and any substring 'invalid connection', which the design rules out (partial), and its counts case fakes the operation text instead of calling SearchIssuesWithCounts. Merge adds glm's TestIsRetryableError row, which covers design step 5's outer-replay guard that no opus test exercises. AC-2/AC-3: equivalent; opus's tests fit its field/helper names and run withReadTx through SearchIssuesWithCounts, including the breaker trip via errors.As. AC-4: opus counts Error: lines and lets driver log lines through, as the design allows; glm demands stderr be exactly one line (brittle) and hard-codes its own 'read transaction:' wrapper. AC-5: both are sound loopback fakes; opus derives the deadline through the real buildServerDSN and matches its code; glm's extra conn/timing asserts add little once SELECT count and typed-error checks hold. AC-6: opus's docs quote the message opus's code actually prints, spell out exit 1/empty stdout vs '[]', avoid restart advice, and add a docsync guard; glm's example quotes a 'read transaction:' prefix that opus's code does not produce.
