title: Landing queue p90 from 38 min toward 60 s: one owner for the number, by design
body:
Spec: judged
Scope: cross-module
The readiness scoreboard's landing queue p90 bar targets at most 60 s; on 2026-11-08 at 10:03 AM it read 38 min over 1 h (n=21), 35 min over 3 h and 30 min over 24 h. Lanes wait for whole probe rounds of 12 to 28 lanes that take about 10 min each, a red or conflicting lane costs the rest a round, and every requeue starts the wait again. The pieces under north#842, north#892 and north#634 each shave part of this; nobody owns the number end to end. Tom asked for substantial, structural improvement here (2026-11-08).

This issue owns the number: find where each minute of the p90 goes from the landing spans, decide the design that can reach minutes rather than tens of minutes (for example landing a lane on its pre-queue verdict when nothing it depends on changed since, checking lanes alone in parallel and streaming them in instead of rounds), and land it, coordinating with the owners of the existing lanes rather than duplicating them.

## Done when
- [x] docs/rationale names where the 1 h landing queue p90 went, by stage, from the land-queue spans, with the command that reproduces it — landed 7eb919bb99 on origin/main as docs/rationale/landing-queue-p90.md: of the lane wait, 48% was rounds that did not land the lane, 21% waiting for a round and 19% the landing round
- [ ] Not before 2026-11-11T15:00Z (two separate hours of the landing-queue reading cannot both pass inside a day, and the dash bars read the laptop's live records): `north ledger scoreboard` shows landing queue p90 over 1 h at or below 10 min in two separate hours Done when: `north dash --bars --all | rg 'landing queue.*p90.*PASS'` exits 0 in two separate hours Needs: laptop.
- [x] `north ledger scoreboard` shows landing queue p90 over 1 h at or below 60 s in one hour, or the issue names the next design step with its measured gap Done when: `north dash --bars --all | sed -n '/^north:/,/^$/p' | rg -q '^landing queue p90 +<= 60 s +PASS'` exits 0 in one hour (rewritten 2026-11-11: the old pattern also matched the target column of a FAIL line and the makgora section) Needs: laptop. Checked: `north dash --bars --all | sed -n '/^north:/,/^$/p' | rg -q '^landing queue p90 +<= 60 s +PASS'` judged this box's command exit 0 on main af45e9dc2b on 2026-11-11 at 4:24 AM on whiterabbit: north's bar read PASS, 35 s (n=11) over 1 h.


## Execution of north#842's design (swarm, 2026-11-08; qp90-lead)
The design is north#842's Design section plus verdict reuse and north#634; the measured split is docs/rationale/landing-queue-p90.md. Each step lands with its replay, then live:
- [x] Probes select tests/it modules by their lanes' affected crates instead of the whole suite (north#634; worker q902-select) — landed 2af69a88d on origin/main; measured 0% saved (138.2 s before, 141.5 s after on a recorded probe) because 38 of 46 modules launch the north binary; the real narrowing is change-to-test edges, north#916, offered to north#917
- Dropped (2026-11-08): design step 1, footprint sub-queues (worker q902-subq, stopped) — every one of the 53 crates is in the root package's dependency closure, so a crate footprint splits nothing; the narrowing moves to change-to-test edges under north#917
- Parked (2026-11-08): design step 3, backup bets on spare slots (worker q902-bets, committed 0c6d39622, unqueued) — the review order puts it after the alone pass and failure-signature blame, and land-first removes the rounds it hedges
- [x] Design steps 4 and 5, refusal-rate stride and urgent first, wired into the lander (worker q902-batch) — landed 29f4b439a5 on origin/main; the 11:15 AM round planned probes of 5, 5, 4, 5 and 6 lanes plus a probe of 1 for the urgent ticket, where the 10:20 AM round planned up to 36; the joiner cap and suspects probed alone follow as q902-pace f7fa4fa48e
- [x] Design step 7, a round never plans more probe jobs than the build hosts' free slots (worker q902-slots) — landed 3480ca0e53 on origin/main: the slot read counts what each build host's job cap leaves after its running and queued jobs, and the replay of the 10:20 AM reading offers 0 of 9 slots where the old read offered 33; one offload job per probe follows as n842-onejob bf122714f
- [x] Pre-queue checks wait in an ordered line for a build host instead of refusing with exit 75 for capacity or an ssh drop (worker q902-prequeue) — landed efa4b83479 on origin/main: replay enqueue_reruns_a_check_before_queueing_on_another_build_host_when_the_first_host_drops_its_connection fails on the old source (exit 75 refusal) and passes; every-host-full wait is a paused-clock unit test in north-land-checks
- [x] Lander watchdog pages and lander notices reach the lander's live owner, with the proxy as fallback (worker q902-alarm; from scratch/n892-addressee) — landed 89ab826db on origin/main: the watchdog and ownerless conflict notices go to land_notice::OWNER while a live or parked session holds that name, else to the proxy prefixed with the name and logged once in .dead-letters.jsonl
- [x] Verdict-reuse runner lands first and urgent, starting the 100-landing shadow clock (n842-reuse / n842-runner) (landed 13cf1918ed on origin/main at 04:05 UTC on 2026-11-08: every nextest land line runs under `north land reuse observe` and logs the set it would reuse beside the real verdict)
- Superseded (2026-11-08) by land-first, which deletes the probe rounds, and by the graph-consumers box below, which blames an after-landing red by `north graph ask blame --log` before bisecting (lane q902-blame 1171de37d1, held, edits only north-land-probes): red probes are blamed by failure signature: a failing check or test that appears in every red probe is traced to the lanes those probes share, minus lanes a green probe carried, and probes failing different signatures are blamed separately (worker q902-blame)


- [x] Already decided by Tom (2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06, docs/rationale/landing-train.md "Land first, test after"): landing takes 10 to 20 s, and checks that need not block the push run after it, with the sheriff bisecting and reverting a red batch. Build it so it is safe at today's failure rate: a lane enters the queue only after it passes alone (gates, build, its changed crates' clippy and tests) on a main at most N landings old, so what can still go red after landing is only interaction between lanes; the merged-tree check moves after the push; a red after-landing run bisects and reverts the culprit. Measured by queue p90 at most 60 s and reverts per landing. (landed 2649c5a3a283)
  - Queued 2026-11-08 as ticket q902-deadcode 47e625b1d3 (urgent; the land-first commit ec8677d63 plus its dead-code follow-up); refused at 1:10 PM by the lander's privacy judge on the rationale paragraph it added, which its own pre-queue privacy run had passed; requeued without that paragraph
- [x] Land-first follow-up, one landing after q902-landfirst lands (owner q902-landfirst): delete the code nothing calls once the probe rounds are gone (bisect::Strikes and escalate, the base-broken pause in pause::raise, north-check-environment's judge and Reading), and make land_first.rs wait through wait::until — landed with land-first as 7e285c4f35

- [x] Graph consumer, test selection (worker q902-gselect, on north-graph-change from north#917): every land check's test selection, before queueing and in the after-landing run over the batch's range, asks `north graph ask affected BASE HEAD` for the tests a range can affect and always runs the tests it adds; exit 3 or 2 falls back to today's crate-level selection. Scoping the after-landing run to overlap's pairwise intersections waits until the alone pass runs each lane's affected tests before queueing, because under land-first a lane's own tests first run after the push (qp90-lead, 2026-11-08) (landed f7c70fdfe504)
- [x] Graph consumer, culprit search (worker q902-gblame, on north-graph-change from north#917): a red after-landing run asks `north graph ask blame --log RUN_LOG LANE...` (or --failed) before bisecting: one lane named reverts that lane, several bisect only among them, exit 3 bisects the whole batch as today (landed 8c7407743ed1)

- [ ] Warm build per slot (staffed after q902-gblame queues): each build slot keeps its cargo target across lander runs, trimmed by size and never wiped, so an after-landing run recompiles only what its batch changed. On 2026-11-08 n842-classify's probe compiled 235 crates and g917-change's 77, and the lander logged 'land clean: removed …/lander-probe-0/target (15233 MiB)'. Done when the lander journal shows no slot target removed whole over an hour of at least 15 landings, and an after-landing run of a one-crate batch compiles no crate outside that crate's reverse dependencies (its log's Compiling lines) Done when: `[ "$(journalctl --user -u north-land@north.service --since -1h -o cat | rg -o 'lane (\S+) landed' -r '$1' | sort -u | wc -l)" -ge 15 ] && test -z "$(journalctl --user -u north-land@north.service --since -1h -o cat | rg 'land clean: removed .*/target')"` exits 0 over an hour of at least 15 landings Needs: laptop. A DeepSeek session cannot do this box: it is read from the lander's journal over an hour of landings, a host service.
- [ ] Verdict reuse shadow, moved from north#842 on 2026-11-08 (roadmap review): for at least 100 landings after 13cf1918ed the lander computes which tests it would reuse and still runs them, and reused and real verdicts disagree 0 times. Done when: `north land reuse report --since 7d` on the lander host prints at least 100 landings and 0 disagreements. Needs: laptop.
  - [x] Code half of the reuse shadow box above (split 2026-11-11 by land-lead): since 13cf1918ed the shadow would reuse 0 of 639174 units over 786 landings (`north land reuse report --since 62h` on the lander host, 2026-11-11 4:40 AM), so its 0 disagreements prove nothing; the cause is found and fixed, and a recorded pass whose inputs match is reused by the shadow again. - [ ] Tests: the gate records a session's own `cargo nextest run` the same way, keyed by tree, package and test filter plus the runtime identity the nextest land line's key already hashes, and the enqueue alone pass and after-landing run reuse it. Done when: `north land reuse report` shows at least 50% of test-seconds reused with 0 disagreements over an hour of at least 15 landings, and cpuSeconds per landed lane drops against the 24 h before (read from the land-queue spans). Needs: laptop.







## Moved from north#1057 on 2026-11-10 (Take generated registries out of lanes: docs/features.md, help.txt, reference.txt, verb tables and structure.toml's module map come from per-unit files)
Landing speed: generated-registry conflicts cost landing rounds.

- [x] Each generated registry is built from per-unit source files at build or land time and never appears in a worker's diff: `docs/features.md`, `src/cli/help.txt`, `src/cli/reference.txt`, the verb tables and `structure.toml`'s module map. Check: a lane changing a command or module leaves these files unchanged in `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`, and the build writes them. Done when: `test -z "$(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- docs/features.md src/cli/help.txt src/cli/reference.txt structure.toml)" && ! git ls-files --error-unmatch docs/features.md 2>/dev/null` exits 0 — Evidence (2026-11-11, origin/main bffcfdbc1e): the Done-when command exits 0; `docs/features.md` is untracked; `build.rs` writes `src/cli/reference.txt`, `src/cli/verbs.rs` and `structure.toml` from their per-unit trees, `north docs help-index` and the lander write `src/cli/help.txt`, and `north land scan generated-registry` (crates/north-land-scans/src/generated_registry.rs) refuses a lane that commits one.
- [x] The land gate refuses a worker commit that edits a generated registry by hand and names the source file to edit instead. Check: a test replays a lane touching `docs/features.md` and sees the refusal, and `north land scan` lists the gate. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-land-checks -E 'test(/a_hand_edit_of_a_generated_registry_is_refused_naming_its_source/)' && north land scan 2>&1 | rg -q 'generated-registry'` exits 0 (check rewritten 2026-11-11 by land-lead: `north land scan` prints its gate list on stderr, so the pipe read nothing) Checked: cargo nextest run -p north-land-checks -E 'test(/a_hand_edit_of_a_generated_registry_is_refused_naming_its_source/)' && north land scan 2>&1 | rg -q 'generated-registry' judged this box's command exit 0 on main 6179709333 on 2026-11-11 (landed as b44e5fceb8; run by land-lead on cpx62b) Needs: none (code only: its check is a test that runs on any build host; added 2026-11-11 by land-lead, since a laptop need recorded on nexus for this issue's other boxes held it off the build hosts).
  Checked: `cargo nextest run -p north-land-checks -E 'test(/a_hand_edit_of_a_generated_registry_is_refused_naming_its_source/)' && north land scan | rg -q generated-registry` judged this box's command exit 0 on main b44e5fceb8 on 2026-11-11 (the scan listing read through `./bin/head-north --code crates/north-land-scans/src/` because the installed runtime had not yet been promoted to the landed code)
- [x] The generated files are stale-proof: `north docs features-index` and the build that writes `help.txt`, `reference.txt` and `structure.toml`'s module map exit 0 on main with `git status --porcelain` empty. Check: run them on main and capture the exit code. Done when: `north docs features-index && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"` exits 0 Checked: `north docs features-index && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"` judged this box's command exit 0 on main 3b16e3aee on 2026-11-11 in a fresh clone on cpx62, and in the same clone `./bin/land-shell --dev -- cargo check --locked --offline -p north` (the build script that writes src/cli/help.txt, src/cli/reference.txt and structure.toml) exited 0 with `git status --porcelain` still empty.
- [ ] Lander-conflict rows per 100 landings fall: the strategy's baseline (37 of 85 conflicts on 2026-11-08) is re-read over 7 days after the change (not before 2026-11-17T13:00Z). Check: `north dash --weekly` conflict reading and the lander's `land.conflict` rows. Done when: `north dash --weekly | rg -q 'conflict'` exits 0 and the reading is below 37 of 85 Needs: laptop.




## Lanes held out by aged alone passes (2026-11-10, n902-batch-rate)

- [x] A lane whose pass for its head has aged joins the next candidate instead of waiting for a serial alone check. Measured from the north lander journal, 2:14 to 4:11 PM (+07) on 2026-11-10: the serving loop spent 44.8 of 117 minutes in seven one-lane alone checks (1.9, 9.4, 7.7, 11.2, 8.0, 3.0, 3.6 min), five of them for passes that had only aged; at 4:12 PM 18 of 18 queued tickets were 7 to 40 first-parent commits past their pass against `landing.alone-pass-landings` = 5, which one 9-lane batch exhausts; 48 h: 7 aged-pass rechecks, 5 green, 2 red; two runtime restarts killed checks of 11.2 and 3.0 min. Lane n902-batch-rate (5c8ca6645b) drops pass age from admission; the after-landing run still runs a lane's whole selection when its pass is older than the setting. Done when: the three lander rounds after it is live each carry every queued lane that has a pass for its head (journal `candidate ... carries N lanes` against the queue count). Done when: `journalctl --user -u 'north-land@north.service' --since '-1 h' -o cat | rg 'candidate .* carries [0-9]+ lanes' | tail -3 | wc -l | rg -q '^3$'` exits 0 Landed 1478c3cc68 on origin/main, live in the lander from 4:42 PM on cb929a45e8: rounds of 13 lanes (4:50 PM, 18 queued at round start, 3 conflicts, 1 deferred behind a lane ahead on its files), 13 lanes (4:52 PM, 1 conflict, 2 deferred) and 1 lane (4:58 PM, after the queue drained to 0 at 4:53 PM); no lane waited for an alone check in any of them. Follow-up d2428ad059 steps a lane aside after two no-verdict alone checks on one head.
- [x] An alone check (a lane with no pass for its head) never holds the round: lanes with a pass form and land their batch while the alone check runs beside it on another build host, and a runtime restart adopts or keeps an alone check in flight instead of discarding it. At 4:15 to 4:20 PM on 2026-11-10 ds-1057-x's alone check held 22 queued lanes with nothing landing; n1039-blame's checks ran on gex45 for 7.7, 11.2 and 8.0 min each. Done when: the lander journal shows a candidate pushed while an alone check is in flight, in a replay that fails with the check run inline. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-lander -E 'test(/a_candidate_is_pushed_while_an_alone_check_is_in_flight/)'` exits 0 Needs: none (code only: its check is a test that runs on any build host; added 2026-11-11 by land-lead). The test lives in north-lander, where the serve loop is, so the command names that crate. Evidence: `cargo nextest run -p north-lander -E 'test(/a_candidate_is_pushed_while_an_alone_check_is_in_flight/)'` passed on main c96dda75cad2fab1915f4970e6bf6f4494c21922 on 2026-11-11, exit 0.


- [ ] A lander fix reaches the lander within one landing round, not one promotion cycle. On 2026-11-10 the lander link moved twice in the hour to 4:25 PM (fa30c0ecf6 at 3:46 PM, 45e6055dfe at 4:03 PM) and read 3 landings and 26 min behind current at 4:25 PM: each `north land promote` replays the recorded rounds and shadows the queue for 3 min (6 passes), about 15 to 20 min, while promote-on-landing (e068c4c057) moves current about every 15 min. It keeps up with one cycle of lag rather than stalling; over the whole of /home/tom/.local/state/north/runtime-follow.log, 554 promotions followed, 39 were refused because current moved during the candidate's replay, and 120 times the newest runtime replayed next after a finished replay. Done when: the lander link is at most one landing behind current over an hour of at least 15 landings, read from the lander doctor's 'runs runtimes/X, N landing(s) behind' line. Done when: `north land doctor | rg -q 'runs runtimes/.*, [01] landings? behind'` exits 0 after at least 15 landings in an hour Needs: laptop. A DeepSeek session cannot do this box: it is read from the lander host after 15 landings in an hour.
  - [x] Code half: the lander link moves to the newest passed runtime while an older runtime's replay still runs. On 2026-11-11 at about 5:43 AM the doctor read the link 17 landings and 33 min behind current (0bd8f8a8 against b5744d7b), though the land-first move above (3cf35e8dc4) is in both runtimes involved. `follow_lander` in crates/north-runtime/src/runtime/follow.rs holds lander-promote.lock for a whole `north land promote`: a recorded-round replay plus a 3 min shadow, allowed 30 min. pid 611710 had run 22 min, under a `north runtime promote` of 3b16e3ae that had run 62 min. Every newer promotion that finds the lock held returns at once ("another promotion holds lander-promote.lock and replays the newest runtime when its replay ends"), so the link moves only between replays while landings arrive every few minutes. The link move for the newest passed runtime takes only a short lock, and no replay of an older runtime holds it back. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-runtime -E 'test(/a_newer_runtime_moves_the_lander_link_while_an_older_replay_runs/)'` exits 0 Needs: none (code only: a test on any build host; added 2026-11-11 by land-lead; the parent's doctor reading stays the laptop's) Taken 2026-11-11 by the running session cpx62-n1022-page-live as its next task after its north#1022 page box, reused because no account admitted a new Claude launch that day (claude:d held by its burn governor, claude:e's window spent, the API reserve limited to operational callers); the queued launch cpx62b-n902-link-lock is for the same box. Checked: `cargo nextest run -p north-runtime -E 'test(/a_newer_runtime_moves_the_lander_link_while_an_older_replay_runs/)'` judged this box's command exit 0 on main e985a49be on 2026-11-10
  - [x] The lander link moves to the newest current runtime as soon as that runtime's canary has passed, and the recorded-round replay and shadow judge it afterwards. A divergence the held runtime does not share sends the link back to the held runtime and writes lander-refused, the same way the doctor's rollback does. This is the parent box's fix: it applies land-first (docs/rationale/landing-train.md) to the lander link. Measured 2026-11-10 from 9:18 to 10:18 PM by sampling `north land doctor` every 1 to 2 min (/tmp/n902/samples.log on whiterabbit): 35 landings an hour on origin/main. The link read 4 landings behind 5 times, then 14 landings and 27 min behind at 10:17 PM. Each promotion replays 8 recorded rounds. In /home/tom/.local/state/north/runtime-follow.log lines 272204 to 272211, every round recorded landed and replayed failed on both the candidate and the held runtime ("the held runtime replays it the same way"), so that hour the replay held nothing back and cost two replays per round. A fast path for lander-neutral landings alone is not enough: only 36 of the 105 landings in the 3 h to 10:20 PM touched no crate in north-lander's path-dependency closure, src/, Cargo files or tests/it/land. Done when: the parent box's Done-when. Needs: laptop. A DeepSeek session cannot do this box: it changes how the lander host moves its runtime link, a host service. (landed 3cf35e8dc4c2)
  - [x] Recorded-round replays reach the verdict the round recorded: find why `north land replay` of a landed round fails on both runtimes (runtime-follow.log lines 272204 to 272211) and fix the cause, so the after-the-fact replay above is evidence. Done when: the newest `north land promote` block in /home/tom/.local/state/north/runtime-follow.log has at least half its rounds ending `replayed landed: matches`. Needs: laptop. (landed 665dcc4cd388)
  - [x] A queued `north runtime promote` whose candidate is no longer current exits instead of waiting 600 s on runtime-promote.lock. At 10:19 PM, 5 waiters for 43ec2f7cfb were alive after current had moved on. Done when: `pgrep -fc '[n]orth runtime promote'` reads at most 2 in each of 10 samples taken 1 min apart during an hour of at least 15 landings. (The pattern is bracketed since 2026-11-10: the plain form also counted the sampling shell and any session quoting the text, and read 3 in ten samples while three bracketed checks found 0 promote processes.) Evidence (2026-11-10): `pgrep -fc '[n]orth runtime promote'` read 1 1 2 2 2 2 1 1 1 1 in ten samples one minute apart; origin/main had 15 landings in the hour (git log --since="1 hour ago"). Fix: e0358bf2d1 and earlier on main.


- [ ] Building a candidate of many lanes takes seconds, not minutes. On 2026-11-10, once lane n902-batch-rate (1478c3cc68) was live, the first round's candidate of 18 queued lanes took 7.7 min to build (4:42:21 to 4:50:02 PM, `journalctl --user -u north-land@north.service`), with no journal output between the first lane's pick-time gates at 4:42 PM and the next lane's at 4:49 PM; the pick-time gates and scans run lane after lane inside the serving loop. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-landing -E 'test(/a_candidate_of_ten_lanes_runs_its_pick_time_gates_outside_the_serving_loop/)'` exits 0, and the lander's spans show candidate build at most 60 s for a candidate of at least 10 lanes, in three rounds. Needs: laptop.
- [x] A fetch or ref-lock failure inside an after-landing check is an infrastructure signature: the check is rerun once before main is called red, and `north land red-check` answers "environment" for it instead of blaming the lane. On 2026-11-10 at 6:08 PM south main was called red at feef10e2e6 because `bash bin/catalog-owner-check` hit `cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/main'` when two fetches raced on one offload checkout; the same check run by hand exits 0, and `north land red-check` said "the failed log names no test; treating it as this lane's failure". Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-lander -E 'test(/a_ref_lock_failure_in_an_after_landing_check_is_rerun_and_judged_environment/)'` exits 0 Evidence: landed as 343ffb8666934b42c2d239e7a820a11bfc42e547 on origin/main (2026-11-10); the Done-when test passed (1 passed) before landing.
- [x] The Cargo workflow's environment step does not turn main red on a package-mirror stall: installing bubblewrap retries or comes from a cached or pinned source, so a runner that cannot reach the apt mirror fails over instead of timing out. On 2026-11-10 at about 6:50 PM the Cargo run on main 91e3999520 (run 42810542459) failed in step `Cargo test environment` with exit 124 while apt fetched bubblewrap from azure.archive.ubuntu.com, and the cover job failed for the missing shard; a rerun of the failed jobs was requested by hand. Done when: `rg -c 'bubblewrap' .github/workflows/*.yml | rg -q . && rg -q 'retry|cache' .github/actions/cargo-test-environment/action.yml` exits 0 (landed be65fe6e5c00: apt install of bubblewrap retries 3 times and is skipped when bwrap is present; action moved to .github/actions/cargo-test-environment)
- [ ] North's after-landing run never compiles on the settling host: on 2026-11-11 at 8:15 AM, with the laptop CPU reserve on and every runtime build already on build hosts, `north land checks --after --dry 1` (runtime bbd09095) ran 7 rustc on the laptop, the last compile left there. Safe-push's land checks for every repository and makgora's and wisp's after-landing runs already offload through `north capacity offload run` to the freest of cpx62, cpx62b and gex45. North's after-landing run takes the same path; when no build host answers, it waits and reports exit 75 instead of compiling on the settling host. Check: over 30 min of north landings, no rustc on the laptop has `north land checks --after` as an ancestor. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-lander -E 'test(/the_after_landing_run_offloads_to_a_build_host/)'` exits 0 on main Needs: none (code half; land-lead reads the laptop check after it lands).















- [ ] Not before 2026-11-11T16:30Z (its check needs a full day of at least 15 landings after the fix 18e683db35; three sessions stopped on it on 2026-11-10, two of them on hosts that cannot read the laptop land records): Flaky tests found by `north land missed` on 2026-11-10 are each fixed at their cause or removed: tests that alternate between "left out" and "also fails on the base" across consecutive main runs (the fleet_tick floor test at 060eaa5e584d, 56e18867c706, d40da46550a8 and 940277eb9abe) fail without any change reaching them, so they are flakes, not selection gaps, and neither a rerun to green nor a weakened assertion counts as the fix. Done when: `north land missed --since 24h --repo /home/tom/code/north/main` lists no test as also failing on the base over a day of at least 15 landings Needs: laptop.

Moved from north#892 on 2026-11-11:
  - [ ] The lander-link test waits on the replay event, not on a time limit: on 2026-11-11 GitHub Cargo failed runtime::follow::tests::a_newer_runtime_moves_the_lander_link_while_an_older_replay_runs on 0b1d7c7ec6 (job test 1/3, crates/north-runtime/src/runtime/follow/tests.rs:49, "the newer runtime was never replayed while the older replay ran", after 16 s on a loaded runner), while the lander's own after-landing run of that commit passed; the test (from e985a49bee) waits for a second replay within a deadline. It is the fourth wall-clock test of the day after ssh_master, the lane-reaping test and the replay budget. The test proves the same ordering by waiting on the replay it starts, with no wall-clock bound, and still fails when the link waits for the older replay. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-runtime -E 'test(/a_newer_runtime_moves_the_lander_link_while_an_older_replay_runs/)' --stress-count 50` exits 0 Needs: none (code only: a test on any build host; added 2026-11-11 by land-lead, red main) Same test and fix as the north-runtime box of #1109 (folded from #1129, 2026-11-12), which owns it.
  - [ ] The wall-time scan also reports a test that hands the code under test a sub-second wall-clock budget: the reaper test above (Duration::from_millis(300) into reap_within) is the fifth wall-clock test to fail main or a batch on 2026-11-11 after ssh_master, the lane-reaping test, the replay budget and the lander-link test, and the scan landed for the measured-duration class does not see a budget passed in. The scan reports that class (with the old reaper line as a recorded fixture, and a budget decided by an injected clock spared), and every existing test it reports on main is converted or names its reason in the scan's allowlist. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-land-checks -E 'test(/wall_time/)'` exits 0 Needs: none (code only: a test on any build host; added 2026-11-11 by land-lead)
  - [ ] The lander blames a lane for a red after-landing run only on a fresh run of that lane's prefix, never on the batch's own red log: on 2026-11-11 at 5:01 AM the bisection of bd34b8ad5f's red run (one lane, n1081-canary) greened only the base deb4f2cb8e and then named the lane red by citing land-check-zJuXk8pFoq.log, the 4:54 AM batch run itself, although the lander's reruns of the same test on 22803418f and a70ac5dd (both containing the lane) passed at 5:02 and 5:03 AM; its revert was not queued only because it no longer reverted cleanly. A test replays that one-lane bisection and sees no blame until a rerun of the lane's prefix fails. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-lander -E 'test(/a_one_lane_batch_is_blamed_only_on_a_rerun_of_its_prefix/)'` exits 0 Needs: none (code only: a test on any build host; added 2026-11-11 by land-lead)
- [ ] Under a playtest-bound desk, agents get the 12-CPU bound while Tom is at the desk and the laptop takes no heavy land checks; away keeps the 22-of-24 quota. Decided 2026-11-10 (gate 213, option 1, chosen by the proxy on Tom's delegation) after the laptop ran at load 76 to 110 (3:05 to 3:36 PM) and 208 (4:46 PM) with agents at 2200% while he worked, and measured 19 of 24 cores and load 26 to 63 under a 12-CPU hold; it costs roughly 45% of laptop agent throughput at the desk until north#1036 moves builds to the servers. `north capacity mode relieve` and the playtest hold work on top of it. Rule landed 69093c66c4 on origin/main (desktop row of capacity_mode_table no longer build-host; replay: `cargo nextest run -p north-capacity -p north-pacing` 53/53 passed); the box stays open until the live check passes with the proxy's temporary hold and relief lapsed. Done when: `north capacity mode status | rg -q 'CPUQuota 1200%' && awk '{exit !($3<24)}' /proc/loadavg` exits 0 Needs: laptop. A DeepSeek session cannot do this box: it sets the laptop's capacity mode, a host service. 2026-11-11 on whiterabbit: the broker (north-worker-outside) and the runtime promote, checkouts and mirror scopes ran in app.slice, outside the 12-CPU quota, compiling rustc there; both now start under agent.slice (7ce08052f9, e999ce4efe). Load stayed 39 to 185 afterwards, mostly D-state threads (143 blocked, io pressure some avg10 77) from rustc of the lander (north-land@north.service) and promote writing to the encrypted disk, which a CPU quota cannot bound; the check also matched 'quota' against status text that prints 'CPUQuota', so it could never pass and now names 'CPUQuota 1200%'. The load half waits on north#1036 moving the lander's builds off the laptop.
- [ ] A lane whose later commit strengthens the test its first commit added passes mutant kill on its whole diff: on 2026-11-11 the build-host launch fix of north#1054 (fix and weak test in 04e39fbe44, stronger test in e772aff25f) was refused twice with "survive all 5 mutant(s)" naming the mutants the second commit's test kills, because `judge_each` in crates/north-land-scans/src/test_admission/kills.rs splits a lane at each commit ("since a lane lands as one commit") and stops at the first refusal; squashing the lane into one commit (88f220be0e) passed at once. A lane is judged on its whole range unless it is a probe of several lanes, so a follow-up commit on the same lane counts. Done when: `cargo nextest run -p north-land-scans -E 'test(/a_lane_whose_second_commit_strengthens_its_test_is_judged_as_one_diff/)'` exits 0 (a test that fails on today's code). Needs: none (added 2026-11-11 by n1054-host-start; it cost two first tries of a break-glass fix)

title: North landing flow: proven stall alerts, no cancelled gex45 land checks, first commit to main under 10 minutes
body:
Class: a landing path that stalls, cancels or delays a lane between its first commit and origin/main.

Split from north#245 (2026-10-30): the North landing-flow boxes that need elapsed time or gex45 landings rather than a code change in one lane. Each box is moved verbatim with its source.

Owner: harness-planner.

## Moved from #20 Landing flow: WIP gate, push-to-land time and landing-stall alerts

- [ ] The laptop timer `agents-flow-stall` has run for a day, and every stall it reported was real.
- [ ] time-gated: one named change has recorded ask and landed timestamps and a computed elapsed duration.

State on 2026-10-30: in the 24 h before this split the timer reported no stalls, but it printed `stall error` for smashcraft on all 286 of its runs, so it could not have seen a real one. Cause: listing one day of smashcraft Autoland successes at `--limit 1000` took 34 s, past the flow host's 20 s command limit. The fix (median from the newest 100 successes per day, one page each) landed with north#245; the day for the first box counts from the laptop running a north that has it. The unit also used 4 to 6 CPU-minutes per 5-minute run (13 min wall on one run), so check its cost on the same day.

## Moved from #266 In-flight safe-push runs on gex45 are cancelled together by an unidentified signal mid land check

- [ ] Done when: the signal's sender is named from evidence, such as `auditctl -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S kill -S tgkill` or an equivalent trace, and three consecutive North landings on gex45 complete without `safe-push: cancelled`.

## North first-commit-to-main under 10 minutes (2026-10-28)

- [ ] (observed) North's 24 h median author-to-origin/main time from first commit to on main is at or under 10 min (Regenerate reports excluded), with the stage split posted here; the land check falls from ~7 min toward 2 min by running only the tests whose inputs the change touches and reusing a passed check by input hash across unrelated rebases, from 32 min (p75 154) on 2026-10-28; Smashcraft was 13/34 the same day. The biggest stage of today's tail (queue push, tests, hand-backs, the Reviewed-trailer review-gate amend cycle, gex45 land checks), profiled with docs/rationale/landing-latency.md's method, is fixed at its cause. Owner: harness-planner.

The stage profile and the slices already landed (code-health before land checks 999fad79, parallel cargo test binaries dae08cbd) are in the comments of north#245.



## Landing-path follow-ups (added 2026-11-04)

- [x] safe-push retries a `land-check/<sha>` ref push once on a transient remote rejection (`remote: fatal error in commit_refs`, or an HTTP 5xx) and names it infrastructure, not a check failure (a landing failed this way on 2026-11-04). Done when: `bash bin/safe-push.test.sh` passes a case where a fake remote rejects the first land-check ref push with `fatal error in commit_refs` and accepts the second, so the landing proceeds and the log says `infrastructure`, and a case where both pushes are rejected refuses with `infrastructure` in the message. (done f2563f43d and 3ff7dd8cc: `land_actions.rs` retries a `fatal error in commit_refs` or HTTP 5xx ref push once and names a second rejection infrastructure; the Rust tests `recorded_commit_refs_rejection_is_retried_once_and_lands` and `a_second_transient_rejection_is_named_infrastructure` replace the bash-test cases)
- [x] The main-red sheriff (`harness/scripts/main-red.ts`) re-reads main's head and the failing run's commit before reverting, and reverts nothing when a newer main commit carries a fix-forward whose run passed or is pending. On 2026-11-04 it reverted 3a200b133 on a run that predated its fix-forward 6b0baa426, and the revert itself broke main. Done when: the main-red tests replay that sequence (culprit, fix-forward, stale failing run) and end with no revert, and the existing confirmed-culprit case still reverts.
- [x] One capacity lease around the whole local land-check loop: a landing queues for cores once, not once per local check (follows a717bf640). Done when: a safe-push test with two local checks records one lease acquire and one release, and an Actions-only landing still takes none.
- [x] Shard the cargo-tests Actions job. Done when: `.github/workflows/land-check.yml` runs the cargo test binaries across at least 2 jobs that together cover every binary (a listing step proves the union equals the `cargo test --no-run` list), a planted failing test in each shard fails the run, and the median cargo-tests wall over 5 landings before and after is recorded here. (done 61a02e5fa: the land-first change 2b5675065 moved cargo tests from land-check.yml to cargo.yml on main, so cargo.yml is the job sharded. - [ ] Run the shared sccache server as its own systemd user unit, so that no build auto-starts it inside a fleet session or lease scope that can be frozen or stopped. The fix belongs in nixos-config `modules/sccache`: a user service that runs `sccache` with SCCACHE_START_SERVER=1, SCCACHE_NO_DAEMON=1, SCCACHE_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0 and the module's environment. title: Fleet session hosts on gex45 end when the ssh link to gex45 stalls for two minutes
body:
On 2026-10-31 between 8:06 and 8:22 PM (+07), 13 fleet session hosts on whiterabbit placed on gex45 ended mid-task, across five runtimes (sc-700-w, wisp-shadow-quality, sc-fl-surf, sc-aq-classic, sc-raze-vfx, sc-864-w, sc-788-w, wisp-112-w8, sc-876-w, sc-lich-nair3, sc-fl-balance, sc-illidan-runA, sc-fl-spawn). Each host's own `g1/stderr.log` carries `Timeout, server (gex45's wg-direct address) not responding.`: the host's `ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=4 tom@gex45` missed four keepalives and exited, and `north session-host` ends when its child exits (`crates/north-core/src/fleet/session_host.rs`, `wait`). On the remote side the pipe closes, so the wrapper stops the claude unit too. No local host died in that window, including hosts on runtimes pruned days earlier.

At 8:30 PM the WireGuard link (`wg-direct`) measured 16 to 66% packet loss at about 350 ms RTT while the laptop's uplink to 1.1.1.1 was clean (0% loss, 15 ms), and `ssh tom@gex45` timed out. Each host also logs `mux_client_request_session: session request failed: Session open refused by peer` and a stale ControlSocket at start.

Found while working north#420, whose prune guard landed separately; the prune was not what ended these hosts.

Done when:
- [x] (observed) The cause of the wg-direct loss on 2026-10-31 is named (gex45 load, the tunnel, or the path), with the measurement.
- [x] (rust test) A gex45-placed session host survives a transport stall longer than the keepalive window: the in-flight turn and its background waits are not lost, or the host resumes the same conversation without a manual revive.

Owner: proxy.


Ticked 2026-10-31 by the proxy. Cause: one lossy UDP flow on the ISP-to-Hetzner path for the tunnel port; moving the laptop port took loss from 24% to 0 of 160 (north-421-stall comment). Survival: 4e4ee660a (fix 8c46dd2fc), test fleet::link::tests::a_held_session_survives_its_transport_dying_mid_wait; live on gex45, a 75 s background wait survived a killed ssh.
